## 2. The time kernel

The crate is `duet-time`.

### 2.1 The two units

Musical time is an integer tick count at B40 ticks per quarter note. A triplet eighth is 640 ticks.
A quintuplet sixteenth is 384 ticks. Both are exact (Ardour 1, adopt item 4).

Audio time is a superclock count, not a sample count, at B41 ticks per second. That rate divides
exactly by 44100, 48000, 88200, 96000, 176400, and 192000, so a change of sample rate does not move
existing material (Ardour 1, critic 1.2). A sample count appears only at the device edge.

```rust
/// A magnitude in the beat domain.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Ticks(i64);

/// A magnitude in the audio domain.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SuperClock(i64);

/// A device sample rate. The type makes a zero divisor impossible.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SampleRate(NonZeroU32);

/// A sample counter at the device edge, in frames since the stream opened.
///
/// It is the one sample-domain value, and `convert` is the one place it
/// meets a superclock count. The MIDI ring orders by it, so it carries the
/// comparison traits of VR1 row 3.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SampleClock(i64);

/// A count of audio frames.
///
/// It derives `Default`, because zero frames is a count and not an absence.
/// `GateState::hold_frames` needs it (section 15.2, critic S1).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FrameCount(u32);

/// A count of bars, which the count-in uses.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BarCount(u16);

/// A channel index inside one stream.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChannelIndex(u16);

/// A count of channels that cannot be zero.
///
/// **It exists so that `chunks_exact_mut` cannot panic** (section 5.11,
/// critic C19-8). `chunks_exact_mut` panics on a chunk size of zero, and
/// `panic = "abort"` makes that panic a lost take, so the audio path takes
/// the count from a type that has no zero rather than from a `u16` that a
/// refusal is supposed to have screened. `new` is the only way in, and it
/// answers `None` on a zero, so every caller decides once and off the audio
/// thread.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChannelCount(NonZeroU16);

impl ChannelCount {
    /// One count, or `None` when `value` is zero.
    pub const fn new(value: u16) -> Option<Self>;

    /// The count as a non-zero number. A chunk size is a `usize`, so a caller
    /// writes `usize::from(count.get().get())`, which is total and never
    /// zero (section 5.11, critic C20-W2).
    pub const fn get(self) -> NonZeroU16;
}

/// Seconds since the Unix epoch. A calibration records when it was measured.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct UnixSeconds(i64);

/// A document schema number.
///
/// It derives `Ord`, because property 1 of section 3.6 migrates an older
/// document and property 4 refuses a newer one, and neither decision can be
/// written without an order (critic Q8).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SchemaVersion(u32);

impl SchemaVersion {
    /// Build a version at compile time, for the constants of section 1.6.
    pub const fn new(value: u32) -> Self;
}
```

**`SchemaVersion` sits in `duet-time` because PL2 puts it there.** `duet-score`, `duet-session`,
and `duet-command` each own a versioned document, and `duet-time` is the one crate all three reach.
It carries no time semantics: it is a plain ordered newtype, and the invariant of section 1.2 is
about a time **value**, which a schema number is not.

**Every one of the counts above is declared, because no template exists.** Section 15 declares
every name section 1.5 places, PG4b proves the two sets are identical, and PG10b fails on a `Copy`
derive over a field this document does not decide. `Calibration`, `TransportSnapshot`,
`TransportCommand`, and `MidiRecord` each hold one of these five (critic Q1, Q2, R1).

**A kernel value type derives what its own use needs.** `Ticks` is a sort key in the canonical
writer, and `Position` is a cache key, so both derive `Eq` and `Hash`. VR1 removes `Eq` and `Hash`
from the vocabulary above them, so no payload ever forces a trait upward. That is the direction that
made the revision-4 vocabulary fail to compile.

### 2.2 Arithmetic is checked or saturating, never bare

`[profile.release]` sets `panic = "abort"` and `overflow-checks = true`. One overflow in the audio
path would end the process and lose a take (critic 5.5). The answer makes the fault impossible.

| Operation | Form | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Add or subtract two magnitudes | `Ticks::saturating_add`, `SuperClock::saturating_sub` | Saturates at the `i64` bound |
| Parse or import a value | `Ticks::checked_from_i64` | Returns `Result<_, TimeError>` |
| Divide | `div_euclid`, `div_ceil`, `checked_div` | Never the `/` operator |
| Scale by a ratio | `convert::muldiv` | 128-bit intermediate, then `i64::try_from` |

`Ticks` and `SuperClock` implement no `Add` and no `Sub` trait, so a bare `+` does not compile.
`clippy::integer_division` denies the `/` operator (critic 10.2). Every divisor in `duet-time` and
on the audio path is a `NonZero` type or a `checked_div` call.

### 2.3 The one conversion module

`duet-time::convert` is the only module in the workspace that holds an
`#[expect(clippy::as_conversions, ...)]`. Every other crate calls it (critic 10.1).

Two rules keep each suppression verifiable at its own site.

1. **A function whose correctness depends on the caller takes a checked newtype**, not a raw float.
2. **A function whose input range is unbounded returns `Result`**, and it checks the range before
   the cast. A reader therefore checks the invariant in the function body.

```rust
/// A sample value in the closed range -1.0 to 1.0.
///
/// Only `new` and `clamped` build one, so every consumer knows the range.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
pub struct Unit(f32);

impl Unit {
    /// Clamp a float into the unit range. A non-finite value becomes zero.
    pub fn clamped(value: f32) -> Self;

    /// The inner value, always in the closed range -1.0 to 1.0.
    pub fn get(self) -> f32;
}

/// How an integer conversion resolves a remainder.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Rounding { Down, Nearest, Up }

/// Multiply and then divide with a 128-bit intermediate.
///
/// # Errors
/// Returns `TimeError::Overflow` when the result leaves the `i64` range.
pub fn muldiv(value: i64, numerator: i64, denominator: NonZeroI64, rounding: Rounding)
    -> Result<i64, TimeError>;

/// A 16-bit sample as a float. Lossless; uses `f32::from`, no suppression.
pub fn i16_to_f32(sample: i16) -> Unit;

/// A 24-bit sample as a float. Lossless; 24 bits fit the f32 mantissa and
/// the divisor is 2^23.
pub fn i24_to_f32(sample: I24) -> Unit;

/// A 32-bit sample as a float. Exact below a magnitude of 2^24, and lossy
/// above it, because the f32 mantissa holds 24 bits. The divisor is 2^31.
pub fn i32_to_f32(sample: i32) -> Unit;

/// A unit sample as a 24-bit integer. The type carries the range, the scale
/// factor is 2^23, and `I24::new` clamps the one product above `I24::MAX`.
pub fn unit_to_i24(value: Unit) -> I24;

/// A unit sample as a 32-bit integer. The type carries the range, the scale
/// factor is 2^31, and `i32::try_from` clamps the one product above
/// `i32::MAX`.
pub fn unit_to_i32(value: Unit) -> i32;

/// A double as a single.
///
/// # Errors
/// Returns `TimeError::NotRepresentable` when the value is not finite, or
/// when its magnitude leaves the `f32` range. The check runs before the cast.
pub fn f64_to_f32(value: f64) -> Result<f32, TimeError>;

/// A tick count as a double.
///
/// # Errors
/// Returns `TimeError::NotRepresentable` at or above the magnitude B44,
/// where an `f64` stops holding every integer.
pub fn ticks_to_f64(ticks: Ticks) -> Result<f64, TimeError>;

/// A superclock count as a sample count at a rate.
///
/// # Errors
/// Returns `TimeError::Overflow` when the result leaves the `i64` range.
pub fn superclock_to_samples(clock: SuperClock, rate: SampleRate, rounding: Rounding)
    -> Result<i64, TimeError>;

/// A sample count at a rate as a superclock count.
///
/// # Errors
/// Returns `TimeError::Overflow` when the result leaves the `i64` range.
pub fn samples_to_superclock(samples: i64, rate: SampleRate) -> Result<SuperClock, TimeError>;

/// A finite double as a single, with no error path.
///
/// **It returns no `Result`, and that is the whole reason it exists.** A
/// caller that paints a length has no error surface to return one on. Every
/// constructor of `Finite` refuses a NaN and an infinity, so the input is
/// finite and the narrowing carries two losses and no third: it drops
/// mantissa bits, and it saturates to an `f32` infinity above the `f32`
/// range. Both are documented behaviour rather than silent behaviour.
/// `f64_to_f32` stays the fallible form for every caller that can report
/// (section 10.2, critic C16-14, C17-2, Appendix B.1 item 3).
#[must_use]
pub fn finite_to_f32_saturating(value: Finite) -> f32;
```

**`finite_to_f32_saturating` names no window bound, and that is the repair of Appendix B.1 item 3.**
Revision 23 wrote that `LogicalPx` is bounded by B102 and B104, so the saturating case is
unreachable. Both budget rows are true of a window, and neither is true of this function: it takes
every `Finite` from every crate, and `LogicalPx` is a `duet-command` type that `duet-time` cannot
name without an inversion of the section 1.3 graph. B102 and B104 bound the window and they bind
`duet-command`, which is where section 10.2 states them; they bind nothing in this module.

Seven functions carry a suppression: `i24_to_f32`, `i32_to_f32`, `unit_to_i24`, `unit_to_i32`,
`f64_to_f32`, `ticks_to_f64`, and `finite_to_f32_saturating`. **PG33 holds this list and the
Appendix B.1 suppression-reason table to ONE SET in both directions**, so a row with no declaration
and a declaration with no row are each a red run. Revision 16 carried a B.1 row for a function no
section declared, through seventeen revisions, because no rule read that table (critic C17-2,
N17-9). Appendix B.1 gives the reason text for each. `i16_to_f32` uses
`f32::from`. A length converts through `u32::try_from` and then `f64::from`, so `len_to_f64` does
not exist.

**Duet is a lossless editing system, so every sample round trip this module offers is exact where
the two types can carry it, and it states an exact bound where they cannot.** Every scale factor
above is a power of two, so a scaling adds no rounding of its own and the only loss any pair can
carry is the mantissa of the float. Three statements follow, and each one is a measurement.

| Round trip | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `i24_to_f32` then `unit_to_i24` | **Exact for all 16,777,216 values** | A 24-bit integer fits the f32 mantissa exactly, and both scale factors are 2^23 |
| `i32_to_f32` then `unit_to_i32` | **Exact at a magnitude of 2^24 or below; bounded by 64 above it** | The f32 mantissa holds 24 bits, so a larger sample rounds by at most one half of a unit in the last place. The paragraph below derives the 64 |
| `unit_to_i24` then `i24_to_f32`, and the 32-bit pair | **Quantized, and exact for every unit value the encode produces** | An encode maps a continuous range onto 2^24 or 2^32 integers, so the loss is the quantization the sample format states and nothing more. The one unit value that does not return itself is exactly +1.0, which clamps to `I24::MAX` or to `i32::MAX` |

**The clamp is at exactly +1.0 and nowhere else.** A scale factor of 2^23 sends +1.0 to 8_388_608.0,
which is one above `I24::MAX`, and `I24::new` answers `None` there. The `None => I24::MAX` arm the
body already carries is the clamp, so the repair of item 1 of Appendix B.1 changes one constant and
no control flow. The 32-bit form takes the same shape with `i32::try_from` (Appendix B.1 item 2).
**The negative arm of each match is UNREACHABLE at these scale factors and it stays for totality.**
A scale factor of 2^23 sends -1.0 to exactly -8_388_608.0, which `I24::new` accepts, and 2^31 sends
-1.0 to exactly -2_147_483_648.0, which `i32::try_from` accepts. Section 1.6 states the same
property for the `None` arm of `non_zero`, and each site names its binding accordingly.

**The 64 is one half of the f32 spacing at the top of the 32-bit range, and this is its derivation.**
An `f32` carries a 24-bit significand, so inside one binade every representable value sits one unit
in the last place from the next. The widest binade an `i32` magnitude reaches is 2^30 up to 2^31,
where that unit is 2^(30 - 23), which is 2^7, or 128. Round to nearest moves a value by at most one
half of that unit, which is 64. Both scale factors are 2^31, a power of two, so neither scaling adds
a term: a division and a multiplication by a power of two move the exponent alone. The rounding back
to an integer adds none either, because the product of an exact `f32` and 2^31 is an integer here.
**The bound is 64 and no sample exceeds it**, which an exhaustive scan of all 4,294,967,296 values
confirms.

**No sample is THE worst case, and this document names one only as AN example.** Many samples attain
the bound, and three independent models each named a different one: 1_195_673_408, 1_073_741_888 and
1_946_040_768 all drift by exactly 64. The first the ascending scan finds is
**-2_147_483_584**, which is `i32::MIN` plus 64. Revision 24 wrote one of them as "the worst case",
which is a singular claim the measurement does not support. `i32::MIN` and `i32::MAX` each round
trip EXACTLY: `i32::MIN` is -2^31, which an `f32` holds, and `i32::MAX` clamps back to itself
through the match.

Required tests in `duet-time`:

1. A round trip for each sample conversion, over every `I24` value a proptest draws. The 24-bit
   assert is equality over the whole range, and the 32-bit assert is the stated bound of 64.
2. A round trip for the clock at every supported rate.
3. A proptest that `muldiv` matches an `i128` reference and never overflows.
4. A proptest that `f64_to_f32` and `ticks_to_f64` return an error for every out-of-range input.

#### The conversion guard

The guard is a subcommand of `tools/xtask`, not a test.

```
cargo xtask check-conversions
```

Its contract has twelve rules, and DR5 gives each one exactly one probe (section 1.9). The prototype
is `roadmap/duet-v1/tools/conversion_check.py`, and chunk M0 ports it to
`tools/xtask/src/check_conversions.rs`.

**What the guard adds over clippy, stated first.** The root `Cargo.toml` sets
`as_conversions = "deny"`, and `scripts/dod.sh` runs
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, so clippy already refuses every
cast. **Clippy is the backstop and this guard is the earlier, cheaper signal**: it runs without a
build, and CG6 is the rule clippy cannot carry, because a `#[expect]` silences clippy and does not
silence a text scan (critic Q3).

**Two shapes escape CG1, and the site states them** (concern N15-8). A `#[path = "../outside.rs"]`
module above the crate root is not scanned, because the walk starts at the member root. A member
whose one target sits outside `src/` leaves the whole of `src/` outside the walk. **CG1b answers the
second by a DERIVED file set**; the first is a review item, and `cargo machete` and the compiler both
see the module.

#### CG1b is a derived coverage rule and it holds no constant

**Decision: the expected member set and the expected file set are derived from the tree, and any
difference fails by name.** Revision 16 used a count floor of three members and six files, plus two
environment variables that removed the floor at the production entry point. The Critic reproduced
the vacuous green the floor existed to stop: a workspace of five crates under `crates/`, one
`exclude` line, and a real cast in the excluded crate exited 0 at the production defaults (critic
C16-2). **A count floor bounds the scan by a number that does not track the thing it measures.**
Section 13 creates fifteen more crates, so from the first new crate onward one `exclude` line
removes any member and the remaining count still clears the floor, and nothing in section 13 raises
the floor.

The rule now has three parts and no constant. Chunk M0 ports all three to
`tools/xtask/src/check_conversions.rs`.

1. **The zero test.** Zero members or zero files is exit 2. It is the fail-closed-on-zero rule PG12
   already states for a denominator, and it needs no number.
2. **The derived member set, from the root manifest's own `members` globs.** Each entry of that
   array contributes its own match AND a sibling pattern at EVERY level of its own path, so
   `crates/*`, `crates/duet-a`, and `tools/nested/one` each reach every sibling of every segment
   they name (critic C18-W8). Revision 18 expanded one level alone, so a member listed by full path
   left its own siblings outside the rule while the sentence claimed the opposite.
   **A directory whose name opens with a dot is a member like any other** (critic C18-4). Cargo has
   no hidden-file rule, and Python's `glob` does, so the expansion walks each pattern with
   `os.scandir` and `fnmatch`, which match a segment exactly as Cargo does. A member at
   `crates/.fixture` is therefore inside the scan, and revision 17 let one carry a real cast past
   the guard. The
   derived set is compared with the member set `cargo metadata` reports, and **a member the scan
   does not cover is exit 2 WITH ITS PATH**. **`exclude` is deliberately not read**: an excluded
   member is exactly what this rule exists to see.
   **Revision 17 read two literals, `crates` and `tools`, at any depth**, and both halves were
   wrong (critic C17-W6, C17-W7). One line added to the root manifest took a whole third tree
   outside the rule. The any-depth walk also fired on every nested fixture crate, a `trybuild` case
   among them, which no rule forbids; the globs reach the levels their own path names and the
   sentence claimed they reach
   any depth.
3. **The derived file set.** Every `.rs` file under each covered member's own `src/` directory is a
   file the scan must hold, and one it does not hold is exit 2 with its path.

**The build-directory prune is ANCHORED, and this sentence is the contract chunk M0 ports** (critic
C17-6). Both derivations compare canonical paths against the workspace root plus `target` and
against each member root plus `target`, and against nothing else. Revision 17 pruned any directory
NAMED `target` at any depth, so a member at `crates/target/` never entered the expected set and one
`exclude` line gave a clean run over a crate that held a cast. CG1's own `build_directories` had
been anchored for that exact reason since revision 11 (critic WR-8), and the new rule was written
with the filter its own sibling had already condemned.

**No environment variable changes any part of it**, and a conversion probe needs none: a throwaway
workspace that keeps its members outside `crates/` and `tools/` derives an empty expected set and
meets the zero test alone. Revision 16's two variables are deleted (concern N16-2).

**The rule's own limits, stated here.** It decides COVERAGE and never a verdict about a file it does
scan. **It derives the expected member set from the `members` globs of the manifest under test, so a
crate no glob reaches is outside it** (critic N21-4). The twenty-first Critic deleted the `crates/*`
glob with no `exclude`, planted a real cast in `crates/alpha`, and the run was green at
`EXPECTED MEMBERS: 1`. **The miss has no run-time cost**: a crate no glob reaches and no path
dependency names is built by nothing, so neither the cast nor the crate reaches a binary, and CG1's
own backstop covers every crate cargo does build. A manifest that deletes a glob and keeps the crate
reachable by a path dependency is back inside the rule, which probe `CP1b-nested` records.

**The backstop covers a member and never an EXCLUDED member** (critic C17-W6). `cargo clippy
--workspace` operates on workspace members, and an `exclude`d package is not one, so clippy never
lints it. For every member the workspace excludes, there is no backstop at all, and that is
precisely the class CG1b exists for. Revision 17's limit paragraph named clippy as the safety net
for the one class that has none. For a member the workspace does NOT exclude, clippy is a real
backstop and shares the same denominator (critic K-10).

**A symbolic link to a directory is outside both halves** (concern N17-8). `os.walk` does not follow
one, in `source_files` and in the two derivations alike, so a `pub mod linked;` whose directory is a
link outside the member is compiled by rustc and scanned by neither. The member is not excluded in
that shape, so `cargo clippy` is the backstop that sees it. The limit sits here beside the
`#[path = "../outside.rs"]` limit CG1 already names, because both are the same class: a module the
walk cannot reach from the member root.

**No conversion-guard rule reads a block of this document.** The whole input of this guard is
`cargo metadata --no-deps` and the bytes of the files it names, so the DR7 block register of section
1.9 carries no `CG` row and PG27 holds no rule of this guard. A `CG` rule that ever reads a block
enters that register in the same changeset.

**CG1. It takes its file set from the `cargo metadata --no-deps` targets, and it accepts no path.**
The prototype takes no argument either, so no caller can narrow the scope to a sub-workspace; a
probe changes directory into its own throwaway workspace instead, and no probe reads this repository
(critic C3, critic 18). The file set is every target's `src_path` plus every `.rs` file beside it
that belongs to the same member, matched without case sensitivity, so `Other.RS` is scanned
(critic 19). That covers `src/`, `tests/`, `benches/`, `examples/`, and a `build.rs`. Revision 5
walked `src/` alone while CG3 said "anywhere", and the two disagreed for every non-library target.
`clippy --all-targets` denies the cast in those targets too, so the guard and the lint cover the
same set.

**The rule states a second limit, and `clippy` is the backstop for it.** A module reached by a
`#[path = "..."]` attribute that points outside the target's own directory is outside the walked
set, because the walk starts at each target's `src_path` and grows to the `.rs` files beside it. A
cast in such a module exits 0 here. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` in `scripts/dod.sh`
compiles that module and denies the cast, so the defect cannot reach `main`; the guard is the
earlier and cheaper signal and never the only one (critic concern 8).

**The build directory is the one exclusion, and it is anchored.** The guard compares a canonical
path against the workspace root plus `target` and each member root plus `target`. Revision 11
tested any path component named `target` at any depth, so every file under a source module named
`target` left the scanned set in silence and the run reported success over the files it did see
(critic WR-8).

**CG2. One lexer pass classifies every byte before any rule reads the text.** The pass runs left to
right over five states: code, line comment, block comment, string, and character literal. It
decides what a token means from the state it is already in, and it blanks every byte outside code
while it keeps every newline, so a reported line number is the file's own. A block comment nests, as
Rust's does. **The pass reads a string prefix, and the prefix set is `b`, `c`, `r`, `br`, `cr`, and
`rb`.** A prefix that carries an `r` opens a raw literal, which processes no escape and ends at the
quotation mark that carries its own opening hash count, so `r##"say "as" here"##` and
`br#"a " b"#` are each one literal and not two. A hash run needs an `r`, because `b#"` and `c#"` are
not Rust. Revision 10 read a bare `r` only, so `br#"a " b"#` opened an ordinary string at the first
quotation mark, the raw text closed it early, and every later cast fell inside a false string and
vanished; that was a vacuous green, and CG3b states the guard prefers a false red to a miss (critic
W-3). A `'` opens a character literal only when a literal matches at that point, so `'static` stays
code. Revision 7 ended a raw string at the first quotation mark and reported a false cast (critic
Q16). **The rule does not classify a macro body that is not valid Rust token soup**; clippy is the
backstop.

**CG2b. A comment token inside a literal opens no comment, and a quotation mark inside a comment
opens no string.** This is the half CG2 states and a three-pass scrub cannot hold. Revision 9
removed block comments, then line comments, then strings, each with its own regular expression, so
`let s = "/*"; let n = x as u32; let t = "*/";` hid a real cast and `let s = "// not a comment";`
hid every cast on its line (critic W10). The one pass removes the class by construction, and CP2b
plants both shapes and the three prefixed raw strings.

**CG3. It fails on any whole-word `as` token outside the one conversion file.** The cast itself,
not only its suppression, is the thing the rule forbids.

**CG5's left side may be generic, and the guard reds it.** `<ArrayVec<SlotSpec, MAX_SLOTS> as
Default>::default()` beside a real cast on one line reports two findings, one of them false. That is
inside the CG3b preference and it is stated here so no reader takes it for a defect (critic K-8).

**CG3b. An exclusion never hides a cast, and it prefers a false red to a miss.** CG4 and CG5 remove
a span before CG3 reads the text, and a removal that swallows a real cast turns the guard's own
subject into a blind spot. **A `<... as ...>` span is exempt only when both sides of the `as` parse
as one type path with no expression token**: no bracket, no call, no field access, no operator, no
literal, and no space between two identifiers. `a<b && c as u32 > d` fails the left-side test,
because `a<b && c` is not a type path, so the cast reaches CG3. Revision 8 kept only the last
whitespace token on the left and the whole remainder on the right, so the two sides were not
symmetric and CP3b passed only because its span held a parenthesis (critic R3).

**The false-red classes are named here.** Two shapes produce a finding that is not a cast. A
comparison pair whose two sides both read as a type path is one. A **raw identifier** is the other:
`let r#as = 1u32;` reports two findings on one line, because the scan reads a whole-word `as` and
the `r#` prefix does not change the word. Each one is a red an author removes by rewriting the line,
never a cast the guard misses, which is the trade this rule states (critic concern 9).

**When the rule is unsure it reports.** A qualified path this test rejects gives a false cast
finding, which an author answers by moving the expression out of the span. A missed cast gives
silence, and clippy is the only thing left. The guard takes the loud answer.

**CG4. A `use` item is an excluded form, and the guard excludes the whole item.** A `use` item
stands in statement position: the text before it on its line is empty, is `pub`, or ends with `;`,
`{`, or `}`. A `use` token anywhere else, such as one inside a `macro_rules!` pattern, is not an
item and blanks nothing. The guard joins the text from the `use` keyword to its terminating `;`,
**across lines**, and removes that span before CG3 runs. `crates/duet/src/main.rs` opens `use gpui_kit::{` on one line and carries `AppContext as _` on
the next. A line-oriented reading would therefore fail on the tree that chunk M0 leaves (critic
S10).

**CG5. Qualified path syntax is the second excluded form.** The guard removes the span from a `<` to
its matching `>` whenever that span carries a whole-word `as` token at its own nesting depth, and it
removes every such span before CG3 runs. `<i64 as TryFrom<i128>>::try_from` and
`<Self as Default>::default` are ordinary Rust, they are not casts, and a trait method that two
traits share can be written no other way. The guard is not a lint, so `#[expect]` does not reach it,
and `scripts/dod.sh` is the only gate surface: without this rule the first crate that needs the form
is blocked with no documented answer (critic N7).

**CG4b. A `use` item with no terminating `;` is a failure, exit 2.** The guard names the file and
the line and stops. Revision 8 blanked from that token to the last character of the file, so one
half-edited file, or one `use` a macro pattern held, disabled CG3 for every cast in it and the run
reported success it did not earn (critic R4). It is **fail-closed**, in the shape CG8 already had.

**CG5 in full.** The guard tracks bracket depth from the opening `<`, stops at the matching `>`,
and removes the span only when the `as` sits at depth one and a type-shaped token sits on each side
of it. `<i64 as TryFrom<i128>>::try_from` and `<Self as Default>::default` are ordinary forms, they
are not casts, and a trait method that two traits share can be written no other way. The guard is
not a lint, so `#[expect]` does not reach it, and `scripts/dod.sh` is the only gate surface: without
this rule the first crate that needs the form is blocked with no documented answer (critic N7).

**CG6. It fails on an `#[expect(clippy::as_conversions` or `#![expect(clippy::as_conversions`
attribute outside the one conversion file.** Both the outer and the inner form are matched. This is
the rule clippy cannot carry.

**CG7. The one exempt file is matched by canonical path.** The guard resolves every symbolic link in
the workspace root and in each candidate path before it compares, so a workspace reached through a
symbolic link still exempts `crates/duet-time/src/convert.rs`. Revision 7 compared a relative path
against a literal, and `cargo metadata` returns a resolved path, so a macOS temporary directory
reported the sanctioned cast and the sanctioned suppression as failures (critic Q17).

**CG8 also covers every read failure of a member file.** A byte pair that is not UTF-8 and a file
the process cannot open each make the read fail, and the guard prints one named line and exits 2.
Revision 10 let the decode error escape and the interpreter exited 1, and it reported an open
failure as a finding whose own text said "fail-closed" while its status said otherwise; either way a
caller that reads only the exit status could not tell a fail-closed run from a findings run (critic
K-9). **The three exit codes stay distinct: 0 is clean, 1 is findings, and 2 is fail-closed.**

**CG8. A workspace that `cargo metadata` refuses is a failure, not a pass.** The guard prints one
line that names the command and the exit status, and it exits 2. It is **fail-closed**, exactly as
PG2 makes the placement guard. Revision 7 raised an uncaught exception, which was fail-closed by
accident and stated by no rule (critic Q17).

**CG9. The Appendix B.1 reason cell and the `reason =` string of the code WILL be one text, and
chunk M90 adds the rule** (critic C1-4). Today no guard compares them. `check_placement::run` takes
the document alone and never reads a crate source, so its `B.1 SITES: 7     2.3 LISTED: 7` counter
compares two lists inside one document. `check-conversions` scans member files for a cast token and
never reads `architecture.md`. **That gap is the mechanism that let the T1-1 defect live through a
whole revision**: the appendix stated one scale factor, the code carried another, and every gate was
green. Revision 24 repaired the value and left the mechanism, so this rule repairs the mechanism.

The rule joins `check-conversions`, because that guard already resolves the workspace through
`cargo metadata` and already owns `crates/duet-time/src/convert.rs` as its one exempt file. It has
SIX parts.

1. **It reads the document the `--appendix <path>` argument names**, and it reads no document when
   the caller passes no such argument. A document the argument names and the guard cannot open is
   **exit 2** with one named line, exactly as CG8 answers a workspace that does not read.
2. **It takes the site set from the `b1-convert` guard block**: cell one of each row is the function
   name and cell three is the reason text, between its outer quotation marks.
3. **It takes the code set from the one exempt file.** For each `fn` item of that file it reads the
   attribute run above the item and, when that run holds an `#[expect(...)]` with a `reason =`
   string, it records the function name and the string.
4. **The two sets are ONE set in both directions.** A `b1-convert` row whose site the file does not
   declare, a site the file declares with a `reason =` string that no `b1-convert` row names, and a
   reason text that differs from its cell are each a **finding at exit 1**, with one indented line
   per failure under the tag ``  REASON TEXT: ``. The guard prints
   `REASON TEXTS:    <n>     REASON TEXT BAD: <n>`, so the denominator is readable.
5. **The compare is exact, character for character.** Appendix B.1 opens with the rule that a reason
   names an invariant a reader CHECKS in the body, and a paraphrase is not that reason. **The
   compare reads the DECODED value of the string literal and not its raw source token**, so a
   backslash continuation, two adjacent literals, and a `\"` escape each answer the text a reader
   sees. A cell that must hold a vertical bar writes it as `\|`, which is the escape the markdown
   table already needs, and the guard reads the cell after it removes that escape. No cell needs
   either convention today.
6. **CG9 is PATH CONDITIONAL, and the caller turns it on** (critic C2-1). `scripts/dod.sh` passes
   `--appendix roadmap/duet-v1/architecture.md` only when the change under test names a path that
   opens `roadmap/` OR names `crates/duet-time/src/convert.rs`. It passes no argument otherwise, and
   the guard then prints `REASON TEXTS:    skipped (no --appendix)` while CG1 to CG8 run unchanged.
   A skip PRINTS; it is never silent. The `plan-lint` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes the
   argument always.

**Why part 6 exists, and it is not an exception.** `scripts/dod.sh` runs `cargo xtask
check-conversions` on EVERY commit with no path condition. An unconditional CG9 would therefore make
every commit in this repository depend on one roadmap markdown file, which is the exact coupling
section 14 refuses two paragraphs before it states the path-conditional plan step. Two named failures
follow from that coupling. A document that moves or is archived turns every commit in the workspace
red for a reason unrelated to the commit. An Architect edit to one B.1 reason cell turns every commit
red until a repair chunk lands the matching code, and no engineer may clear it: SM9 part 1 makes
`architecture.md` the Architect's, and the `reason =` strings need a chunk that holds `convert.rs` in
its write scope. This act already met that deadlock once and answered it by the M91-before-M90 order
of section 13.3; the next occurrence may have no such order available.

**The denominator of part 6 is the SAME three-clause union `scripts/dod.sh` computes for the plan
step**, and the script computes it once and reads it twice. Section 14 rung one states the three
clauses, the no-upstream fallback, and the rule that the step RUNS when neither ref resolves. **Both
halves of the binding are in the condition, and one half alone would be wrong**: a `roadmap/`-only
condition would skip CG9 on a commit that edits `convert.rs`, and that commit is exactly a commit
that can break the binding.

**What part 6 covers and what it does not.** It covers every commit and every push that carries a
change to either half, on the machine that makes it. It does NOT cover the two residual limits that
clause 3 carries, which section 14 states: a force update that moves the remote ref backward, and a
long-lived branch that already pushed the change. It also does not cover a pull request that touches
`crates/duet-time/src/convert.rs` and no `roadmap/` or `tools/xtask/` path, because the `plan-lint`
job filter names neither path and the roster compile in that job costs 4.0 GB and several minutes,
which section 14 states as the reason the job is narrow. **The local step is the cover for that
case**, and its two residual limits are the whole gap.

**Who clears a red CG9.** The red is local and path conditional, so it blocks the author who created
the divergence and nobody else. The Architect owns `architecture.md` under SM9 part 1, and only a
chunk that holds `crates/duet-time/src/convert.rs` in its write scope may change the code. **The
Orchestrator adjudicates** and takes one of two paths under SM9: it dispatches a repair chunk that
lands the code half, or it reverts the appendix edit until such a chunk exists. **No engineer may
clear a red CG9 by editing the appendix**, and no party may clear it by removing the row: the marker
`<!-- GUARD BLOCK id=b1-convert rows>=7 -->` asserts the denominator, and PG27 refuses a block cut
below its stated minimum while PG27b refuses a floor below the block's own row count.

**The rule's own limit, stated here.** It binds the appendix to `duet-time::convert` alone, which is
the one file CG7 exempts and the one file whose reasons Appendix B.1 mandates character for
character. The complexity, copy and variant blocks of that appendix name sites in other crates, and
no rule binds those; PG24 and PG33 hold what they hold. **Cell two, the lint list, is UNBOUND**
(critic C2-5): each `b1-convert` row names its lints, CG9 reads cell one and cell three, and a
function may therefore carry `#[expect(clippy::some_other_lint, reason = "<the exact cell three
text>")]` while CG9 stays green. `clippy::unfulfilled_lint_expectation` is the PARTIAL enforcer: it
fires on a named lint that does not fire, so it catches a lint the site does not need, and it catches
neither a superset nor a different lint that does fire. Review holds the rest. Chunk M90 lands CG9,
its probe CP9, the `b1-convert` half of the contract, and nothing wider.

**There is no denominator floor.** A floor stopped chunk M0 from passing its own Completion command.
It also protected nothing that CG1 and CG8 do not already protect. A file set drawn from
`cargo metadata` is empty only when the workspace is empty, and CG8 fails first.

**Twelve tests in `tools/xtask` cover it, one per rule (DR5), and chunk M90 makes them thirteen.** Revision 16 said eleven against a twelve-rule contract, and the rule most likely to be dropped in the port was CG1b, which is the rule the last two revisions added (critic C16-W14, C17-W1). Section 1.9 names the probe of each
rule and records the result. Each test builds a throwaway cargo workspace with one member in a
temporary directory; no conversion test reads this repository and none reads any file under
`roadmap/`.

Chunk M0 writes `tools/xtask/src/check_conversions.rs`, adds the `mod` line and the subcommand arm
to `tools/xtask/src/main.rs`, and adds the line to `scripts/dod.sh`.

### 2.4 The tuplet rounding rule

B40 equals 2^7 times 3 times 5. A division into 7, 11, or 13 parts is not exact (critic 1.3).

**Rule.** A tuplet of `n` parts over a span of `s` ticks gives each of the first `n - 1` parts
`s.div_euclid(n)` ticks. The last part takes `s - (n - 1) * s.div_euclid(n)`. The parts sum to `s`
exactly.

```rust
/// A tuplet: `count` notes written in the time of `over` of the same value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Tuplet { count: NonZeroU8, over: NonZeroU8 }

/// Split a span into `parts` tick counts that sum to the span exactly.
///
/// The last part absorbs the remainder.
pub fn split_tuplet(span: Ticks, parts: NonZeroU8) -> SmallVec<[Ticks; 13]>;
// The inline capacity is B113, which is B43's divisor maximum.
```

A test asserts the sum over the whole range B43.

### 2.5 The position type

```rust
/// Which unit a value counts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TimeDomain { Beats, Audio }

/// A point on the timeline, measured from timeline zero.
///
/// Equality is structural: the same domain and the same value. Two positions
/// in different domains are never equal, which is the correct answer for a
/// cache key and for a dirty check.
///
/// This type implements no `PartialOrd` and no `Ord`. Order is a tempo-map
/// query, because two positions in different domains relate only through the
/// map.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Position {
    Beats(Ticks),
    Audio(SuperClock),
}

/// A signed magnitude in one domain. Equality is structural, as above.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Delta {
    Beats(Ticks),
    Audio(SuperClock),
}
```

The split between the derives is the design.

- **`PartialEq`, `Eq`, and `Hash` are structural and safe.** Two values are equal when the domain
  and the value match. That answer is correct for a map key and for a dirty check. It never claims a
  cross-domain relation.
- **`PartialOrd` and `Ord` are absent.** A derived order would place every beat position before
  every audio position, whatever the real time. The answer would be plausible and wrong, and no test
  finds it until two domains meet in one list (critic 1.1).

Code sorts with `slice.sort_by(|a, b| map.cmp(*a, *b))`. Nothing sorts a `Position` with `sort()`.

The tag is an enum of two newtypes, not a packed bit. A packed form needs masks and casts, which the
lint policy denies, and the extra bytes cost nothing at this call rate (critic 1.4).

### 2.6 The count type

A duration is not a scalar. "Three beats" has no length in samples until the origin is known,
because a tempo change can sit inside it (Ardour 1).

```rust
/// A distance together with the position where it starts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Span { origin: Position, delta: Delta }

impl Span {
    pub fn new(origin: Position, delta: Delta) -> Self;
    pub fn origin(self) -> Position;
    pub fn end(self, map: &TempoMap) -> Position;
    pub fn in_beats(self, map: &TempoMap) -> Ticks;
    pub fn in_audio(self, map: &TempoMap) -> SuperClock;
}
```

### 2.6a The `Finite` newtype

`duet-time` owns it, because `duet-score`, `duet-session`, `duet-command`, and `duet-dsp` all carry a
`duet-time` edge and all four hold one (PL2).

```rust
/// A finite `f64` with a canonical bit pattern.
///
/// Two invariants hold, and `new` is the only way in, on every path.
/// 1. The value is never NaN and never an infinity.
/// 2. Negative zero is canonicalized to positive zero.
///
/// `#[serde(try_from = "f64")]` routes deserialization through `TryFrom`,
/// which calls `new`. A hand-edited NaN in a canonical file is therefore
/// rejected with a serde error, and a hand-edited `-0.0` is canonicalized.
/// A derived `Deserialize` would write the inner field directly and break
/// both invariants.
///
/// **It derives `Default`, and the derived value is `ZERO`.** A derived
/// `Default` on a one-field struct writes `0.0_f64`, which is finite and
/// which is already the canonical positive zero, so the derive breaks
/// neither invariant and needs no constructor. Ten `duet-dsp` state types
/// derive `Default` over a `Finite` field, and revision 9 stated that the
/// derive chain stopped here (critic S1).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(try_from = "f64")]
pub struct Finite(f64);

impl Finite {
    /// Build a finite value, or `None` for a NaN or an infinity.
    /// A negative zero becomes a positive zero.
    pub fn new(value: f64) -> Option<Self> {
        value.is_finite().then_some(Self(value + 0.0))
    }

    /// Build a finite value at compile time, for the constants of section 1.6.
    ///
    /// `Finite::new` returns an `Option` and `expect` is denied, so a `const`
    /// cannot go through it. **This `const fn` asserts instead**, which is
    /// house form 5 of section 12.3. In a `const` item the assertion is
    /// evaluated at compile time, so a constant that is not finite fails the
    /// build rather than the run. `clippy::missing_assert_message` is denied,
    /// so the assertion carries its message. Adding a positive zero
    /// canonicalizes a negative zero and changes no other finite value, which
    /// is the second invariant.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    /// It panics when `value` is a NaN or an infinity. House form 5 binds
    /// every caller to a `const` item, so the assertion runs at compile time
    /// and no binary carries the panic (critic W-9).
    pub const fn from_finite_const(value: f64) -> Self {
        assert!(value.is_finite(), "a `Finite` constant must be finite");
        Self(value + 0.0)
    }

    /// The inner value. It is finite, and it is never a negative zero.
    pub const fn get(self) -> f64 { self.0 }

    /// Zero, which every default uses.
    pub const ZERO: Self = Self(0.0);
}

impl TryFrom<f64> for Finite {
    type Error = TimeError;
    fn try_from(value: f64) -> Result<Self, TimeError> {
        Self::new(value).ok_or(TimeError::NotFinite)
    }
}

impl PartialEq for Finite {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool { self.0.to_bits() == other.0.to_bits() }
}
impl Eq for Finite {}
impl Hash for Finite {
    fn hash<H: Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) { self.0.to_bits().hash(state); }
}
impl Ord for Finite {
    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering { self.0.total_cmp(&other.0) }
}
impl PartialOrd for Finite {
    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> { Some(self.cmp(other)) }
}
```

**The order is `f64::total_cmp`, not the bit order.** A bit order is wrong for a negative value. The
sign bit puts every negative value above every positive one, and it reverses the order among
negatives. A gain curve is routinely negative, so the wrong order would reach the file on disk. `total_cmp` is total, it agrees with `<` for every non-NaN pair, and
it needs no panic primitive.

The five impls are hand written. A derive of any one of them over an `f64` field does not compile.
`PartialOrd` returns `Some(self.cmp(other))`, which is what
`clippy::non_canonical_partial_ord_impl` requires, and no impl calls `unwrap` (critic P9, P10).
**A hand impl supplies a trait and demands nothing of a field**, which is why PG19 reads a derive
and never an impl.

`f64::is_finite` is a `const fn` on the pinned toolchain, so `from_finite_const` needs no feature
and no second constructor. Revision 9 declared it as a `const fn` whose body matched on
`Finite::new`, which is not a `const fn` and cannot become one while it stays the one guarded
run-time constructor (critic W3).

`LogicalPx` wraps a `Finite`, so its derived `Deserialize` reaches `Finite::try_from` and inherits
both invariants. `Unit` carries no serde derive, so no file can build one.

**The required test.** A proptest draws an arbitrary `f64`. It asserts five properties.

1. `Finite::new` returns `None` for every NaN and for both infinities.
2. `Finite::new(-0.0)` and `Finite::new(0.0)` produce equal values with equal hashes.
3. For two finite inputs, equality holds exactly when the bits match after the negative-zero rule.
4. For two finite inputs `a` and `b`, `Finite::new(a)` and `Finite::new(b)` are both `Some`, and
   `x.cmp(&y)` equals `a.total_cmp(&b)`. Revision 4 compared two `Option` values here, which proved
   nothing about the order (critic R14).
5. A JSON round trip through `serde_json` returns an equal value, and a hand-written `NaN` token,
   a `null`, and a `-0.0` each give a rejection or the canonical value.

### 2.7 The position API

`Position` implements no `Add` and no `Sub`. Six named methods replace them, and each takes the map.

```rust
impl Position {
    pub fn domain(self) -> TimeDomain;
    pub fn in_beats(self, map: &TempoMap) -> Ticks;
    pub fn in_audio(self, map: &TempoMap) -> SuperClock;
    pub fn distance(self, other: Self, map: &TempoMap) -> Span;
    pub fn earlier(self, span: Span, map: &TempoMap) -> Self;
    pub fn later(self, span: Span, map: &TempoMap) -> Self;
}

impl TempoMap {
    /// Order two positions, across domains when they differ.
    pub fn cmp(&self, left: Position, right: Position) -> core::cmp::Ordering;

    /// Test two positions for equality, across domains when they differ.
    pub fn same_instant(&self, left: Position, right: Position) -> bool;
}
```

**The method is named `same_instant` and not `eq`, and the lint policy is the reason.**
`TempoMap` derives `PartialEq`, so a second method named `eq` trips
`clippy::same_name_method`, which `[workspace.lints]` denies. That lint reads the NAME alone,
where the neighbouring `clippy::should_implement_trait` reads the arity and stays silent. Revision
23 declared `eq` and no rule read the pair, so chunk T1 met a declared shape that the declared
policy refuses. The rename removes the clash with no suppression, which is what the Appendix B.1
preamble asks of an implementer. It also serves ADR-0001: structural equality and timeline
equality are two different questions, and two methods named `eq` hide the difference that the ADR
says the two names must keep visible. `cmp` needs no rename, because `TempoMap` derives no `Ord`
(chunk T1, 2026-09-22).

### 2.8 Bars, beats, and ticks

```rust
/// A bar, beat, and tick address. Bars and beats are one-based.
///
/// It derives no `Ord`, because a bar marker can reset the address. `Ticks`
/// is the monotonic value and the only sort key on the timeline.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Bbt { bar: NonZeroU32, beat: NonZeroU16, tick: u16 }
```

### 2.9 The tempo map

```rust
/// An exact ratio. The tempo holds one so that no float enters the kernel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Ratio { numerator: i64, denominator: NonZeroI64 }

/// A written note value.
///
/// It derives `Ord` so that `DurationSelector::pending` can take the
/// shortest held letter (section 10.6).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum NoteValue { Whole, Half, Quarter, Eighth, Sixteenth, ThirtySecond }

/// A tempo, held as an exact ratio so that no float enters the kernel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Tempo { beats_per_minute: Ratio, beat_unit: NoteValue, ramped: bool }

/// A time signature.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Meter { beats_per_bar: NonZeroU8, beat_unit: NoteValue }

/// One tempo entry. It carries its own position in the two views the beat
/// and audio queries read, so a lookup never calls back into the map.
///
/// It derives serde, because `score/meta.json` holds the tempo map
/// (section 3.6). It carries no `extra` bag: `duet-time` has no `serde_json`
/// edge, and an unknown field on a tempo entry would be a tempo this build
/// cannot honour, so the reader refuses it (critic W8).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TempoPoint { ticks: Ticks, clock: SuperClock, tempo: Tempo }

/// One meter entry, with the two views the bar queries read and the same
/// serde rule.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MeterPoint { ticks: Ticks, bbt: Bbt, meter: Meter }

/// A sorted tempo and meter map.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TempoMap { tempos: Vec<TempoPoint>, meters: Vec<MeterPoint> }

impl TempoMap {
    pub fn superclock_at(&self, ticks: Ticks) -> SuperClock;
    pub fn ticks_at(&self, clock: SuperClock) -> Ticks;
    pub fn bbt_at(&self, ticks: Ticks) -> Bbt;
    pub fn ticks_at_bbt(&self, bbt: Bbt) -> Result<Ticks, TimeError>;
    pub fn convert(&self, position: Position, target: TimeDomain) -> Position;

    /// A builder that checks the sort order and the first-point rule.
    pub fn edit(&self) -> TempoMapEdit;
}
```

Each point holds its own address in the axis its own queries read. A point never asks the map to
convert its own position. That breaks the circular dependency at the base of the design (Ardour 1).

**An entry carries TWO views and not three, and chunk T1 is the site that says why.** Revision 23
gave each entry a tick, a clock, and a bar address. A tempo entry's bar address and a meter entry's
clock are read by NO query: `superclock_at` and `ticks_at` read a tempo entry's tick and clock, and
`bbt_at` and `ticks_at_bbt` read a meter entry's tick and address. Neither of the two unread views
can be checked without the OTHER list, so the gate of section 2.9 could not hold them, and the
strict-rise rule made the TRUE tempo address ILLEGAL whenever the meter list was empty: the gate
refused the honest map and accepted the false one. The Engineering Critic proved both halves on the
chunk's own fixtures. A redundant cached value that no gate checks is a second source of truth, and
`TempoMap::tempos` and `TempoMap::meters` publish it to fifteen consumer crates that cannot repair
it, because no later chunk writes `duet-time`. The ADR-0001 decision 7 reason is untouched: each
query still reads the entry's own cached view for its own axis, so no lookup calls back into the
map. The two removed views never broke that cycle; they created a second, cross-list cycle
(chunk T1, 2026-09-22).

### 2.10 Conversion takes the map as an argument

Every method that crosses a domain takes `&TempoMap`. No function reads a thread-local map, and no
type stores a map pointer. The research file lists Ardour's `TempoMap::use()` under "concepts to
reject", because it makes a conversion depend on hidden state (Ardour, reject list).

The cost is one parameter on about forty methods. The gain is that a conversion is visible in every
signature, and a test needs no thread setup.

### 2.11 How the map reaches other threads

`duet-core` owns the tempo map on the core thread. It reaches the audio thread through
`triple_buffer`, never through `arc-swap`. Section 5.8 gives the rule and the reason, and its
carrier table names the two ends: `DuetCore.tempo` writes and `EngineProcess.tempo` reads.

**It does NOT reach the engine disk thread** (critic C22I-W13). That thread reads a
`PlaybackPlan`, whose `PlaybackSpan` carries a `SampleClock`, so the disk thread needs no beat
domain and no tempo map at all. Revision 22 named a second reader here, section 5.8 carried no row
for it, no declaration held a read end, and this sentence cited section 5.8 for a rule that
section did not hold, which DR4 forbids.

ADR: `adr/0001-time-kernel-representation.md`.

## 3. The score model

The crate is `duet-score`. It holds the aggregate, the canonical document, and the notation
invariants. It names no file format parser.

### 3.1 The aggregate boundary

`Score` is one aggregate root. No smaller consistency boundary exists. A tie crosses a measure, a
slur crosses a staff, and a lyric verse runs the length of a part. A command applies to the root.

### 3.2 Identity

Every entity carries a `u64` identifier from a counter that the score owns and persists.

```rust
/// A stable identifier for a note.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NoteId(u64);
```

The same shape gives `PartId`, `StaffId`, `VoiceId`, `MeasureId`, `SpannerId`, and `MarkId`. A
generational arena index is smaller. It is wrong here, because the identifier must survive a save, a
git commit, and a hand edit by a terminal agent.

### 3.3 Entities and value objects

Entities: `Part`, `Staff`, `Voice`, `Measure`, `Note`, `Rest`, `Spanner`, `ScoreMark`.

Value objects: `Pitch`, `Duration`, `NoteValue`, `Tuplet`, `KeySignature`, `Meter`, `Clef`,
`Dynamic`, `Articulation`, `Lyric`, `TieState`.

```rust
/// The four vocal parts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum VoiceType { Soprano, Alto, Tenor, Bass }

/// One named part. A score holds many parts of each voice type.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Part {
    id: PartId,
    voice_type: VoiceType,
    /// 1 for "Soprano 1", 2 for "Soprano 2".
    ordinal: NonZeroU16,
    name: PartName,
    staves: Vec<StaffId>,
    /// Fields from a newer schema that this build does not model.
    #[serde(flatten)]
    extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

/// One staff with a clef and a written transposition.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Staff {
    id: StaffId,
    clef: Clef,
    transpose_semitones: i8,
    voices: Vec<VoiceId>,
    /// Fields from a newer schema that this build does not model.
    #[serde(flatten)]
    extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

/// A bar on the shared timeline. Every staff shares the same measures.
///
/// It carried `Copy` until revision 10. Property 4 of section 3.6 gives every
/// `score/meta.json` record an `extra` bag, a `BTreeMap` is not `Copy`, and a
/// record that keeps an unknown field cannot also be a register value
/// (critic W8).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Measure {
    id: MeasureId,
    start: Ticks,
    meter: Meter,
    key: KeySignature,
    /// Fields from a newer schema that this build does not model.
    #[serde(flatten)]
    extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

/// A diatonic step.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Step { C, D, E, F, G, A, B }

/// How a respell chooses an accidental.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Accidental { Natural, Sharp, Flat, DoubleSharp, DoubleFlat }

/// How far an octave spanner shifts, in octaves and in direction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum OctaveShift { Up8, Down8, Up15, Down15 }

/// A key signature. `fifths` is negative for flats and positive for sharps.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct KeySignature { fifths: i8, major: bool }

/// A written pitch.
///
/// It derives `Ord` so that the canonical writer can sort `notes.jsonl`
/// (VR1). The order is octave, then step, then alter, which is sounding
/// order.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Pitch {
    octave: i8,
    step: Step,
    /// -2 is a double flat, 2 is a double sharp.
    alter: i8,
}

/// A written duration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Duration { value: NoteValue, dots: u8, tuplet: Option<Tuplet> }

impl Duration {
    /// The exact tick count of this duration.
    pub fn ticks(self) -> Ticks;
}

/// Whether a note starts or ends a tie.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TieState { starts: bool, stops: bool }

/// One note.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Note {
    id: NoteId,
    staff: StaffId,
    voice: VoiceId,
    /// The onset in ticks from score zero, not from a measure start.
    onset: Ticks,
    duration: Duration,
    pitch: Pitch,
    tie: TieState,
    articulations: SmallVec<[Articulation; 2]>,
    lyrics: SmallVec<[Lyric; 2]>,
    /// Fields from a newer schema that this build does not model.
    #[serde(flatten)]
    extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

/// A mark that spans more than one note.
///
/// **It derives no `Copy`.** `score/spanners.jsonl` is one of the three files
/// that property 4 of section 3.6 names, so every record carries the `extra`
/// bag, and a `BTreeMap` is not `Copy`. Revision 9 gave the type `Copy` at 32
/// bytes and the same property required a bag it could not hold (critic W8).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Spanner {
    id: SpannerId,
    kind: SpannerKind,
    from: NoteId,
    to: NoteId,
    /// Fields from a newer schema that this build does not model.
    #[serde(flatten)]
    extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

/// The spanner kinds that v1 draws.
///
/// It derives `Ord` so that the canonical writer can sort `spanners.jsonl`
/// (VR1).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum SpannerKind { Slur, Crescendo, Diminuendo, Octave(OctaveShift) }

/// A mark on the score that is not a note and not a spanner.
///
/// Contract 2.7 group 6 offers `System break`, `Repeat`, and `Rehearsal
/// mark` in the Insert menu.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ScoreMark {
    id: MarkId,
    at: Ticks,
    kind: MarkKind,
    /// Fields from a newer schema that this build does not model.
    #[serde(flatten)]
    extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

/// What a score mark means.
///
/// The expectation is the one `variant_size_differences` refusal in this
/// plan. `MarkKind` holds three arms: two carry nothing, `Repeat` carries one
/// byte, and `Rehearsal` carries a `Box<str>` newtype. The lint compares 16
/// against 1, so it refuses every shape that stores a pointer. **A boxed arm
/// does not satisfy it either**, because a pointer is still above three times
/// one byte; the PG25 roster compile measures both shapes and both fail
/// (Appendix B.1).
#[expect(
    variant_size_differences,
    reason = "`Repeat` carries one byte and `Rehearsal` carries one pointer, so the ratio test \
              refuses every shape that stores text, a boxed arm included"
)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum MarkKind {
    /// Force a new system at this point.
    SystemBreak,
    /// A repeat barline. `Start` and `End` pair by position order.
    Repeat(RepeatSide),
    /// A rehearsal mark with its printed text.
    Rehearsal(RehearsalText),
}
```

A note onset is absolute, in ticks from score zero. A measure is a shared entry on the timeline, not
a container. That choice makes the unified timeline direct: a note, a region, and an automation
point all answer one `Position`. It also makes an agent edit unambiguous.

A tie is a property of a note, as MusicXML models it. A slur is a spanner, because it joins two
notes that need not share a pitch.

### 3.4 Commands and events

`duet-score` declares `ScoreCommand`, `ScoreEvent`, and `Applied`. `duet-command` wraps them inside
`Verb`. Every type below derives the VR1 set.

```rust
/// What a command acts on. One selection type serves every edit verb.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Selection {
    Notes(Vec<NoteId>),
    Spanners(Vec<SpannerId>),
    Marks(Vec<MarkId>),
    /// Every element of one staff inside a tick range.
    Range { staff: StaffId, from: Ticks, to: Ticks },
}

/// One intent against the score.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ScoreCommand {
    // Structure
    AddPart { voice_type: VoiceType, name: PartName },
    RemovePart { part: PartId },
    AddStaff { part: PartId, clef: Clef },
    RemoveStaff { staff: StaffId },
    SetClef { staff: StaffId, at: Ticks, clef: Clef },
    InsertMeasures { after: MeasureId, count: NonZeroU16 },
    RemoveMeasures { from: MeasureId, count: NonZeroU16 },
    SetKeySignature { measure: MeasureId, key: KeySignature },
    SetTimeSignature { measure: MeasureId, meter: Meter },
    AddMark { at: Ticks, kind: MarkKind },
    RemoveMark { mark: MarkId },

    // Content
    InsertNote { staff: StaffId, voice: VoiceId, onset: Ticks, pitch: Pitch, duration: Duration },
    InsertRest { staff: StaffId, voice: VoiceId, onset: Ticks, duration: Duration },
    SetPitch { notes: Vec<NoteId>, pitch: PitchEdit },
    SetDuration { notes: Vec<NoteId>, duration: Duration },
    SetTie { note: NoteId, tie: TieState },
    SetArticulations { notes: Vec<NoteId>, articulations: SmallVec<[Articulation; 2]> },
    SetLyric { note: NoteId, verse: VerseNumber, text: LyricText },
    SetDynamic { staff: StaffId, onset: Ticks, dynamic: Dynamic },
    AddSpanner { kind: SpannerKind, from: NoteId, to: NoteId },
    RemoveSpanner { spanner: SpannerId },

    // Assign, which contract 2.6 block 4 needs
    SetVoice { notes: Vec<NoteId>, voice: VoiceId },
    SetPart { notes: Vec<NoteId>, part: PartId, staff: StaffId },

    // Edit, which contract 2.6 block 5 needs
    Move { selection: Selection, by: Ticks, to_staff: Option<StaffId> },
    Duplicate { selection: Selection, at: Ticks },
    Remove { selection: Selection },
    Paste { clipboard: Box<Clipboard>, at: Ticks, staff: StaffId, voice: VoiceId },
}

/// How a pitch edit is expressed. The context menu offers all four.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum PitchEdit {
    Absolute(Pitch),
    BySemitones(i8),
    ByOctaves(i8),
    Respell(Accidental),
}

/// A detached copy of a selection. `Cut` and `Copy` produce one.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Clipboard { origin: Ticks, notes: Vec<Note>, spanners: Vec<Spanner> }

/// One fact about a score change.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ScoreEvent {
    PartAdded(PartId),
    PartRemoved(PartId),
    StaffAdded(StaffId),
    StaffRemoved(StaffId),
    NoteInserted(NoteId),
    NoteChanged(NoteId),
    ElementsRemoved(Selection),
    ElementsMoved(Selection),
    SpannerAdded(SpannerId),
    SpannerRemoved(SpannerId),
    MarkAdded(MarkId),
    MarkRemoved(MarkId),
    MeasuresChanged { from: MeasureId, count: u16 },
    SignatureChanged(MeasureId),
    ClefChanged(StaffId),
}

/// What one command produced.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Applied {
    /// The facts a view needs.
    pub events: Vec<ScoreEvent>,
    /// The commands that undo this one, in application order.
    pub inverse: Vec<ScoreCommand>,
    /// How many commands and how many bytes the inverse holds. The undo
    /// stack of section 4.9 uses both to hold its memory bound.
    ///
    /// `InverseCost` is declared in this crate (section 15.3). Revision 9
    /// declared it in `duet-core`, which depends on `duet-score`, so this
    /// field was a Cargo cycle (critic S2).
    pub inverse_cost: InverseCost,
}

impl Score {
    /// Apply one command. The score is unchanged when the result is an error.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `ScoreError` when the command names a missing element or
    /// breaks a notation invariant.
    pub fn apply(&mut self, command: ScoreCommand) -> Result<Applied, ScoreError>;

    /// Copy a selection without a change. `Cut` is `copy` then `Remove`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `ScoreError::MissingElement` when the selection names one.
    pub fn copy(&self, selection: &Selection) -> Result<Clipboard, ScoreError>;

    /// The revision counter. It increases on every successful command.
    pub fn revision(&self) -> Revision;
}
```

`Move` carries a `Ticks` value, not a bare `i64`. `Ticks` is signed, so a negative shift moves a
selection earlier (critic N23).

`Cut` is not a command. It is `Score::copy` followed by `ScoreCommand::Remove`, so the clipboard is
a query result and the edit is one undo transaction.

The inverse command list replaces a memento. It is small, it serializes, and it needs no weak
pointer back to the object (Ardour 8). `apply` is transactional: it validates first and mutates
second, so a rejected command leaves no partial change.

`duet-session` declares `SessionCommand` and `SessionEvent` by the same rule.

```rust
/// One intent against the session: tracks, takes, and the mix document.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum SessionCommand {
    // Track lifecycle. PR R-02.
    TrackAdd { part: PartId, staff: StaffId, name: TrackName },
    TrackRename { track: TrackId, name: TrackName },
    TrackReorder { track: TrackId, before: Option<TrackId> },
    TrackRemove { track: TrackId },

    // Input and monitor. PR R-04.
    TrackSetInput { track: TrackId, input: InputSelection },
    TrackSetMonitor { track: TrackId, monitor: MonitorMode },
    TrackSetArmed { track: TrackId, armed: bool },

    // Take and region edits. PR R-10 and R-12.
    TakeSetMuted { take: TakeId, muted: bool },
    RegionSetStart { region: RegionId, start: Position },

    // Mute and solo. PR M-02 and M-06.
    StripSetMute { strip: StripId, mute: bool },
    StripSetSolo { strip: StripId, solo: bool },
    StripClearSolo,

    // Slots and buses. PR M-04 and M-03.
    StripInsertSlot { strip: StripId, at: SlotPosition, kind: SlotKind },
    StripRemoveSlot { strip: StripId, slot: SlotId },
    StripAddSend { from: StripId, to: StripId, tap: SendTap },
    BusAdd { name: StripName, role: BusRole },
    /// Change `Strip::name`. It is the edit path the `StripName` doc comment
    /// states and revision 21 declared nowhere (critic C21-W15).
    StripRename { strip: StripId, name: StripName },
}

/// Where a track takes its input. PR R-04.
///
/// `None` is the one encoding of "no input". `Track::input` is therefore not
/// an `Option`, and two encodings of one state cannot disagree (critic R18).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum InputSelection {
    None,
    Device { device: DeviceKey, channel: ChannelIndex },
    Pair { device: DeviceKey, left: ChannelIndex, right: ChannelIndex },
}

/// When a track passes its input to the monitor bus. PR R-04.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum MonitorMode { Off, WhenArmed, Always }

/// What a bus is for. PR M-04 makes a reverb bus and a delay bus MUST.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum BusRole { Part(PartId), Reverb, Delay, Monitor, Master }
```

**`SessionCommand` carries no view state.** Revision 4 kept a `SetViewState { mode, state }` variant
beside the paragraph that deleted it. `ViewState` and `Mode` are `duet-command` types, so the
variant would give `duet-session` an edge to `duet-command` beside the existing
`duet-command` to `duet-session` edge, which Cargo refuses. `Verb::ViewSet` and `Verb::ViewGet` are
the only paths, and `duet-project` persists `view.json` (section 10.2).

**The track-safety rule, tied to `armed`.** Two refusals protect a record pass and a take.

1. `SessionCommand::TrackRemove` returns `SessionError::TrackArmed` when `Track::armed` is true. An
   armed track may be recording, and a remove would race the disk writer.
2. `TrackRemove` returns `SessionError::TrackHasTakes { count }` when the track holds a take. The
   user interface offers "Remove and keep the audio", which is `TakeDelete` for each take and then
   `TrackRemove`, as one undo transaction. Section 4.4 keeps the audio reachable.

`TrackSetInput` returns `SessionError::TrackArmed` for the same reason. `TrackSetMonitor` and
`TrackRename` are safe while armed and do not refuse.

**Which fields reach the file.** `name`, `input`, `monitor`, `record_mode`, and `align` are persisted
in `session/session.json`. `armed` is runtime state: it is not persisted, and every track opens
disarmed, because an armed track on open would record on the first `Play`.

### 3.5 The vocabulary rules

**VR7. No declaration carries a public field, and three RESULT types are the stated exemption**
(critic N22I-9). The coding guide makes a public field a public API a later revision cannot change,
so every type of this document takes accessors instead. `Applied`, `MusicXmlImport` and `SmfImport`
each carry public fields, and each one is a value a pure function RETURNS and the caller then
destructures: the whole value moves to one consumer, it holds no invariant across its fields, and an
accessor per field would be three lines that answer a move. Revision 22 stated the rule at section
5.1 alone, where it bound one section, and three declarations elsewhere broke it with no exemption
written down. No guard reads a field's visibility, so this rule is held at review.

**VR1. A declaration derives `Eq` wherever every field supplies `Eq`. `Hash` and `Ord` appear only
where this rule names the use.** `PartialEq` and `PartialOrd` are outside the rule: a partial
comparison asks a payload for nothing that a total one does not, and `Unit` carries `PartialOrd`
over an `f32` that has no total order (critic C5).

**`Eq` is not a choice, and revision 11 is the revision that says so.** The root `Cargo.toml` sets
`clippy::nursery` to `deny` and relaxes two nursery lints, neither of which is
`clippy::derive_partial_eq_without_eq`. That lint fires on every type that derives `PartialEq`,
derives no `Eq`, and could derive `Eq`. Revisions 4 to 10 read VR1 as a licence to keep `Eq` rare,
and revision 10 removed `Eq` from six more types to satisfy PG22. **The compiler refuses that
design.** The tenth Critic review compiled four of the declared shapes on the pinned toolchain and
all four failed; the revision-11 roster compile of PG25 then found 212 declarations in the same
class, and every one of them now derives `Eq` (critic C-1). A type with an `f32` or an `f64` payload is outside the
class, because a float supplies no `Eq`. **A `serde_json::Value` payload is inside it**: the section
1.9 row states that `Value` supplies `Eq` and `Hash`, a compiler run proves it, and the eight
`score/meta.json` records derive `Eq` over a `BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>` (critic 5).

**The direction of the demand is what VR1 protects, and it still holds.** `Eq` follows the fields
and never points upward: a container derives `Eq` because every payload already has it, so no
payload is ever forced. `Hash` and `Ord` are the two traits that do point upward, because a map key
and a sort key are a use a caller chooses. Those two stay rare, and the table below names every use.

**The table names every type that derives `Hash` or `Ord`, because PG22 reads it.** Revision 9
wrote "every identifier newtype" in one cell, which named no type and let eight derives stand with
no stated use (critic W16). PG22 fails on a `Hash` or an `Ord` derive the table omits, and the rule
runs in one direction only, which PG22's own site states. **PG23 holds the other half**: it fails on
a declaration that derives `PartialEq`, derives no `Eq`, and whose every field supplies `Eq`, which
is the exact shape the nursery lint refuses. PG25 then compiles the whole roster under the real lint
table, so neither rule rests on an argument.

#### Every VR1 derive and its use

<!-- GUARD BLOCK id=vr1-table rows>=27 -->
| Types that derive it | The use |
|---|---|
| `NoteId`, `PartId`, `StaffId`, `VoiceId`, `MeasureId`, `SpannerId`, `MarkId`, `PartName`, `LyricText`, `RehearsalText` | A `BTreeMap` or `BTreeSet` key inside `Score`, and the sort keys of `notes.jsonl` and `spanners.jsonl` (section 3.6) |
| `TrackId`, `TakeId`, `RegionId`, `LocationId`, `StripId`, `SendId`, `SlotId`, `ParamId`, `SourceHash`, `TrackName`, `TakeName`, `LocationName`, `StripName` | A `BTreeMap` or `BTreeSet` key inside `Session` and `MixState`. `SourceHash` also keys `media.manifest`, `derived/peaks/`, and the path cache of section 10.5 |
| `JobId`, `BranchName`, `CommitDigest`, `HashKind`, `CommitId` | `JobRegistry` keys by `JobId`, a reference edit keys by `BranchName`, and the reachability walk of section 4.4 holds a `BTreeSet` of commits. `CommitId` wraps a `CommitDigest`, so the digest carries the same set |
| `ChannelCount` | A `BTreeMap` key in the `configure_chain` agreement table, and an `Ord` comparison against `MAX_CHANNELS` at the one place that builds one. It derives the pair because `ChannelIndex` beside it does and the two are compared in the same expression (section 5.11) |
| `PortSlot` and `MidiPortId` | The two halves of `MidiPortMap`, which looks up in both directions (section 8.1). `MidiPortInfo` derives `Eq` because a hot-plug consumer compares two of them |
| `MidiPortInfo` | The same comparison, stated for the record the event carries |
| `DeviceId` | `StreamRequest` names one, and the backend finds the open device by that name in its own enumeration (section 5.4). A string identity with no `Eq` cannot be looked up |
| `DeviceKey` | The `session/session.json` calibration map key (section 5.4) |
| `Ticks`, `SuperClock`, `SampleRate`, `Position`, `Delta`, `Span`, `Bbt`, `TimeDomain`, `Tempo`, `Meter` | A cache key and a dirty check (section 2.5) |
| `Finite` | The canonical sort order on disk (section 2.6a). The three impls are hand written, because a derive over an `f64` does not compile |
| `Pitch`, `SpannerKind` | The JSON Lines sort key (section 3.6) |
| `Mode` | The `BTreeMap<Mode, ModeView>` key inside `ViewState` |
| `SampleClock`, `FrameCount`, `BarCount`, `ChannelIndex`, `UnixSeconds`, `Generation` | A count or a clock the engine compares; `SampleClock` orders the MIDI ring and `Generation` orders a publication |
| `SchemaVersion` | The migrate-or-refuse decision of section 3.6, which needs an order |
| `Ratio`, `NoteValue`, `Step`, `OctaveShift` | A payload of `Tempo`, `Pitch`, or `SpannerKind`, which the rows above already name. The demand points down |
| `NoteValue` again, for its own use | `DurationSelector::pending` takes the shortest held letter (section 10.6) |
| `MidiNote` | The sort key of `notes.jsonl` after an import, and the ordering the engrave step reads. The sounding-note set of section 8.2 is a fixed-size bitset and asks for neither |
| `Symbol` | `FontMetrics` keys `BTreeMap<Symbol, f32>` and `BTreeMap<Symbol, (f32, f32)>` (section 15.6) |
| `SystemId` | The path-cache key of section 10.5, and the `ElementId` of one rendered system |
| `VerseNumber` | `Lyric` sorts by verse, so the engraver stacks verse one above verse two (section 10.5) |
| `Layer` | The regions of one take sort by `Layer`, which is what puts the newest region on top under `RecordMode::Layered` (section 6.2) |
| `Version` | The core compares a client's last `Version` with the current one to find a gap (section 5.8), and TH8 compares two in the `Save` re-check (section 9.6). It derives no `Hash`: nothing keys by it |
| `Revision` | The engrave task compares the revision of its own result with the current one and drops a stale one (section 10.5). It derives `Eq` alone |
| `MenuPath` | `MenuHost` holds a `BTreeMap<MenuPath, Action>` and looks one up on every dispatch (section 10.2) |
| `ZoomStep` | The Compose and Record path-cache key (section 10.5) |
| `ZoomScalar` | The Mix and Master path-cache key (section 10.5) |
| `PathKey` | `PathCache` keys a `BTreeMap` by it and holds a `VecDeque` of it for the least-recently-used order (section 10.5) |

**Revision 11 restores `Eq` on 212 declarations, and it keeps every `Hash` and `Ord` drop.**
`ElementRef`, `RepeatSide`, `NodeIndex`, `BackendName`, `TransactionName`, and `Velocity` each carry
`Eq` again, because the compiler demands it, and each one still drops `PartialOrd`, `Ord`, and
`Hash`, because the table names no use. `Revision` keeps `Eq` and drops the other three. `Version`
and `Layer` each keep their order and drop `Hash`. The rule that changed is which trait is a choice,
not which use the table records.
