3. **An external profiler run** as a documented manual step before a release.

### 5.8 Which mechanism crosses each boundary

#### Structural traffic: bounded, lossless, ordered, versioned

| From | To | Mechanism | Bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any client | Core | `async_channel::bounded::<CoreInput>` | B28; the sender suspends when full |
| Core | Any client | `async_channel::bounded::<CoreEvent>`, `try_send` | B29; on full, the core marks the client stale |
| Core | Any client | `async_channel::bounded::<Snapshot>`, one per client | B30; the snapshot never shares the event channel |
| Core | The engine handoff thread | `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel::<ConfigureCommand>`, `try_send` | B109; on full the core keeps the request in `pending_configure` and re-sends it (section 5.5) |
| The engine handoff thread and the engine disk thread | Core | `async_channel::bounded::<EngineEvent>`, `try_send` | B138; on full the sending thread keeps the event in its own `pending_event` and the engine handoff thread drains no further fault until the slot empties, so the backpressure reaches B34 |

**The configure channel is a standard-library channel and not an `async_channel`, and the receiver
decides it.** The engine handoff thread parks on a deadline of B108 so that its `basedrop` drain
runs whether or not a command arrives (TH5). `async_channel` offers no timed blocking receive, and
`std::sync::mpsc::Receiver::recv_timeout` is exactly the shape B.5 already names for B18, B19, and
B22. The sender side is `try_send`, which is what the "keep it in `pending_configure`" rule needs.
No other structural row changes: the three channels above are read by an executor and stay
executor-agnostic.

Every core document carries a `Version(u64)`. A `CoreEvent` carries the version it produced. A client
that sees a gap, or that the core marked stale, sends `CoreInput::Resynchronize`.

**The resynchronize path has its own channel and its own hysteresis.**

1. A snapshot travels its own channel at B30, one per client. A snapshot in flight blocks
   nothing, and B101 gives its size at B1. It carries the score, the session, the mix, the view
   state, and the engine state, each document in the byte form `BundleDocument::to_bytes`
   produces, so a client that dropped events recovers its tracks and its strips as well as its
   score (section 15.5, critic W15).
2. The core stops every event to a stale client until the snapshot is taken, so the client drains one
   value and not a backlog.
3. A client may resynchronize at the rate B39. A second request inside the window is answered with
   the same snapshot.
4. Past B39 the core declares the client unable to keep up. It emits `CoreEvent::ClientDegraded`, the
   user interface shows a persistent bar, and an agent client receives the same fact as a Model
   Context Protocol error.

#### High-rate traffic: latest value, lock free, no event

<!-- GUARD BLOCK id=snapshot-table rows>=7 -->
| From | To | Mechanism | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audio | `duet-core` | `triple_buffer::Output<TransportSnapshot>`, read by the one `TransportReader` | Once per frame |
| Audio | `duet-core` | `triple_buffer::Output<MeterSnapshot>`, read by the one `MeterReader` | Once per frame |
| Audio | `duet-core` | `triple_buffer::Output<SlotMeterSnapshot>`, read by the same `MeterReader` | Once per frame |
| Core | Audio | `triple_buffer::Input<TempoMap>` | On a tempo edit |
| Engine handoff | Audio | `triple_buffer::Input<GraphChain>` | On a topology change |
| Core | Audio | `triple_buffer::Input<ParamSnapshot>` | On a parameter change |
| Core | Engine disk | `triple_buffer::Input<PlaybackPlan>` | On a session edit that changes what any track plays |

`triple_buffer` replaces `arc-swap` on every path the audio thread reads. With `arc-swap` the audio
thread can hold the last reference to a retired value and run its destructor inside the callback
(critic 5.1). A `triple_buffer` reader borrows and never owns, so the writer thread drops every
retired value. The licence is MPL-2.0, which the operator accepts. `arc-swap` is not a dependency of
any Duet crate.

**The same mechanism reverses on the first two rows, and TH9 is the answer.** There the audio thread
is the writer, so it is the dropper. `TransportSnapshot` and `MeterSnapshot` are therefore `Copy`
plain data with fixed-size fields and no heap field, which section 5.9 declares and PG13 checks.

**Each publication has exactly one read end, and `duet-core` owns it** (critic CR-11).
`triple_buffer::triple_buffer()` returns one `Input` and one `Output`, and the section 1.9 external
table records that an `Output` is neither `Clone` nor `Copy`, so one value exists and one owner
holds it. Revision 12 gave a `MeterReader` to `MeterLayer` and to `MasterMeterLayer`, and a
`TransportReader` to the `PlayheadLayer` of Compose and of Record, which needs four values where two
exist. Section 10.2 states the frame order that replaces it: `CoreHost` holds the one `MeterReader`
and the one `TransportReader`, it polls both once per frame before any child view renders, and every
view reads the `Copy` result through `MeterReader::latest` and `TransportReader::latest`. No view
holds an `Output`.

#### Sample traffic and owned handoffs

**One primitive per boundary, and the declaration agrees with the row** (critic WR-11). Revision 12
declared three of these ends as an `rtrb::Producer` in section 15 and as a
`crossbeam::queue::ArrayQueue` here, and neither stated overflow rule was reachable from the
declared type. **This table is the one place the primitive is decided**, and every other site
follows it; revision 20 declared the fault queue here in one primitive and in section 12.4 in
another, and the second named a crate `duet-engine` did not depend on (critic C20-5).

**Two questions decide the primitive, and the producer count is asked first.**

1. **How many producers does the boundary have?** An `rtrb::Producer` is one value and it is not
   `Sync`, so a second producer cannot exist and a boundary with two producers cannot be an `rtrb`
   ring at all. `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue` is the multi-producer primitive of this design, and it
   is the answer whatever the overflow action is. The fault queue is the one boundary in that class:
   the audio callback and the cpal error callback both push (TH11).
2. **What is the overflow action?** For a single-producer boundary, **`rtrb` carries every boundary
   whose producer only pushes**: `Producer::push` returns the value on a full ring and evicts
   nothing, so the loss is the newest value. **`ArrayQueue` carries every boundary that must
   evict**: `force_push` drops the oldest element, which is what "drop the oldest" and "keep the
   newest" both need. An `ArrayQueue` can also refuse the newest, with `push`, and the fault queue
   is the one row that takes that arm.

`triple_buffer` carries every latest-value publication. **No boundary names two primitives, and no
row names two consumers.**

**Every `rtrb` ring is single producer and single consumer, and every consumer gets its own ring.**

| From | To | Mechanism | Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disk | Audio | `rtrb` ring of `f32` | One per playback channel |
| Audio | Disk | `rtrb` ring of `f32` | One per capture channel |
| cpal input callback | cpal output callback | `rtrb` ring of `f32` | One per input channel |
| MIDI thread | Audio thread | `rtrb` ring of `MidiRecord`, B32. A full ring drops the newest record and increments the shared drop counter that section 8.3 names | One, for the monitor voice and for a MIDI take |
| Audio | Disk | `rtrb` ring of `RefillRequest`, B33. A full ring means the disk thread is behind; the request is dropped and the starved ring reports itself as `CycleOutcome::PlaybackStarved` | One |
| The audio callback and the cpal error callback | The engine handoff thread | `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue<EngineFault>` at B34, inside the one `FaultQueue` that also holds the `AtomicU32` drop counter. **Two producers, so the primitive is not `rtrb`** (TH11). `ArrayQueue::push` refuses the NEWEST fault on a full queue and increments the counter, because the first fault of a burst names the cause and the later ones repeat it; the consumer reads the counter and mints `EngineFault::FaultsDropped { count }` (section 12.4) | One |
| Engine handoff | Audio | `rtrb` ring of `GraphHandoff` at B105, which carries the new chain-state array and its own generation. B105 is 1, so a second configuration cannot be in flight while the first waits; a full ring keeps the configuration in `handoff_retry` and the generation does not move (section 5.5, critic CR-20) | One |
| MIDI thread | `duet-core`, for note entry | `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue<NoteEntry>`, B31; `force_push` drops the oldest record and increments the shared drop counter | One |
| MIDI presence listener | MIDI thread | `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue<PlatformPort>`, B87; `force_push` keeps the newest and the listener sets the resync flag | One |
| MIDI thread | Core | `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue<HotplugEvent>`, B100, with the same `force_push` rule. The MIDI thread mints the `MidiPortInfo` the event carries, because it is the one owner of `MidiPortMap` (TH10) | One |
| Core | Audio | `Arc<ResetGenerations>`, which holds `[AtomicU32; MAX_STRIPS]`, one meter-reset generation per strip, read once per cycle with a relaxed load | One array at B86 |
| Core or the engine handoff thread | Audio | `basedrop::Shared<T>` for any other owned value the audio thread must release. The builder needs a clone of the one `basedrop::Handle` that `GraphConfigurator` mints (section 5.5) | Per value |

The MIDI thread writes each note twice: once into the audio ring and once into the note-entry queue.
A duplicated fixed-size `Copy` record is cheaper than a second thread, and the two consumers then
have independent backpressure. Section 8.3 gives the record its size and states what a full
note-entry queue does. **Neither record owns a heap allocation**, so the ring allocates on no note
and frees on no note, which is what TH1 needs on the B9 path (critic N1).

`rtrb` is the one ring buffer crate. Its small surface is a small review surface. `ringbuf` is not a
dependency (critic 5.6). **The queue crate is `crossbeam-queue` and not the `crossbeam` umbrella**,
for the same reason: only `ArrayQueue` is used, and the narrower pin is the smaller review surface
and the smaller dependency tree. `duet-midi`, `duet-core`, and `duet-engine` are the three crates
that name it, and the section 1.2 row of each one carries the edge. **Revision 20 removed the
`duet-engine` edge and kept an `ArrayQueue` declaration at section 12.4**, so the one path every
engine fault takes to the user named a type the crate could not spell (critic C20-5).

`basedrop`'s collector runs on the engine handoff thread and drains once per B108 (TH5). **No
deferred verb runs on that thread**, so an export render cannot delay a drain. The audio thread
never calls `free`.

#### Every cross-thread carrier, and the two ends it needs

**PG41 reads this block, and TH13 is the rule it runs** (critic C22I-1, C22I-2, C22I-3, C22I-7,
C22I-8). Every earlier revision answered a review at one level and left the level below it open.
Revision 21 found closure rows that named a FIELD no declaration held. Revision 22 declared every
one of those fields and left the CHANNEL, the SENDER and the RECEIVER between two threads
undeclared, so eight Criticals were one class: a stated duty whose carrier no declaration holds.
This plan already refuses a type with no place, a place with no type, a derive with no use, a
citation with no site and a chunk with no crate. This block is the missing one: a message with no
channel.

Each row names one message, the declared field that holds the write end, the carrier and its bound,
the declared field that holds the read end, the thread of each end, and what a full carrier or an
elapsed bound does. **A sender and a receiver may be ONE field** when the carrier is a
`crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue` behind an `Arc`, because one value carries both ends and the external
verdict for `ArrayQueue` already states that.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CoreInput` | `CoreLink.inputs` | `async_channel` at B28 | `DuetCore.inputs` | GPUI foreground and Job threads (B37) and File watch and `duet-quit-save` -> Core | The sender suspends when full |
| `CoreEvent` | `ClientLink.events` | `async_channel` at B29 | `CoreClient.events` | Core -> GPUI foreground | On full the core marks the client stale and stops every event to it until the snapshot is taken |
| `Snapshot` | `ClientLink.snapshots` | `async_channel` at B30 | `CoreClient.snapshots` | Core -> GPUI foreground | Capacity one per client; a second request inside B39 is answered with the same snapshot |
| `ConfigureCommand` | `DuetCore.configure` | `sync_channel` at B109 | `GraphConfigurator.commands` | Core -> Engine handoff | On full the core keeps the request in `pending_configure`; `EngineEvent::GraphConfigured` is the one re-send trigger |
| `EngineEvent` | `EngineLink.events` | `async_channel` at B138 | `DuetCore.engine_events` | Engine handoff and Engine disk -> Core | On full the sender keeps the event in its own `pending_event` and the engine handoff thread drains no further fault until the slot empties |
| `GatewayCall` | `AgentBridge.requests` | `async_channel` at B35 | `AgentBridge.inbox` | tokio workers (B38) -> GPUI foreground | The sender suspends when full, so a runaway agent slows down and never exhausts memory (section 9.5 rule 6) |
| `VerbOutcome` | `GatewayCall.reply` | `oneshot` at B23 | `AgentCall.reply` | GPUI foreground -> tokio workers (B38) | Capacity one and `send` consumes the end; on B23 the tokio task abandons the wait and the connection closes, which section 9.5 rule 9 states as the agent contract |
| `JobId` | `JobRunner.queue` | `async_channel` at B36 | `JobWorker.queue` | Core -> Job threads (B37) | On full `JobEnqueue` answers `GatewayError::JobQueueFull`; the reserved tail of B36 is kept for a user-started verb |
| `TempoMap` | `DuetCore.tempo` | `triple_buffer` | `EngineProcess.tempo` | Core -> Audio | Latest value wins; the writer drops the retired value, which is why this is not `arc-swap` |
| `GraphChain` | `GraphConfigurator.topology` | `triple_buffer` | `EngineProcess.topology` | Engine handoff -> Audio | Latest value wins; the publication follows the B105 handoff and never precedes it |
| `ParamSnapshot` | `DuetCore.params` | `triple_buffer` | `EngineProcess.params` | Core -> Audio | Latest value wins; the cycle reads it once and `generation` states which one |
| `PlaybackPlan` | `DuetCore.plan` | `triple_buffer` | `EngineDisk.plan` | Core -> Engine disk | Latest value wins; a job thread builds the plan inside B130 and the core performs the one write |
| `TransportSnapshot` | `EngineProcess.transport_out` | `triple_buffer` | `TransportReader.output` | Audio -> Core | Latest value wins; TH9 binds the published type, so the write copies fixed-size data and frees nothing |
| `MeterSnapshot` | `EngineProcess.meters` | `triple_buffer` | `MeterReader.output` | Audio -> Core | The same rule, at B8 per write |
| `SlotMeterSnapshot` | `EngineProcess.slot_meters` | `triple_buffer` | `MeterReader.slots` | Audio -> Core | The same rule, at B133 cells per write |
| `PlaybackSpan` samples | `EngineDisk.fills` | `rtrb` at B53 | `DiskReader.samples` | Engine disk -> Audio | A short ring makes the cycle report `CycleOutcome::PlaybackStarved`; B58 is the mark that pushes a refill |
| `Cycle` capture samples | `DiskWriter.samples` | `rtrb` at B53 | `EngineDisk.drains` | Audio -> Engine disk | A full ring refuses the push and the cycle counts the frames it could not write, which raises `EngineFault::CaptureOverflow` |
| `StreamInfo` input samples | `CpalInput.write` | `rtrb` at B53 | `CpalOutput.read` | cpal input callback -> Audio | cpal gives two callbacks and not one duplex callback, so a short ring is a shortfall and raises `EngineFault::CaptureShortfall` |
| `RefillRequest` | `EngineProcess.refills` | `rtrb` at B33 | `EngineDisk.requests` | Audio -> Engine disk | A full ring means the disk thread is behind; the request is dropped and the starved ring reports itself |
| `GraphHandoff` | `GraphConfigurator.handoffs` | `rtrb` at B105 | `HandoffReader.consumer` | Engine handoff -> Audio | Capacity one; a full ring keeps the configuration in `handoff_retry` and B95 caps the attempts |
| `MidiRecord` | `MidiSink.records` | `rtrb` at B32 | `EngineProcess.midi` | MIDI -> Audio | A full ring drops the newest record and increments the shared drop counter |
| `NoteEntry` | `MidiSink.notes` | `ArrayQueue` at B31 | `DuetCore.notes` | MIDI -> Core | `force_push` drops the oldest record and increments the shared drop counter |
| `PlatformPort` | `HotplugSink.ports` | `ArrayQueue` at B87 | `HotplugSink.ports` | Platform presence listener -> MIDI | `force_push` keeps the newest and the listener sets the resync flag. **Both threads hold a `HotplugSink`** (critic C23I-N3): the queue is one `Arc<ArrayQueue>` the two clones share, so one field declares both ends |
| `HotplugEvent` | `MidiPortMap.hotplug` | `ArrayQueue` at B100 | `DuetCore.hotplug` | MIDI -> Core | `force_push` drops the oldest event and the MIDI thread sets the resync flag |
| `EngineFault` | `FaultQueue.queue` | `ArrayQueue` at B34 | `FaultQueue.queue` | Audio and cpal error callback -> Engine handoff | `push` refuses the NEWEST fault and increments the counter, because the first fault of a burst names the cause |

**What this block does not cover, stated here.** It reads the ENDS and never the bodies: a row
proves that one field holds the write end and one field holds the read end, and no rule of this
document writes the statement that pushes a value. It also declines a handoff that is not a
channel: a `basedrop::Shared<T>` moved into a callback closure, and the `Arc<ResetGenerations>` the
audio-exempt block names, are each an owned value and not a message, so section 5.8's third table
decides them and this one does not. The run prints `CARRIERS` and `CARRIER FIELDS`, so both
denominators are readable.

### 5.9 The transport state machine

```rust
/// The transport state. Count-in and latency pre-roll are frame budgets, not
/// states, because a budget composes with every state (Ardour 4).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TransportState { Stopped, Rolling, Locating { target: SuperClock } }

/// The record arm state. Three steps, as Ardour models them.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RecordState { Disabled, Enabled, Recording }

/// The whole transport.
#[expect(
    missing_copy_implementations,
    reason = "the live transport is an identity the audio thread owns, and the type is the size \
              the PG24 table prints for `Transport`"
)]
#[derive(Debug)]
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
pub struct Transport {
    state: TransportState,
    record: RecordState,
    position: SuperClock,
    count_in_remaining: FrameCount,
    preroll_remaining: FrameCount,
    loop_range: Option<Span>,
    punch_range: Option<Span>,
}
```

`TransportCommand` is a `duet-command` type (section 15.5). `DomainEvent` carries it to every
client, and `duet-engine` depends on `duet-command`, so an intent declared here would be a Cargo
cycle (critic S2).

```rust
impl Transport {
    /// Apply one intent.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `TransportError::PunchAndLoop` when both ranges would be armed.
    pub fn apply(&mut self, command: TransportCommand) -> Result<TransportState, TransportError>;
}

/// What the audio thread publishes about the transport, once per cycle.
///
/// TH9 makes it `Copy` plain data with no heap field, because the audio
/// thread is the writer on this path and the writer runs the drop.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TransportSnapshot {
    position: SuperClock,
    state: TransportState,
    record: RecordState,
    count_in_remaining: FrameCount,
    preroll_remaining: FrameCount,
    generation: Generation,
}

impl TransportSnapshot {
    /// The transport stopped at the start, which is the value the
    /// publication carries before the first cycle writes one.
    ///
    /// `triple_buffer::triple_buffer` takes an initial value, and
    /// `SuperClock` derives no `Default`, so the type carries a named
    /// constructor exactly as `MeterView::silent` does (critic C-7).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn stopped() -> Self;
}

/// Every strip's meter values for one frame, and its held over marks.
///
/// Both arrays are fixed at B86 and `live` says how many entries the mixer
/// view reads, so the audio thread writes a fixed-size value and frees
/// nothing (TH9). One write is a memory copy of the size the PG24 table
/// prints for `MeterSnapshot`, which fits B8 with room to spare. Revision 12
/// stated that size as a literal here, the `latched` array made it stale, and
/// no guard read a doc comment (critic WR-15).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MeterSnapshot {
    readings: [MeterReading; MAX_STRIPS],
    over: [OverMark; MAX_STRIPS],
    live: u16,
    /// Per strip, the reset generation the audio thread had applied when it
    /// last latched that strip's `OverMark`. **One scalar cannot carry B86
    /// independent counters**, which is why revision 11's single field could
    /// publish no per-strip reset at all (critic CR-1). `MeterReader`
    /// compares each entry with the shared `ResetGenerations` entry and
    /// paints a mark when the latch is at or above the reset.
    latched: [Generation; MAX_STRIPS],
}
```

```rust
/// Every configured slot's live measurement for one frame.
///
/// **It is the second audio-to-core publication, and section 7.3 states why
/// one was needed** (critic C21-7). `MeterSnapshot` is per strip, contract
/// 5.2 and PR M-03 ask for a value per slot, and no boundary of section 5.8
/// carried one before revision 22.
///
/// The array is fixed at B133 and `live` says how many cells the configured
/// topology fills, so the audio thread writes a fixed-size value and frees
/// nothing (TH9). The cell index is the section 7.3 formula, which both ends
/// compute and neither stores. It derives no `Default`, because B133 is far
/// above the array length the standard library implements `Default` for.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SlotMeterSnapshot {
    measures: [SlotMeasure; MAX_SLOT_METERS],
    live: u16,
    generation: Generation,
}

impl SlotMeterSnapshot {
    /// Every cell silent, which is the value the publication carries before
    /// the first cycle writes one.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn silent() -> Self;
}
```

`MeterSnapshot` carries an array and not an `ArrayVec`, because an `ArrayVec` of a `Copy` element is
`Copy` only when the crate says so, and an array is `Copy` by the language rule. `live` gives the
mixer view the same bound an `ArrayVec` length would give it. **`SlotMeterSnapshot` takes the same
shape for the same reason.**

`ArmRecord` and `DisarmRecord` move `RecordState` only. Neither one writes `Track::armed`, which
`Verb::TrackSetArmed` alone writes (section 6.1).

Punch and loop are mutually exclusive while the transport rolls; `apply` refuses to arm both
(Ardour 4). The machine is pure and holds no buffer, so it runs under `cargo test` with no device.

### 5.10 The disk reader and the disk writer

One thread serves every track. Ardour calls it the butler (Ardour 5). Every file read and every file
write goes through `duet-media`; `duet-engine` names no audio format crate (section 1.2). **The disk
cycle period is B14**, and the two media bounds below are whole multiples of it, so a bound is a
count of cycles the thread failed to complete and never a second clock.

#### How a refill finds its source (critic C21I-1)

**A `RefillRequest` names a track and a timeline position, and the `PlaybackPlan` turns that pair
into a file and an offset.** Revision 21 declared neither half of that sentence, so the disk thread
was asked to open a file no declaration named and the take model of sections 6.1 and 6.2 had no
consumer at all.

1. **The core builds the plan, on a job thread** (TH3, section 9.6). It walks each track's active
   `Take`, applies the layer order, the `opaque` rule, and the record mode of section 6.2, and
   flattens the result into one ordered, non-overlapping `Box<[PlaybackSpan]>` per track. Flattening
   is a session computation and it touches no device, so it never runs on a real-time thread. B130
   bounds the build and `EngineFault::AllocationSlow` is not raised here, because a job thread that
   overruns delays no cycle; the core emits `CoreEvent::JobProgress` as it does for every deferred
   verb.
2. **It publishes the plan** over the one `triple_buffer::Input<PlaybackPlan>` of section 5.8. The
   core is the writer, so the core drops every retired plan and the disk thread borrows and never
   owns, which is the same rule every other publication of this design follows.
3. **The disk thread reads the plan once per B14 cycle**, before it serves any request. For each
   `RefillRequest` it finds the span that covers `from`, opens `media/<hh>/<hash>.wav` for that
   span's `source` through `duet_media::SourceReader`, seeks to `offset` plus the distance from
   `at`, reads, **applies the span `gain` and the two fades**, and pushes the frames into the ring.
   A position no span covers reads as silence, which is what a gap on the timeline is.
4. **The audio thread applies no region envelope**, which is why `SlotKind` holds no fade arm and
   why `ChainState` holds no region. The envelope is a property of the SOURCE and not of the chain,
   and the disk thread is the one thread that already touches the source.

**Refusals, both off every real-time thread.** A track whose flattened span count passes B128 is
refused with `SessionError::PlaybackTooDense { track, spans }` when the plan is built, and a plan
whose total span count passes B129 is refused the same way. The user sees one line and the last good
plan stays published, so a refused edit never silences a track.

**A locate discards every playback ring, and the AUDIO thread does the discard** (critic C21I-1).
On the first cycle in which `Transport::state` is `TransportState::Locating { target }`, the runner
drains each playback ring to empty with a `Consumer::pop` loop, which allocates nothing and frees
nothing, and pushes one `RefillRequest` whose `from` is `target`. The disk thread therefore stays
stateless per request and needs no way to tell a locate from an ordinary refill. A drain of B53
frames is bounded and it is the one cycle that pays for the locate.

- **Playback.** The disk thread fills each ring from `media/<hh>/<hash>.wav` through
  `duet_media::SourceReader`, at the source and the offset step 3 resolved. A ring below B58 pushes a
  `RefillRequest`. A starved ring outputs silence, returns `CycleOutcome::PlaybackStarved`, and adds the silent frames
  to `ChainState::starved`; the runner pushes one `EngineFault::PlaybackStarved` when that run
  closes (critic C21-1). The audio thread never blocks, never
  allocates a ring, and never frees one: `configure` allocates every ring into the `ChainState` it
  builds, and the collector releases every ring of a retired `ChainSetHandle` (section 5.5).
- **Capture.** The audio thread writes into the ring. The disk thread drains and appends through
  `duet_media::TakeWriter`, and flushes on every drain (PR 10.5). `TakeWriter` owns the RF64
  promotion rule of section 1.2.
- **A full capture ring loses the NEWEST frames, and the take records it** (critic C19-9).
  `rtrb::Producer::push` returns the value on a full ring and evicts nothing (section 5.8), so the
  audio thread cannot keep the newest sample without dropping an older one that the file already
  owes. The cycle therefore writes what the ring will take, counts the frames it could not write,
  returns `CycleOutcome::CaptureOverflow`, and adds the frames it lost to
  `ChainState::overflow`. **The push goes through the LATCH and never once per cycle** (critic
  C21-1): the runner opens the run on the first cycle the condition holds, accumulates on every
  later one, and pushes one `EngineFault::CaptureOverflow { track, frames }` when the run closes,
  with `frames` the whole run. **It never blocks, never allocates, and never retries inside the
  cycle**, which TH1 requires. The gap is a real hole in the take, so `TakeFlag::HadOverrun` marks the take and section
  6.4 states who observes it. Revision 19 declared the outcome and the fault and stated no action at
  all, so three designs were each consistent with the text: drop the newest, evict the oldest, or
  block (critic C19-9).

**Every media read and every media write is bounded, and the bound is a budget** (critic C19-10).
The disk thread is the one thread that waits on a file, and a file on a network volume or a
spinning disk can wait for a time no cycle budget covers. A read runs inside B117 and a write runs
inside B118, and each bound has a stated action.

| Media call | Bound | Action on expiry |
|---|---|---|
| `SourceReader::read_block`, per ring refill | B117 | The read is abandoned and the ring stays short. The cycle that meets the short ring returns `CycleOutcome::PlaybackStarved`, which is the path an empty ring already takes, so no new surface exists |
| `TakeWriter::append` and its flush, per drain | B118 | The pass ends, `EngineFault::CaptureStalled { track }` is raised, and the take keeps every sample already flushed. `TakeFlag::HadOverrun` marks the take, because the frames the ring then loses are the same hole |
| `PyramidBuilder` append to `derived/peaks/<uuid>.peaks` | B118 | The peak write is abandoned for the pass. **No fault is raised and the take is not marked**, because a peak file is derived data that section 4.4 rebuilds; the lane draws the range it has |

**The disk thread drains no fault queue** (critic C19-10). Revision 19 put the drain on this thread,
which means that the one path a fault takes to the user interface waited behind the one call that
can wait for seconds: a stalled write hid every fault it caused, `DeviceLost` included. The drain
moved to the engine handoff thread, which parks on a bounded receive of B108, touches no file, and
already raises two faults of its own (section 12.4).
- **Peaks during a record pass.** The disk thread builds peak bins as it writes, through
  `duet_dsp::peaks::PyramidBuilder`, and appends them to `derived/peaks/<uuid>.peaks`. The lane draws
  the new range at once (Ardour 9).

**`duet-dsp` owns the peak pyramid format.** Both `duet-engine` and `duet-analysis` build and read
the same file, so the header, the level layout, and the bin type have one definition.

```rust
/// One bin of a peak pyramid. The level layout is B68. It is six bytes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PeakBin { min: i16, max: i16, rms: u16 }

/// The on-disk header of a `.peaks` file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PyramidHeader {
    magic: [u8; 4],
    format_version: u16,
    channels: NonZeroU8,
    levels: NonZeroU8,
    frames: u64,
}

/// Build a pyramid one block at a time, during a record pass or after it.
///
/// **Nothing accumulates for the length of the take** (critic C20-W4). A
/// closed bin is written to the file and forgotten. Revision 20 held every
/// closed bin in a `Vec`, which is about 130 MB of resident memory on the
/// disk thread for one hour of stereo at 96 kHz, against a whole-engine
/// worst case of B55 at 104 MB, and no budget row named it.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct PyramidBuilder {
    header: PyramidHeader,
    /// The bin each level is filling now. B68 gives the level layout.
    open: Box<[PeakBin]>,
    /// How many frames each level's open bin has absorbed.
    filled: Box<[u32]>,
    /// The bins this append closed, and nothing older.
    ///
    /// It is FIXED at B123 bins and it is drained to the file on every
    /// `append`, so the builder's residency is B123 times the six bytes of a
    /// `PeakBin` whatever the length of the take is. A full staging buffer
    /// inside one `append` is a flush and never a growth.
    staging: ArrayVec<PeakBin, PEAK_STAGING_BINS>,
}
```

**The read path takes ONE level and never the whole file** (critic C20-W4). `Pyramid::load_level`
reads the header, seeks to the level the zoom step names, and reads the span the lane draws, so the
resident cost is B124 and not the size of the file. `LaneView` asks for the level whose bin covers
at least one device pixel, which is the level it would otherwise average by hand.

### 5.11 The house idiom for the audio path

`clippy::indexing_slicing` is denied, and `[profile.release]` sets `panic = "abort"` (section 2.2).
**A panic on the audio path is therefore a process abort and a lost take, so the idiom must be free
of every panic and not only free of every index.** Revision 19 listed five forms and three of them
could panic: `chunks_exact_mut` panics on a chunk size of zero, `split_at_mut` panics past the
length, and `copy_from_slice` panics on a length disagreement (critic C19-8). A lint-clean form is
not the same thing as a panic-free form, and the lint set proves the first and not the second.

**These six forms are lint clean AND panic free**, and each one removes a bounds check that indexing
would add (critic 10, "The honest pass").

1. A per-sample loop over two slices a TYPE has already proved equal:
   `for (dst, src) in output.iter_mut().zip(input.iter())`. **`zip` stops at the shorter side**, so
   it never panics, and it also never reports. **The form is legal only where the equality is
   already proved, and the proof is named at the call site** (critic C20-W3). One proof exists on
   this path: `Cycle::input` and `Cycle::output` each return `Option<&[f32]>` of exactly
   `cycle.frames()` frames, because the backend lends one plane per channel of one cycle
   (section 5.1). **Where no type proves it, form 4 is the answer**, and a bad length there returns
   `CycleOutcome::Faulted(FaultCode::Misconfigured)`. Revision 20 let this form answer a length
   disagreement with a silent partial write, which leaves the tail of a playback buffer holding the
   previous cycle and raises no fault; that is the defect class the capture shortfall already fixed
   (section 5.4).
2. Interleaved frames, with the widening written out:

   ```text
   let width = usize::from(channels.output().get().get());
   for frame in output.chunks_exact_mut(width) { ... }
   ```

   **The chunk size is a `usize` and the value behind it is a `NonZeroU16`**, so the one panic
   `chunks_exact_mut` carries cannot be reached. `ChannelConfig` holds a `ChannelCount` and not a
   `u16`, and `configure_chain` is the one place that builds one: it returns
   `ConfigError::ChannelMismatch` on a zero, off the audio thread and before any allocation. A
   zero-channel chain is a misconfiguration, not a runtime case. **The `u16` to `usize` step is a
   WIDENING and `usize::from` is total**, so it needs no `duet-time::convert` site: section 12.3
   form 3 binds every numeric NARROWING and this is not one. Revision 20 wrote
   `chunks_exact_mut(channels.output().get())`, which passes a `NonZeroU16` where the standard
   library takes a `usize`, so the one expression the section calls the house form did not build
   (critic C20-W2).
3. A two-span ring read: `split_at_mut_checked`, with a `let ... else` on the `None`:

   ```text
   let Some((head, tail)) = buffer.split_at_mut_checked(mid)
   else { return CycleOutcome::Faulted(FaultCode::Misconfigured); };
   ```

   `split_at_mut_checked` answers `None` past the length where `split_at_mut` panics. The refusal is
   a `CycleOutcome`, which section 12.4 already carries to the user interface, so an impossible
   split costs one silent cycle and one fault instead of the process.
4. A bounded copy, which keeps the memory copy and drops the panic:

   ```text
   let (Some(into), Some(from)) = (head.get_mut(..count), source.get(..count))
   else { return CycleOutcome::Faulted(FaultCode::Misconfigured); };
   into.copy_from_slice(from);
   ```

   Both slices are exactly `count` long after the `let ... else`, so the one panic
   `copy_from_slice` carries cannot be reached and the call is still one `memcpy`. A `zip` loop
   would also be panic free and it would give up the copy, which the B8 budget pays for.
5. A fallible single element:
   `let Some(value) = slice.get(index) else { return CycleOutcome::Faulted(code) };`.
6. A fixed window: a slice pattern, `[a, b, c, rest @ ..]`.

**Every audio module uses these forms and no other**, and no `#[expect]` is needed for indexing
anywhere. **The rule that binds them is one sentence**: on the audio path a length is either proved
by a type, as form 2 proves it, or answered by an `Option`, as forms 3, 4 and 5 answer it. A form
that panics on a bad length is not in the set, whatever the lint says about it, **and a form that
truncates a bad length in silence is not in the set either** (critic C20-W3). Form 1 is the one
form whose proof is at the call site rather than in its own expression, so the module that writes
it names the proof in a doc comment beside it, and chunk C3's verification step reads every `zip`
of the crate against that rule.

### 5.12 The latency budgets

Section 1.6 holds every number. This section names what measures each one.

- **B2, B3, and B4** are measured by a criterion bench on `duet-engrave`, summed over the visible
  systems, plus a manual profiler run.
- **B5** is measured by a test that times `DuetCore::call` on the largest project fixture. The same
  budget covers the one `Arc::make_mut` clone of section 9.6, which a criterion bench in
  `duet-core` measures on the same fixture.
- **B6** is what the gateway promises for a deferred verb: completion, or a job identifier and
  progress events. The first visible acknowledgement is inside B2.
- **B7 and B8** are measured by the soak test, which counts starved cycles.
- **B117 and B118** are measured by the soak test as well, which records the longest read and the
  longest append of the run beside the starved count. A run whose longest append passes B118 is a
  failing run, so the bound is exercised and not only declared (critic C19-10).
- **B9** is measured by a loopback test on the dummy backend with a synthetic port. It has four
  parts: B11 for the platform driver and our parse, B12 for the ring handoff, B7 for the output
  block, and B13 for the device output stage.
- **B10** is B9 plus B2, because the drain runs in `Window::on_next_frame`, before the same frame's
  render (section 8.3).

**The sound path never crosses the GPUI thread, in Compose as well as in Record.** The MIDI thread
writes the monitor record into the audio ring directly. The note-entry queue is a second, separate
path that only puts a note head on the staff (section 8.3).

#### Cross-boundary timeouts

A boundary with no timeout is an unbounded wait.

| Boundary | Timeout | Action on expiry |
|---|---|---|
| The command-line client connects to the socket | B15 | Fall back to the file path, or report `ProjectBusy` when the lock is live (section 3.8) |
| The command-line client waits for a verb reply | B16, or B17 for `ExportAudio` and `Gc` | Print `The project did not answer in <n> seconds` and exit with a failure code. `duet status` reports the verb |
| The core waits for a device to open after `ConfigureCommand::Open` | B18 | **A REPORT, not a cancel**, for the B116 reason: `AudioBackend::open` is a blocking call on the engine handoff thread and no channel receive sits on that path. **The core measures it**, and on expiry the engine moves to `EngineState::OpenTimeout { device }` and the window opens. `BackendError::OpenTimeout` stays declared, because `DummyBackend` and a future native backend each return it from `open` itself (section 5.5, critic C20-4) |
| A `History` call on a job thread | B19 | `HistoryError::Timeout`, shown on the history surface with a retry action (section 4.5) |
| The loopback calibration, whole run | B20 | `EngineFault::CalibrationTimeout`. The device keeps `CalibrationSource::Default` |
| The loopback calibration, one pass | B21 | The pass is discarded. Three discarded passes end the run with the same fault |
| `MidiStream::open_input` | B22 | `MidiError::OpenTimeout`. The port stays unbound and `MidiEvent::BindFailed { port, reason }` is raised |
| `MidiPresence::subscribe_hotplug` | B22 | The platform presence source is abandoned and `MidirPresence` takes over with its documented poll |
| Ring allocation for a playable-set change | B27 | `EngineFault::AllocationSlow`. The change still completes; the fault is evidence for a bound review |
| The engine handoff thread pushes a handoff into the B105 ring | B95 attempts, one per B108 | `ConfigError::PoolHandoffBusy`. Nothing sleeps on a thread that paints: the whole retry lives on the engine handoff thread, which paints nothing, and the pending `Configured` waits there. Nothing retries in the five stopped engine states, because no cycle drains the ring (section 5.5, critic WR-17, CR-15, CR-19) |
| An immediate verb allocates on the GPUI foreground thread | B110 | TH3 refuses the design. A value above the bound is built on the engine handoff thread or on a job thread, and the verb answers at once with the completion as an event (section 5.5, critic CR-19) |
| The core waits for `EngineEvent::StreamClosed` after `ConfigureCommand::Close` | B116 | **A REPORT, not a cancel.** `EngineFault::DeviceStalled` is raised, the engine moves to `EngineState::Faulted`, and no open is accepted until `StreamClosed` arrives. The engine handoff thread stays inside `AudioBackend::stop` and the last `GraphState` is dropped only after that call returns (section 5.5, critic C19-7, C20-4) |
| The core waits for `EngineEvent::HandoffStopped` on the quit path | B119 | **A REPORT, not a cancel.** The core stops waiting and the process exits with the thread abandoned and `Collector::try_cleanup` unrun; the operating system reclaims the B55 bytes (section 9.5 step 8, critic C20-4, C21-2) |
| The engine handoff thread parks on its bounded receive of B109 | B108 | The park ends and the loop runs its `basedrop` drain anyway, which is the whole reason the receive is timed (TH5, section 5.5, critic C20-N1) |
| The disk thread reads one block through `duet_media::SourceReader` | B117 | The read is abandoned and the ring stays short. The next cycle returns `CycleOutcome::PlaybackStarved` (section 5.10, critic C19-10) |
| The disk thread appends and flushes through `duet_media::TakeWriter` | B118 | The pass ends and `EngineFault::CaptureStalled { track }` is raised. The take keeps every flushed sample and carries `TakeFlag::HadOverrun` (section 5.10, section 6.4, critic C19-10) |
| The shutdown wait for in-flight verb replies | B23 | The reply is dropped and the connection closes (section 9.5 rule 9) |
| The quit path waits for `EngineEvent::CaptureDone` for every armed track | B131 | **A REPORT, not a cancel.** The core stops waiting, marks every unfinished take with `TakeFlag::HadOverrun`, and records `EngineFault::CaptureStalled`. The take keeps every flushed sample and the writer repairs the header on the next open (section 9.5 step 3, critic C21I-2) |
| The core waits for one `CoreInput::WorkerStopped` per B37 worker | B132 | **A REPORT, not a cancel.** The core stops waiting and the process exits with the workers abandoned. Every deferred verb writes through a `.tmp/` directory the next start empties, so no partial file survives (section 9.5 step 5, critic C21I-2, C21-2) |
| The core waits for `CoreInput::QuitSaveDone` from the `duet-quit-save` thread | B134 | **A REPORT, not a cancel**, for the B117 and B118 reason. The core stops waiting and the process exits with the save abandoned. The atomic save is the section 4.10 save: each temporary file sits beside its final name and `state/save.commit` lists the set, so the next start completes every rename the marker names (critic C22I-W15, C23I-W2) (section 9.5 step 6, critic C21-3) |
| The tokio runtime shutdown on a detached thread | B24 | The thread is abandoned and the process exits (section 9.5) |
| The writer-lock retry of a second client | B25 | `ProjectError::WriterLocked` reaches the client (section 3.8) |
| The file-watch debounce window | B26 | The batch closes and one `CoreInput::FilesChanged` is sent (section 3.9) |
| The `audio-smoke` workflow wait for the PipeWire socket | B85 | The job fails on expiry (section 11.6, section 14) |

**This table is every cross-boundary wait, and ADR 0004 clause 17a names it** (critic N16-10,
N17-2, C20-N2). Revision 20 cited "clause 24", and the ADR numbers its decision clauses 1 to 22
with lettered sub-clauses, so the one citation that carries the completeness claim resolved to
nothing.
Revision 17 left B24, B25, B26, and B85 with a mechanism row in Appendix B.5 and no row here, so the
one table the ADR cites was not the whole table. **Revision 19 left three waits with no row at
all** (critic C19-7, C19-10): the stop of a device, one media read, and one media write. The first
had no owner that could perform it, and the last two are the only waits in this design that a
network volume can stretch past a second, so their absence was the widest hole the table carried.
**Revision 20 left B108 with a B.5 row and no row here** (critic C20-N1), which is the same shape a
third time, so B108 has a row of its own now and the rule is stated: **every row of the Appendix B.5
timeout table is a row here, and the two tables are one set.** **B110 is the one row that bounds an allocation
and not a wait, and it is the ONE row of this table that Appendix B.5 does not hold** (critic
N21I-4). It sits here because TH3 refuses the design at the same boundary and for the same
reason a wait is refused: a value above the bound reaches the thread that paints. B.5 is a table of
timeout MECHANISMS, and an allocation bound has none, so the "one set" rule above carries exactly
this exception and both sites state it.

ADR: `adr/0004-backend-and-threading-contract.md`.

## 6. Record

The models are in `duet-session`. The runtime is in `duet-engine`.

### 6.1 Takes as playlists, regions over immutable sources

```rust
/// One immutable audio source. An edit never touches its bytes.
#[expect(
    missing_copy_implementations,
    reason = "a source is an identity a caller must not duplicate in silence, and the type is \
              the size the PG24 table prints for `Source`"
)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Source {
    hash: SourceHash,
    channels: NonZeroU8,
    sample_rate: SampleRate,
    frames: u64,
    /// Where the source was captured on the timeline.
    natural_position: Position,
}

/// One view of a source on the timeline.
///
/// The invariant is three numbers: POSITION is the first point on the
/// timeline, START is the first frame inside the source, LENGTH is the
/// extent. A trim and a split change only these numbers (Ardour 3).
/// **It derives `Copy` from revision 21** (critic C21I-W3). Every field is a
/// plain scalar now that a fade is a `Fade` and not a `Curve`, and PG9
/// requires the derive on an all-`Copy` type with no `Drop` impl. The PG24
/// table prints its size, which is below the VR5 bound.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Region {
    id: RegionId,
    source: SourceHash,
    position: Position,
    start: Delta,
    length: Delta,
    gain: GainDb,
    /// The two region fades.
    ///
    /// **A fade is NOT an automatable parameter** (critic C21I-W3). Revision
    /// 21 typed both as a `Curve`, and `Curve` holds a `ParamId`, which is an
    /// address into the B90 `ParamSnapshot` space; a comped take holds
    /// hundreds of regions and two fades each, so either every fade consumed
    /// a cell of the 2048 the design bounds with no refusal to catch it, or
    /// the address meant nothing. `Fade` carries a shape and a length and no
    /// address, and the disk reader applies it before the ring (section
    /// 5.10), so nothing on the audio path reads it at all.
    fade_in: Fade,
    fade_out: Fade,
    /// A transparent region sums with the layer under it.
    opaque: bool,
    layer: Layer,
}

/// One region fade: a shape and a length, and no parameter address.
///
/// `duet_media::SourceReader` applies it on the disk thread before the ring,
/// which is where `PlaybackSpan::fade_in` and `PlaybackSpan::fade_out` carry
/// it in frames (section 5.10, critic C21I-W3).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Fade { shape: Interpolation, length: Delta }

/// One take. A take is a playlist of regions on one track.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Take {
    id: TakeId,
    name: TakeName,
    regions: Vec<RegionId>,
    /// Whether this take is silent in the playable set.
    /// `SessionCommand::TakeSetMuted` is the one writer and chunk K3 draws
    /// the toggle (critic C21-W11). **It is not a `TakeFlag`**: the five
    /// flags are facts the engine OBSERVED about one pass, and a mute is an
    /// intent the user states afterwards, so one value cannot serve both. PR
    /// R-10 asks that both passes appear and each one can be muted, and
    /// revision 21 declared the command and no state for it.
    muted: bool,
    /// When the pass that produced this take started, as the wall clock read
    /// it.
    ///
    /// PR R-09 is a MUST and it asks each take row for a number, a length and
    /// a DATE, and design contract 3.4 draws `Take 3 - 14:22`. Revision 22
    /// declared no field that holds a time, on `Take` or on `Source`, so the
    /// take list could paint two of the three (critic C22I-W11). The length
    /// is derived from the regions and the number is the identifier, so this
    /// is the one fact the list cannot compute.
    recorded_at: UnixSeconds,
    /// Facts about how this take was recorded. A pass can produce more than
    /// one at once, so it is a set, not a single value.
    flags: TakeFlags,
}

/// A set of `TakeFlag` values, held as a bitset over a `u8`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TakeFlags(u8);

impl TakeFlags {
    pub fn contains(self, flag: TakeFlag) -> bool;
    pub fn with(self, flag: TakeFlag) -> Self;
    pub fn is_empty(self) -> bool;
}

/// One track. A track holds many takes and plays one.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Track {
    id: TrackId,
    part: PartId,
    /// The staff whose line the audio lane follows.
    staff: StaffId,
    /// PR R-02. The sidebar shows it and `TrackRename` writes it.
    name: TrackName,
    takes: Vec<TakeId>,
    active: TakeId,
    record_mode: RecordMode,
    align: AlignChoice,
    /// PR R-04. `InputSelection::None` means the track plays back and
    /// records nothing. The field is not an `Option`, because two encodings
    /// of one state can disagree.
    input: InputSelection,
    /// PR R-04.
    monitor: MonitorMode,
    /// PR R-05. `Verb::TrackSetArmed` is the one writer, and three surfaces
    /// read it: `TransportBar`, `Sidebar`, and the mixer strip.
    armed: bool,
}
```

A take swap is a pointer swap, so take management costs no media (Ardour 3, adopt item 7). A trim is
reversible because it changes three numbers and rewrites no audio file (PR 10.6).

### 6.2 The three record modes

```rust
/// What a new region does to the regions under it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum RecordMode {
    /// Add the new region on top and keep the old one under it.
    Layered,
    /// Partition the take so that the new region cuts a hole.
    Replace,
    /// Mark the new region transparent so that both sound together.
    SoundOnSound,
}
```

Three rules cover comping, replacement, and doubling. A vocal application needs all three (Ardour 4,
adopt item 6).

### 6.3 Punch, loop, and count-in

```rust
/// One mark on the timeline. One flagged type covers every kind.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Location { id: LocationId, name: LocationName, span: Span, kind: LocationKind }

/// What a location means.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum LocationKind { Mark, Range, Loop, Punch, SessionRange, Xrun }
```

One type, one renderer, one serializer (Ardour 3, adopt item 18).

**A record pass arms only above B126 of free space** (PR R-14, critic C19-W18, C21-W8). `duet-project`
measures the free space of the bundle volume when the user arms, and the Record top bar shows one
line below the threshold: `This volume has under <n> GB free. Free some space before you record.`
The measurement is a deferred verb, so it never runs on the thread that paints.

**A pass that captured zero frames commits NO take** (PR R-06, critic N21-17). A stop during the
count-in is the ordinary case: `count_in_remaining` is above zero, the disk writer has captured
nothing, and `CaptureInfo::frames` is zero for every armed track. The core then commits no take, no
region and no undo transaction, and it emits no `SessionEvent::TakeAdded`, so the take list is
exactly as it was before the user pressed record. PR R-06 is a MUST that asks for no take on that
path and revision 21 stated no outcome at all.

Count-in is a frame budget, not a state. The disk writer captures nothing while `count_in_remaining`
is above zero. Latency pre-roll is a second budget: the graph runs before the reported transport
moves, and the extra frames are trimmed from the front of the new region (Ardour 4).

### 6.4 Latency alignment

```rust
/// Where a new take lands on the timeline.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum AlignChoice {
    /// Put the take where the transport clock said.
    CaptureTime,
    /// Shift the take earlier so that it lines up with what the singer heard.
    ExistingMaterial,
}

/// One armed track's accumulating flag set, while a pass runs.
///
/// The CORE assembles `TakeFlags` from five observers that section 6.4 names,
/// and it must apply the result to the take that `CaptureInfo::track` names,
/// so the accumulator carries the track (critic C23I-5).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TrackFlags { track: TrackId, flags: TakeFlags }

/// A fact about how a take was recorded. It is stored with the take.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TakeFlag {
    /// The device had no measured calibration, so the offset used the default.
    Uncalibrated,
    /// The input fell behind, so part of the take is silent.
    HadShortfall,
    /// The capture ring filled, so the file is missing frames the singer
    /// sang. Section 5.10 states the action and B118 states the write bound
    /// whose expiry is the other way to reach it.
    ///
    /// **It is not `HadShortfall`** (critic C19-9). A shortfall is an INPUT
    /// that arrived late, so the take holds silence where sound never came.
    /// An overrun is an OUTPUT path that could not keep up, so the take is
    /// missing sound that did come. The singer hears the two apart and a
    /// comp decision differs on them, so one flag cannot serve both.
    HadOverrun,
    /// The backend reported clock drift during the pass.
    HadDrift,
    /// A bound MIDI input left during the pass. Section 8.2 states what the
    /// engine, the core, and the bind policy each do.
    MidiPortLost,
}
```

The default for every vocal track is `ExistingMaterial`, because the singer sings against playback.

The offset is `LatencyReport::capture` plus `LatencyReport::playback` plus the monitor chain latency.
Section 5.4 states where the first two come from.

**The monitor chain latency is DERIVED and it is not a third measurement** (critic C21-W13). It is
the sum of the look-ahead of every slot in the monitor bus chain, and exactly one `SlotKind`
carries look-ahead: `Limiter`, at B122. Every other kind is a sample-by-sample filter or a gain and
adds zero. So the term is B122 times the number of `Limiter` slots the monitor chain holds, which is
zero or one in every topology this plan builds, and a monitor chain with no limiter contributes
nothing. **No type and no budget row holds a "monitor chain latency"**, because the value is
arithmetic over B122 and the published `ChainTopology` the core already has; revision 21 named the
term in this formula alone, so an implementer would have had to invent it, and the term decides
where every take lands on the timeline for the two MUST stories PR R-07 and PR R-08. At commit the region position becomes
`capture_start.earlier(Span::audio(offset), map)`.

**The CORE assembles `TakeFlags`, and the disk thread assembles none of it** (critic C22I-4).
Revision 22 put a `flags: TakeFlags` field on `CaptureInfo` and made the disk thread the producer.
The observer table below names five observers and four of them are the backend, the audio thread
and `duet-midi`; section 5.8 gives the disk thread three boundaries, which carry `f32` samples, a
`RefillRequest` and a `PlaybackPlan`, and not one of them carries a backend observation, an
audio-thread observation or a MIDI departure. A `TakeFlags` built on that thread could therefore
hold at most the one flag that thread raises itself, and the field asked a producer for four facts
it cannot see.

The core sees all five, and it already holds each one before the pass ends: every `EngineFault` of
section 12.4 reaches it on the B138 channel, every `HotplugEvent` reaches it on the B100 queue, and
`Calibration` is project state the core owns. `DuetCore::take_flags` accumulates one `TakeFlags`
per armed track while the pass runs, and the disk thread reports one `CaptureInfo` per armed track
on the B138 channel at the end of the pass, which names the track and the frames alone (section
6.6). The core then applies `SessionCommand` for the new take, with the flags it assembled, in the
same undo transaction as the regions. The flag therefore reaches `session/takes.jsonl` through the
ordinary document path, and an undo removes it with the take.

| Flag | Who observes it | When | How the core learns it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Uncalibrated` | The backend, at arm time | `Calibration::source` is `Default`, or `split` returned `CalibrationInvalid` | The core owns `Calibration` as project state and reads `LatencyReport` from `EngineEvent::Latency` |
| `HadShortfall` | The audio thread, per cycle | The input ring held fewer frames than the cycle asked for | `EngineFault::CaptureShortfall { track, frames }`, latched per track by a `FaultRun` |
| `HadOverrun` | The audio thread, per cycle, and the disk thread, per drain | The capture ring refused a push, so the cycle counted the frames it could not write (section 5.10); or a `TakeWriter` append passed B118, so the drain ended early and the ring then refused the next push | `EngineFault::CaptureOverflow { track, frames }` from the audio thread and `EngineFault::CaptureStalled { track }` from the disk thread, both on the B138 channel |
| `HadDrift` | The backend, per B70 window | The drift magnitude passed the B70 threshold | `EngineEvent::Drift`, which carries a `DriftReport` |
| `MidiPortLost` | `duet-midi`, on a hot-plug departure | A bound input left while `RecordState::Recording` held (section 8.2) | `HotplugEvent` on the B100 queue, which the core drains in the same callback |

**When the calibration is a default or invalid, the take is flagged and the observable offset is
still applied.** A later calibration does not move an existing take, because a take is a fact about
what was recorded. B73 names the residual, which is always late.

The dummy backend reports a configurable `LatencyReport`, so the alignment test of section 5.4
proves the whole path with no device, inside B71.

### 6.5 How a take maps to a part and a staff

A `Track` names exactly one `PartId` and one `StaffId`. A part holds many tracks, because many
singers sing one part. A track holds many takes.

In Record mode the lanes for every track of a part sit under the staff that the track names. One
staff can carry two parts, for example Soprano and Alto on a treble staff. B1 bounds the view.

### 6.6 A capture pass produces regions

The disk writer produces one whole-file region that covers the new source, and then one region per
capture pass. Each pass records its start, its frame count, its loop offset, and its underrun count.
The whole batch becomes one undo transaction on the take (Ardour 3).

```rust
/// What one capture pass produced, for ONE track.
///
/// **`track` is the field that makes this message usable** (critic C21-4,
/// C23I-W3). PR R-05 is a MUST and it asks for one take per armed
/// track, so the core receives one `EngineEvent::CaptureDone` per armed
/// track and each one must say which track it ends. Revision 21 declared
/// neither field, so several armed tracks produced several values of one
/// shape and the core could map none of them to a take.
///
/// **It carries NO `TakeFlags`** (critic C22I-4). Revision 22 added that
/// field and asked the disk thread for four observations no boundary carries
/// to it. Section 6.4 now states the one party that sees all five, which is
/// the core, and `DuetCore::take_flags` is the field that holds them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CaptureInfo { track: TrackId, start: SuperClock, frames: u64, loop_offset: u64, underruns: u32 }
```

**The core keeps the SET of tracks it still owes and never a count** (critic
C21-4). The B138 channel carries one `EngineEvent::CaptureDone` per armed track, the
core removes `CaptureInfo::track` from the owed set, and the quit path of
section 9.5 step 3 waits B131 for that set to empty. On expiry the core marks
every track still IN the set, which is what B131's expiry action needs and
what a count cannot express.

## 7. Mix and Master

The mix document lives in `duet-session`. The mix runtime is a module of `duet-engine`. The export
pipeline is `duet-export`.

### 7.1 The channel strip model

```rust
/// One channel strip. A track strip, a bus, and the master share one type.
///
/// **A strip holds the ORDER of its slots and its sends, and `MixState` holds
/// the values** (critic C21-W17). Revision 21 held a whole `SlotConfig` here
/// and a second whole `SlotConfig` in `MixState::slots`, so one fact had two
/// owners, a slot edit had to write both, and `MixState::validate` checked
/// neither against the other. This document states the rule twice already:
/// two encodings of one state cannot disagree. A `SlotId` and a `SendId` are
/// a reference and not a second copy, so the list here is the order and
/// `MixState` is the one owner of each value. `MixDocument` therefore
/// serializes each value exactly once.
///
/// **Each list is bounded and the bound is refused, not truncated** (critic
/// C21-6). `pre_fader` and `post_fader` each hold at most B45 entries and
/// `sends` holds at most B46, because `ChainTopology` in `duet-engine` is an
/// `ArrayVec` of exactly those capacities and `configure` has no legal answer
/// to a ninth value: `clippy::panic` and `clippy::indexing_slicing` are both
/// denied, so silence and truncation are the only other behaviours and both
/// are wrong. `MAX_SLOTS` and `MAX_SENDS` sit in `duet-time`, which this
/// crate reaches, so the bound is readable where it is enforced.
///
/// **Each list stays a `Vec` and not an `ArrayVec`, and the trade-off is
/// stated rather than hidden** (critic N22I-2). This type is a DOCUMENT: it
/// is deserialized from `mix/strips.json`, which a user or a terminal agent
/// may have edited by hand, and a fixed capacity would make the parse of an
/// over-long list fail inside `serde` with a message that names a capacity
/// and no repair. The design wants the file to PARSE and then
/// `MixState::validate` to refuse it with `MixError::SlotBudgetExceeded`,
/// which names the strip and the bound. The cost is that the type admits an
/// illegal state between the parse and the validation, and the mitigation is
/// that `configure` reads `ChainTopology`, which is an `ArrayVec` and never
/// this type, so no over-long list reaches the audio thread.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Strip {
    id: StripId,
    kind: StripKind,
    /// The name the user reads and edits. `SessionCommand::BusAdd` collects
    /// it, `SessionCommand::StripRename` changes it, and section 7.1 states
    /// where the mixer reads it (critic C21-W15).
    name: StripName,
    trim: ParamId,
    polarity: ParamId,
    /// At most `MAX_SLOTS` entries, in signal order.
    pre_fader: Vec<SlotId>,
    fader: ParamId,
    pan: ParamId,
    /// At most `MAX_SLOTS` entries, in signal order.
    post_fader: Vec<SlotId>,
    /// At most `MAX_SENDS` entries.
    sends: Vec<SendId>,
    /// Where the strip output goes. The master strip outputs to the device.
    output: StripTarget,
    meter_tap: MeterTap,
    /// PR M-02 and M-06 make both a MUST on every strip.
    mute: bool,
    solo: bool,
}

/// What a strip carries. `Bus` carries its `BusRole`, so a reverb bus and a
/// delay bus are two values and the mixer view has something to read.
///
/// **There is no `Master` arm.** The master strip is
/// `Bus(BusRole::Master)`, and one encoding of one state cannot disagree
/// with itself (critic Q10, critic R18).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum StripKind { Track(TrackId), Bus(BusRole) }

/// One box of the master chain, in the fixed order contract 5.2 draws.
///
/// **The order is the arm order, and no position field exists** (contract
/// 5.2). A user cannot reorder the master chain, because the correct order
/// is not a preference, so an order the document could store is an order the
/// document could store WRONG. `MasterView` draws the five boxes by
/// iterating the arms, and `configure` fills the master strip's
/// `pre_fader` list in the same order.
///
/// **Each arm names where its value lives, and the three homes are not the
/// same** (critic C19-11). `Gain` is `ChainState::trim`, which every chain
/// already carries. `Equalizer`, `Compressor`, and `Limiter` are each one
/// `SlotSpec` of `SlotKind` with the same name. `Dither` is `DitherKind` on
/// the section 7.4 export spec: it narrows a render to an integer format and
/// changes no live sample, so its box shows the noise shape and its `Switch`
/// sets `DitherKind::None`. Revision 19 named "five stages" in three places
/// and typed none of them, so PR MA-02, PR M-03, and contract 5.2 each named
/// a tool no chunk could build.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum MasterStage { Gain, Equalizer, Compressor, Limiter, Dither }

impl MasterStage {
    /// The five stages in the contract 5.2 order, which is the arm order.
    pub const ORDER: [Self; 5] = [
        Self::Gain, Self::Equalizer, Self::Compressor, Self::Limiter, Self::Dither,
    ];

    /// The `SlotKind` this stage inserts, or `None` when the stage is the
    /// strip trim or the render dither.
    pub const fn slot_kind(self) -> Option<SlotKind>;
}

/// One send to a bus.
///
/// It is `AuxSend`, not `Send`. A struct named `Send` shares the type
/// namespace with the `Send` marker trait, so a module that imports it
/// cannot write a `T: Send` bound.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AuxSend { id: SendId, target: StripId, level: ParamId, tap: SendTap }

/// Where a send takes its signal.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum SendTap { PreFader, PostFader }

/// The contiguous identifier range one slot's parameters occupy. A slot
/// addresses its parameters by offset from `first`, so a parameter change
/// needs no map on the audio thread. B96 gives `count` for each `SlotKind`,
/// and the sum of every range is what B90 bounds (section 5.5).
///
/// **It is an identifier range and never a value range.** Revision 12 named
/// it `ParamRange` and then gave it to `LevelMeter::scale` and `Knob::range`,
/// where design contract 4.4 and 4.5 each need a value bound; a `ParamId`
/// pair and a count of 12 produce no decibel and no knob taper (critic
/// WR-13). `ParamRange` below is the value range, and the two names no longer
/// collide.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ParamIdRange { first: ParamId, count: u16 }

/// The value range of one automatable parameter: its bounds and the value a
/// reset returns it to.
///
/// Design contract 4.5 gives a knob drag one percent of **this** range per
/// pixel, so the element that paints a parameter needs the bounds and nothing
/// else. Every value is a `Finite`, so a NaN reaches no taper (VR4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ParamRange { min: Finite, max: Finite, default: Finite }

/// Where a strip meter reads.
///
/// It is `MeterTap`, not `MeterPoint`, because `duet-time` already declares
/// `MeterPoint` and `duet-engine` depends on both crates (PL3).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum MeterTap { Input, PreFader, PostFader, Output }
```

#### Solo and mute

PR M-06 makes both a MUST. The semantics are **solo in place**. A soloed strip keeps its own routing
and its own sends. Every strip that is neither soloed nor feeding a soloed strip is muted implicitly.

```rust
/// What the runtime computes from the mute and solo flags, once per
/// topology change, off the audio thread.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AudibleState { explicit_mute: bool, implicit_mute: bool }
```

Three rules define it.

1. When no strip is soloed, `implicit_mute` is false everywhere.
2. When one or more strips are soloed, `implicit_mute` is false for three cases: a soloed strip, a
   bus that a soloed strip feeds, and the master. It is true for every other strip.
3. `explicit_mute` is the strip's own `mute` flag, and it applies whether or not a solo is active. A
   soloed strip that is also muted is silent, and the user interface shows both states.

`AudibleState` travels inside `ChainTopology`, which section 5.5 gives an `audible` field. Chunk C3
publishes it, so the audio thread reads one boolean per strip and computes nothing.

**How the mixer view draws each role.** `StripKind::Bus(BusRole)` decides the strip header, and
every strip reaches it. A `Part` bus takes the part colour and the part name. A `Reverb` or `Delay`
bus takes the muted accent and a fixed icon. A `Monitor` bus is hidden unless the user opens the
monitor section. A `Master` bus is pinned to the trailing edge. Chunk K4 writes it.

**`BusAdd` refuses `Master` and `Monitor`.** Bundle creation builds exactly one of each, and a
second one has no meaning: the master is the strip that reaches the device, and the monitor bus is
the strip that `MonitorMode` feeds. `SessionCommand::BusAdd` therefore returns
`MixError::BusRoleReserved { role }` for either value, and `MixState::validate` returns the same
error for a hand-edited `mix/strips.json` that holds two. `Verb::MixAddBus` reports it as a refusal
through the gateway (critic Q10).

A bus is a strip with no disk reader and no disk writer. The master is a bus with a true-peak meter.
One node type, one `process` call (Ardour 2).

```rust
/// Reject a send or an output that would make a cycle.
///
/// # Errors
/// Returns `MixError::RoutingCycle` with the two strip identifiers,
/// `MixError::BusRoleReserved` for a second master or monitor bus,
/// `MixError::StripBudgetExceeded` past `MAX_STRIPS`,
/// `MixError::ParamBudgetExceeded` past `MAX_PARAMS`,
/// `MixError::SlotBudgetExceeded` for a strip whose `pre_fader` or
/// `post_fader` list passes `MAX_SLOTS`, `MixError::SendBudgetExceeded` for a
/// strip whose `sends` list passes `MAX_SENDS`, and
/// `MixError::CurveBudgetExceeded` for a curve whose point list passes B135
/// (critic C21-6, C21-W14). It also returns `MixError::MissingStrip` and
/// `MixError::MissingParam` for a `SlotId` or a `SendId` on a strip that
/// `MixState` does not hold, which is the read-time half of the one-owner
/// rule (critic C21-W17). **All four constants sit in `duet-time`**, which
/// this crate reaches (section 1.6, critic CR-12, C21-6).
pub fn validate(mix: &MixState) -> Result<(), MixError>;

/// The value range of the parameter at `offset` inside a slot of `kind`.
///
/// It returns `None` when `offset` is at or above the count B96 gives that
/// kind. It is the one source of a knob taper and of an inspector bound, so
/// no view carries a range of its own (critic WR-13).
#[must_use]
pub fn param_range(kind: SlotKind, offset: u16) -> Option<ParamRange>;
```

The routing graph must stay acyclic, and `validate` runs before any topology change reaches the
audio thread.

### 7.2 One curve type for every automation

```rust
/// The points of one curve. The variant carries the domain, so a curve has
/// no domain field that could disagree with its data.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum CurvePoints {
    /// Sorted by `Ticks`, with no duplicate position.
    Beats(Vec<(Ticks, Finite)>),
    /// Sorted by `SuperClock`, with no duplicate position.
    Audio(Vec<(SuperClock, Finite)>),
}

/// One automation curve. The same type serves the fader, the pan, a send
/// level, an equalizer gain, and a MIDI controller (Ardour 7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Curve {
    parameter: ParamId,
    interpolation: Interpolation,
    points: CurvePoints,
}

/// How a curve reads between two points.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Interpolation { Discrete, Linear, Exponential }

impl Curve {
    /// Build a curve. The points are sorted and de-duplicated here.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `MixError::EmptyCurve` for an empty point list,
    /// `MixError::DuplicatePoint` for two points at one position, and
    /// `MixError::CurveBudgetExceeded` for a list above B135. **Every other
    /// collection of this design carries a bound, a budget row and a
    /// refusal** (critic C21-W14): B86 bounds strips, B90 bounds parameters,
    /// and B128 and B129 bound spans. A write-mode ride recorded at frame
    /// rate is the one producer that can pass B135, and `Curve::thin` is the
    /// operation that brings such a capture back inside it, which PR M-07
    /// makes the write-mode contract.
    pub fn new(parameter: ParamId, interpolation: Interpolation, points: CurvePoints)
        -> Result<Self, MixError>;

    /// Which domain this curve is locked to.
    pub fn domain(&self) -> TimeDomain;

    /// The position of one point, in the curve's own domain.
    pub fn position_of(&self, index: usize) -> Option<Position>;

    /// The value at a position. The map converts when the domains differ.
    pub fn value_at(&self, at: Position, map: &TempoMap) -> Finite;

    /// Remove points that a straight line already covers within a tolerance.
    ///
    /// It needs no `&TempoMap`, because every point is in one domain and the
    /// list is already sorted.
    pub fn thin(&mut self, tolerance: Finite);
}
```

Three properties follow from the shape.

1. **A curve cannot hold a point from the wrong domain.** The variant is the domain, so there is no
   field to get wrong and no invariant to check.
2. **`Curve::new` is the only constructor**, and it sorts and de-duplicates.
3. **`thin` needs no map**, because every point is in one domain.

A value is a `Finite`, so a NaN cannot reach the JSON writer (VR4).

The domain is the whole reason a shared timeline works for automation. A fader ride written against
a bar follows a tempo edit. A de-esser ride written against a take does not.

### 7.3 Meters

#### The peak cap has an owner, a field, and two budgets

Design contract 4.4 gives the meter a cap line that holds and then falls. Revision 15 answered the
numeric readout and left the cap with no field, no number, and no owner (critic C15-11).

**Decision: `MeterReader::poll` owns the cap, and no published type carries it.**
`MeterView::caps` is the resolved cap that the reader hands every element, beside
`MeterReading::hold`, which is the highest peak since the last reset. The reader holds the cap at
the peak that set it for B111 and then falls at B112.

**The audio thread is untouched, and the type says so.** `MeterReading` keeps the four fields the
audio thread writes, so `MeterSnapshot` is the size it was, the per-cycle memory copy that B8 bounds
does not grow, and TH9 is unchanged. Revision 16 first put `cap` on `MeterReading`, which gave one
field two writers: the audio thread constructs every `MeterReading` it publishes, Rust has no
partial struct literal, so the audio thread had to write a placeholder that the reader overwrote
(critic C16-8). The cap now lives on the foreground side of the seam alone.

**The reader carries the B111 deadline per strip, and it needs no clock field.**
`MeterReader::caps` holds the cap level of each strip and `MeterReader::holds` holds the
milliseconds of B111 that remain for that strip. `MeterReader::poll` takes the milliseconds since
the last poll as its one argument, which `CoreHost::poll_frame` supplies from the frame it is
inside. A poll that reads a peak above the cap sets the cap and re-arms the hold at B111. A poll
that does not subtracts the elapsed milliseconds from the hold, and it falls the cap at B112 once
the hold reaches zero. The frame delta is the clock, so no entity reads a wall clock and a test
drives the whole rule with plain numbers.

That choice follows the one section 10.2 already made for the over mark: the reader resolves what a
frame shows, and `LevelMeter` and `MeterLayer` paint a value handed to them.

#### The per-slot measurement, and the one cell formula

**PR M-03 and contract 5.2 both ask for a measurement per SLOT, and `MeterSnapshot` is per STRIP**
(critic C21-7). `MeterReading` holds `peak`, `rms`, `true_peak` and `hold` for one strip and carries
no slot dimension, and `ParamSnapshot` travels from the core to the audio thread, which is the wrong
direction for a measurement. So revision 21 had no boundary that could carry one and `StageCurve`
held a field no thread could fill.

**Decision: a second audio-to-core publication, `SlotMeterSnapshot`, declared in section 5.9.** It
is a row of the section 5.8 high-rate table, which is the one place that orders them (critic C23I-N9), and the one `MeterReader` reads beside
`MeterSnapshot`. It is `Copy` plain data with fixed-size fields and no heap field, so TH9 holds on
it exactly as it does on the other two audio-written publications, and B133 states its length and
its size.

**One cell index, stated once here and cited everywhere else.** A cell of the publication is

```text
cell = strip * 2 * MAX_SLOTS + position * MAX_SLOTS + slot
```

where `strip` is the strip's `ChainIndex`, `position` is 0 for a pre-fader slot and 1 for a
post-fader slot, and `slot` is the slot's index in that strip's own list. **Both ends compute it and
neither stores it**: `GraphRunner::run` holds the chain index and the slot index it is inside, and
