`MixView`, `MasterView` and `Inspector` hold the strip order and the slot order they are already
rendering. B133 is the product of the three bounds, so every legal address has a cell and no address
needs a search. `SlotMeterSnapshot::live` gives the number of cells the configured topology fills,
exactly as `MeterSnapshot::live` does for strips.

`MeterReader::slot_measure` answers one cell for one frame, and `StageCurve::measure` is the value
it returns, so a view paints and computes nothing (section 10.3).


Three laws only. Ardour ships thirteen, and the research file rejects that (Ardour, reject list).

```rust
/// The three meter laws that version one shows.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum MeterLaw { Peak, Rms, LufsTruePeak }

/// One strip's meter values for one frame.
///
/// **It carries no peak cap.** The cap is a foreground value that
/// `MeterReader` resolves per frame, and a field here would give the audio
/// thread a placeholder to write every cycle (section 7.3, critic C16-8).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MeterReading { peak: Finite, rms: Finite, true_peak: Finite, hold: Finite }


impl MeterReading {
    /// Every level at zero. `MeterView::silent` fills its array with it.
    pub const SILENT: Self = Self {
        peak: Finite::ZERO,
        rms: Finite::ZERO,
        true_peak: Finite::ZERO,
        hold: Finite::ZERO,
    };
}

/// One slot's live measurement for one frame.
///
/// **It carries TWO quantities and not one** (critic C21-7). Contract 5.2
/// draws a live dot at the compressor INPUT level and a gain-REDUCTION bar on
/// the limiter, and PR M-03 is a MUST that asks the strip to show a
/// compressor's gain reduction as a live meter. Revision 21 gave `StageCurve`
/// one `Option<Finite>` named `live` with no producer at all, so one scalar
/// was asked to carry two different quantities and no thread could fill it.
///
/// `input` is the level the slot saw at its input, on the B106 scale.
/// `reduction` is the decibels of gain the slot removed this frame, at or
/// below zero. A slot kind that measures neither publishes `Finite::ZERO` for
/// both.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SlotMeasure { input: Finite, reduction: Finite }

impl SlotMeasure {
    /// No input and no reduction. `SlotMeterSnapshot::silent` fills its
    /// array with it, exactly as `MeterView::silent` fills its own.
    pub const SILENT: Self = Self { input: Finite::ZERO, reduction: Finite::ZERO };
}

/// The held over marks of every strip, as a bitset.
///
/// B86 sits below the bit width of a `u64`, so one word covers every strip a
/// mix can hold, and `MixError::StripBudgetExceeded` keeps that true. It is a
/// `duet-dsp` type from revision 12, because `MeterView` carries it and every
/// consumer of a meter value reaches this crate (critic CR-4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct HeldMarks(u64);

/// Every strip's meter values for one frame, resolved for painting.
///
/// **It is the one value `crates/duet` reads about a meter.**
/// `duet_core::MeterReader` builds it from the audio thread's
/// `MeterSnapshot` and the shared reset generations, so no `duet-engine`
/// name and no `triple_buffer` name reaches the application crate
/// (section 7.3, critic CR-4). `held` already answers the generation
/// compare, so the view paints and decides nothing.
/// It derives no `Default`: the standard library implements `Default` for an
/// array up to thirty-two elements and B86 is larger, so the type carries a
/// named constructor instead, exactly as `ResetGenerations` does.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MeterView {
    readings: [MeterReading; MAX_STRIPS],
    /// Per strip, the peak cap of design contract 4.4, as `MeterReader`
    /// resolved it for this frame under B111 and B112. It is a foreground
    /// value and the audio thread publishes none of it (section 7.3,
    /// critic C16-8).
    caps: [Finite; MAX_STRIPS],
    held: HeldMarks,
    live: u16,
}

impl MeterView {
    /// Every strip silent, no cap raised, and no mark held.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn silent() -> Self {
        Self {
            readings: [MeterReading::SILENT; MAX_STRIPS],
            caps: [Finite::ZERO; MAX_STRIPS],
            held: HeldMarks(0),
            live: 0,
        }
    }
}

/// The held peak-over flag of one strip.
///
/// The audio thread sets it on the first sample above the ceiling and never
/// clears it. Only `Verb::MeterReset` clears it, so the mark survives every
/// frame until the user acts. PR M-05 and design contract 4.4 both require
/// that behaviour, and revision 7 gave it no type (critic Q11).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OverMark(bool);
```

#### The three meter zones

Design contract 4.4 gives the level meter three colour zones, and revision 17 carried neither
threshold as a number this document declares (critic N16-11, N17-3). **B114 is -12 dB and B115 is
-3 dB.** A value below B114 paints in the base colour, a value at or above B114 and below B115
paints in the middle colour, and a value at or above B115 paints in the warning colour. `OverMark`
answers the ceiling itself and no zone does.

**The zones are a paint decision and not a meter decision**, so `MeterLayer` and `LevelMeter` each
read the two ids through `DuetTokens` and `duet-dsp` publishes no zone. That keeps the meter law one
function, which B106 states, and it keeps the audio thread untouched for the same reason the peak
cap left `MeterReading` (section 7.3, critic C16-8).

**One function maps a decibel value to a meter height, and every element calls it.** Design contract
4.4 fixes the scale, B106 carries its three numbers, and revision 12 gave `LevelMeter` a `scale`
field of the wrong type instead (critic WR-13).

```rust
/// The fraction of a meter's height that one decibel value reaches.
///
/// It applies the non-linear scale of design contract 4.4, which B106 states:
/// `METER_FLOOR_DB` reaches zero, `METER_CEILING_DB` reaches one, and
/// `METER_MID_DB` reaches `METER_MID_FRACTION`. A value below the floor
/// clamps to zero and a value above the ceiling clamps to one, so the result
/// is always in the unit range. It lives in `duet_dsp::meter_law`, which
/// `crates/duet` reaches, so no view carries a scale of its own.
#[must_use]
pub fn db_to_fraction(db: Finite) -> Finite;

/// The fraction of the loudness bar that one integrated loudness reaches.
///
/// It applies the scale of design contract 5.3, which B143 states: `LUFS_FLOOR`
/// reaches zero and `LUFS_CEILING` reaches one, linearly between them, and a
/// value outside clamps. `LUFS_TOLERANCE` is the half width of the band the
/// bar paints around the target, in the same unit, so `LufsMeter` paints the
/// band through this function too (critic C22I-W12).
#[must_use]
pub fn lufs_to_fraction(lufs: Finite) -> Finite;

/// The fraction of the true-peak bar that one true-peak value reaches.
///
/// It applies the scale of design contract 5.3, which B144 states:
/// `TRUE_PEAK_FLOOR` reaches zero and `TRUE_PEAK_CEILING` reaches one. The
/// ceiling is above zero, because a true-peak reading can pass full scale and
/// the bar has to show by how much.
#[must_use]
pub fn true_peak_to_fraction(peak: Finite) -> Finite;

/// The gain one point of the fader travel sets, in decibels.
///
/// It applies the taper of design contract 4.2, which B145 states: unity gain
/// sits at `FADER_UNITY_FRACTION` of the travel and everything below
/// `FADER_SILENCE_FRACTION` answers minus infinity. `ParamRange` gives bounds
/// alone and cannot express a unity point inside the travel, so `Fader` had
/// to invent the map or write a literal and DR3 forbids the literal (critic
/// C22I-W12). `fader_db_to_fraction` is the inverse and the two are tested
/// against each other.
#[must_use]
pub fn fader_fraction_to_db(fraction: Finite) -> Finite;

/// The point of the fader travel that one gain in decibels sits at.
#[must_use]
pub fn fader_db_to_fraction(db: Finite) -> Finite;
```

**The latch lives on the audio thread, and the reset crosses as one generation per strip.** The
audio thread sees every sample and the user interface reads at B2, so a peak between two frames
would be lost if the view held the latch.

**The reset path is `ResetGenerations`, one `AtomicU32` per strip, which section 5.6 declares and
`GraphState` holds behind an `Arc`.** `duet-core` holds the other handle and increments the entry of
the strip the verb names; `Verb::MeterReset { strip: None }` increments every entry. Revision 8
carried one counter for every strip, so `MeterReset { strip: Some(id) }` cleared all of them
(critic R6), and revision 9 named the array in one table row and gave it no type and no owner
(critic W2).

**The audio thread stores the value it last saw, and `ChainState::reset_seen` is where it stores
it** (section 5.5). Once per cycle the audio thread reads its own strip's entry with a relaxed load and compares it with
`reset_seen`. On a change it clears that strip's `OverMark`, clears that strip's
`MeterReading::hold`, which is the "highest peak since the last reset" that design contract 4.4
names, and stores the new value. An atomic load allocates nothing, locks nothing, and cannot block,
so TH1 holds. **`GraphState::chains` is the per-strip array of last-seen values**: one `ChainState`
per strip already exists, and a second parallel array would need a second index and could disagree
with the first. `reset_seen` sits on `ChainState` and not on `MeterState`, because `MeterState` is a
`duet-dsp` type and `Generation` is a `duet-engine` type (PG20).

**The audio thread clears its own held state at the next cycle.** It reads the per-strip entry of
`ResetGenerations` with a relaxed load, compares it with `ChainState::reset_seen`, clears that
strip's `OverMark` and that strip's `MeterReading::hold` on a change, and stores the new value.
**Whenever it latches a mark it writes `reset_seen` into that strip's entry of
`MeterSnapshot::latched`**, so the published value says which reset generation the mark belongs to.

**The reset has a second path, because the engine is not always running.** In
`EngineState::NoServer`, `OpenTimeout`, `NoDevice`, `RateUnavailable`, and `Faulted` no audio cycle
runs, so nothing reads the generation and the triple buffer holds the last published
`MeterSnapshot` with its marks for as long as the engine stays stopped.

**`duet_core::MeterReader` resolves the mark, and the view decides nothing.** The reader owns the
one `triple_buffer::Output<MeterSnapshot>` and a third handle on the shared `Arc<ResetGenerations>`.
**`CoreHost` owns the one reader**, and no view holds an `Output`: `triple_buffer` supplies one read
end per publication, and revision 12 gave that one end to two views (critic CR-11). Once per frame,
before any child view renders, `CoreHost::poll_frame` calls `MeterReader::poll`, which reads the
snapshot, resolves every mark, and stores the resulting `MeterView` in a foreground-only slot on the
reader. `MeterReader::latest` then answers every view with a copy of that slot. Section 10.2 states
the frame order.

**The per-strip compare is the rule, and it is stated once here.** For strip `i` the reader paints a
mark when `over[i]` is set **and** `latched[i]` is at or above the reset generation
`ResetGenerations[i]`, which it reads with a relaxed load. Nothing else decides the bit.

Four cases follow from that one sentence, and each one is the behaviour design contract 4.4 asks
for.

1. **A clip with no reset.** The audio thread sets `over[i]` and writes the current generation into
   `latched[i]`. The two values are equal, so the mark paints on the next frame and every frame
   after it.
2. **A reset while the engine runs.** `Verb::MeterReset` increments `ResetGenerations[i]` on the
   core thread. The next frame finds `latched[i]` below the new value, so the mark clears at once,
   before the audio thread has even seen the increment.
3. **A reset while the engine is stopped.** No cycle runs, so the triple buffer holds the same
   snapshot. Its `latched[i]` is below the new reset generation, so the mark stays clear for as long
   as the engine stays stopped.
4. **A clip after a reset.** The audio thread applies the increment at its next cycle, clears the
   mark and the hold, and writes the new generation into `reset_seen`. The next latch therefore
   carries the new generation and paints again.

**Revision 11 inverted the rule and the `CLIP` indicator became unreachable.** It added a mark only
when the snapshot generation *moved*, and the generation moves only on a reset, so no mark ever
entered the painted set (critic CR-1). It also carried one scalar generation, which cannot publish
B86 independent counters, so `Verb::MeterReset { strip: Some(id) }` had no value to publish at all.
Test 9 of section 10.7 asserted one direction only and passed the inverted rule; revision 12 gives
it both directions.

**The core never writes the `triple_buffer`.** Its writer is the audio thread (section 5.8), and a
`MeterSnapshot` inside a `CoreEvent` would put a `duet-engine` type in `duet-command`, which is the
Cargo cycle PG20 refuses. Revision 9 asked `duet-core` to clear the marks in the published snapshot
itself, and no mechanism in section 5.8 let it (critic W2).

`MeterLaw::LufsTruePeak` needs four-times oversampling, which costs. **Decision: the true-peak law
runs on the master strip only.** Every other strip runs peak and RMS, because 32 oversampled meters
would not fit B8.

The audio thread writes each reading into a `triple_buffer::Input<MeterSnapshot>`. No meter value
travels as an event (critic 4.2).

### 7.4 The export pipeline

`duet-export` runs the offline graph over the dummy backend in `Freewheel` mode.

```
render the mix graph (dummy backend, freewheel)
  -> ChannelMap
  -> SilenceTrim
  -> SampleRateConvert (rubato)
  -> pass 1: LoudnessAnalyse (ebur128) and write an f32 intermediate file
  -> pass 2: read the intermediate -> Gain (computed) -> TruePeakLimiter
             -> Dither -> Encoder
```

The intermediate file exists because pass one must finish before pass two knows the gain. Ardour
uses the same `Intermediate` stage for the same reason (Ardour 10).

**The intermediate file has a named place and a named owner.** It is
`exports/.tmp/<job>/intermediate.f32`, and the running job owns the whole directory. Section 9.6 states the cleanup contract for a cancelled job and a failed
job, and section 4.1 bounds the directory.

```rust
/// One declarative record that fully determines a render (Ardour 10). It is
/// below the VR5 size bound, which the PG24 table prints for `ExportSpec`, so
/// VR5 gives it `Copy`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ExportSpec {
    container: Container,
    sample_format: SampleFormat,
    sample_rate: SampleRate,
    dither: DitherKind,
    normalization: Normalization,
}

/// The output container.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Container { Wav, Rf64, Flac }

/// The output sample format.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum SampleFormat { Int16, Int24, Float32 }

/// Which dither a render applies before it narrows to an integer format.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum DitherKind { None, Rectangular, Triangular, Shaped }

/// How the render sets the level. Every level is a `Finite`, so a hand
/// edited file cannot carry a NaN into the limiter (VR4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Normalization {
    None,
    Peak { dbfs: Finite },
    Loudness { lufs: Finite, true_peak_dbtp: Finite },
}
```

B75 gives the two presets. Custom takes both numbers from the user, through `Finite::new`, so the
form rejects a non-finite entry before the verb is built.

### 7.5 File formats

`duet-export` writes every render through `duet-media`. It names no format crate of its own.

| Container | Crate inside `duet-media` | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| WAV | `hound` | The default for a render under the B67 container limit |
| RF64 | `bwavfile` | The render promotes when the predicted size passes the limit, and the spec records the promotion |
| FLAC | `flacenc` | Integer formats only; a float render refuses FLAC with `ExportError::FormatMismatch` |

The predicted size is `frames * channels * bytes_per_sample + 4096`. The render computes it before
the first write, so the promotion is a decision and not a recovery.

`symphonia` decodes an imported file in a format Duet does not write. That is how a user brings an
MP3 or an AAC reference track into a project.

---

## 8. MIDI

The crate is `duet-midi`. Devices are plug and play, with no setup dialog.

### 8.1 Two traits: presence and stream

Revision 5 gave one trait four methods and then said "the MIDI byte stream stays on `midir` on both
platforms". The two statements disagree, and the identifier that joins the platform layer to `midir`
had no mapping (critic S9). PR C-10, plug and play with no setup, rests on that mapping, so revision
6 splits the trait and declares the map.

```rust
/// Port discovery and hot-plug notification. One implementation per platform.
pub trait MidiPresence: Send {
    /// Every port the platform can see now, as a raw platform handle.
    ///
    /// **It mints no identity.** `MidiPortMap::insert` is the one place that
    /// turns a platform handle into a `MidiPortInfo`, and the MIDI thread is
    /// the one owner of the map (TH10). A presence source that returned a
    /// minted value would need the map on a second thread (critic W6).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `MidiError::Enumerate` when the platform refuses the query.
    fn ports(&self) -> Result<Vec<PlatformPort>, MidiError>;

    /// Subscribe to port arrival and port departure. The sink carries a raw
    /// `PlatformPort`, for the same reason.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `MidiError::Hotplug` when the platform gives no notification,
    /// and `MidiError::OpenTimeout` past B22.
    fn subscribe_hotplug(&mut self, sink: HotplugSink)
        -> Result<HotplugSubscription, MidiError>;
}

/// The byte stream. `midir` is the one implementation on both platforms.
pub trait MidiStream: Send {
    /// Open an input and push every parsed message into the sink.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `MidiError::Unresolved` when the map holds no `midir` index
    /// for this identity, `MidiError::Open` when the port is gone, and
    /// `MidiError::OpenTimeout` past B22.
    fn open_input(&mut self, port: &MidiPortId, sink: MidiSink)
        -> Result<MidiInputHandle, MidiError>;

    /// # Errors
    /// The same three errors as `open_input`.
    fn open_output(&mut self, port: &MidiPortId) -> Result<MidiOutputHandle, MidiError>;
}

/// One port as every other thread sees it.
///
/// It carries both identities, so a consumer needs no lookup and therefore
/// no reference to `MidiPortMap` (critic Q6).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MidiPortInfo { slot: PortSlot, id: MidiPortId, is_source: bool }

/// A device came or went. Both variants carry the whole `MidiPortInfo`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum HotplugEvent { PortAdded(MidiPortInfo), PortRemoved(MidiPortInfo) }
```

| Implementation | Trait | Platform | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CoreMidiPresence` | `MidiPresence` | macOS | The `coremidi` client notify callback. Push, no poll. |
| `PipeWireRegistryPresence` | `MidiPresence` | Linux | The `pipewire` registry listener, filtered to MIDI nodes and ports. Push, no poll. |
| `MidirPresence` | `MidiPresence` | Both | A port-list comparison at B22. The documented exception, used only when the platform presence source fails to open. |
| `MidirStream` | `MidiStream` | Both | The one byte path. It opens by `midir` port index. |

`midir` reports no connect and no disconnect, with five open issues (survey), so the fallback polls.
`MidirPresence::subscribe_hotplug` carries the reason in its own documentation comment, as the
event-architecture rule requires.

#### The port identity and the map

**Two identity types, and the split is the decision.** `MidiPortId` is the app-stable identity a
user reads and a verb carries. **No document field holds one**: `Track::input` keys on `DeviceKey`
and so does `Calibration`, and PR C-10 makes the bind automatic, so nothing persists a port
identity (critic Q19). `PortSlot` is the fixed-size handle the audio path and the note path carry. Revision 6 had one type, put it on both surfaces, and the audio record then
owned a heap allocation that the audio thread freed on every note (critic N1).

```rust
// in duet-command
/// One MIDI port, as the audio path and the note path address it.
///
/// It is two bytes and `Copy`, so a record that carries one allocates
/// nothing and frees nothing (TH1). `MidiPortMap` mints it and is the one
/// place that turns it back into an identity a user reads.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PortSlot(u16);

/// A stable identity for one MIDI port, in the form
/// `<platform>:<unique>:<name>`. It is a string newtype, so it derives every
/// comparison trait of VR1 row 1 and it does not derive `Copy`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MidiPortId(Box<str>);

// in duet-midi
/// One platform port handle. Three namespaces meet here.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PlatformPort {
    PipeWire { global: u32, name: Box<str> },
    CoreMidi { unique: i32, name: Box<str> },
    Midir { index: usize, name: Box<str> },
}

/// The one translation between the four namespaces: a `PortSlot`, a
/// `MidiPortId`, a platform handle, and the `midir` index that opens the
/// port now.
///
/// **It derives no `Default`** (critic C22I-2). A default map would be a map
/// with no write end of the B100 queue, and the one owner of port identity
/// cannot exist without the carrier that reports a change of it. The MIDI
/// thread builds one value, with the queue handle the core minted.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MidiPortMap {
    by_slot: BTreeMap<PortSlot, MidiPortInfo>,
    by_id: BTreeMap<MidiPortId, PortSlot>,
    platform: BTreeMap<PortSlot, PlatformPort>,
    /// The next slot this process run mints. B88 bounds it.
    next: u16,
    /// Which `PortSlot` each `BoundPort` names, at B139.
    ///
    /// `bind` takes the first free entry and returns the `BoundPort`, and
    /// `unbind` clears it, so the index space the audio thread reads is the
    /// set of ports the engine has BOUND and never the set it has seen
    /// (critic C23I-4). `MidiError::BoundPortsExhausted` refuses a bind past
    /// B139.
    bound: [Option<PortSlot>; MAX_BOUND_PORTS],
    /// The write end of the B100 hot-plug queue to the core.
    ///
    /// `insert` and `retire` each mint one `HotplugEvent` and push it here.
    /// This map is the one owner of port identity (TH10), so it is the one
    /// party that can mint the `MidiPortInfo` the event carries; revision 22
    /// stated that and declared the queue on `DuetCore` alone, so the
    /// producer end had no owner (critic C22I-2, TH13).
    hotplug: Arc<ArrayQueue<HotplugEvent>>,
}

impl MidiPortMap {
    /// Record a platform port and return the value every other thread reads.
    ///
    /// A port that returns after a departure keeps the slot it already had,
    /// so the counter advances once per distinct identity and never once per
    /// connect.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `MidiError::PortSlotsExhausted` when B88 distinct identities
    /// have been seen in one process run.
    fn insert(&mut self, port: PlatformPort) -> Result<MidiPortInfo, MidiError>;

    /// The `midir` index that opens this identity now.
    #[must_use]
    fn midir_index(&self, port: &MidiPortId) -> Option<usize>;

    /// Retire a port that left. The record stays, so a later return of the
    /// same identity reuses its slot, and a record still in a ring is never
    /// misread.
    fn retire(&mut self, port: &MidiPortId);

    /// Take the first free `BoundPort` for one slot (critic C23I-4).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `MidiError::BoundPortsExhausted` when B139 ports are bound.
    fn bind(&mut self, slot: PortSlot) -> Result<BoundPort, MidiError>;

    /// Release one `BoundPort`, so a later bind may reuse the index.
    fn unbind(&mut self, port: BoundPort);
}
```

**The MIDI thread is the one owner of `MidiPortMap`, and no other thread holds a reference** (TH10,
section 5.7).
`insert` and `retire` take `&mut self`, and `midir_index` takes `&self`; all three run on the MIDI
thread. Every other thread reads a `MidiPortInfo` that the map already minted and that the event
carries. Revision 7 said that `duet-core` turned a slot back into a name through the map, which put
a shared reference across a thread boundary that no mechanism sanctioned (critic Q6).

**A slot is never exhausted by re-plugging.** `PortSlot` wraps a `u16`, and a session that connects
and disconnects one device a thousand times mints one slot. The counter advances only for an
identity the map has never seen, so B88 bounds the number of **distinct** devices in one process
run. Past B88 `insert` returns `MidiError::PortSlotsExhausted`, the port stays unbound, and the
status bar shows the `BindFailed` line of section 8.2 (critic Q18).

**Both directions go through the map, and one thread runs it.** The platform listener produces a
raw `PlatformPort` and nothing else. The MIDI thread drains that queue, calls `insert`, and is
therefore the one thread that ever mints a `MidiPortInfo`. Revision 9 gave the listener thread the
`HotplugEvent` to push, and only `insert` mints the `MidiPortInfo` that event carries, so two
threads needed `&mut MidiPortMap` (critic W6). `MidirStream::open_input` calls
`midir_index`, and a `None` returns `MidiError::Unresolved { port }`, which reaches the user as
`MidiEvent::BindFailed`. The `midir` port list is re-read on every hot-plug event, so an index that
moved is corrected before the next open.

**VR1 row 2 pays for both lookups.** `MidiPortId` derives `Ord` and `Hash`, so an identity is a
`BTreeMap` key; `PortSlot` derives the same set, so a slot is one too. The audio thread asks the map
nothing: a record carries the slot it needs.

#### How a hot-plug event crosses to the core

The platform listener runs on its own thread, and `duet-core` runs on the core thread. Section 5.8
holds every boundary, and revision 7 gave this one no row, no mechanism, and no bound (critic Q6).

1. **The listener thread pushes a `PlatformPort` into a bounded
   `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue<PlatformPort>` at B87.** It is the only producer, and it mints
   nothing: a `PlatformPort` is the platform handle the callback already holds.
2. **The MIDI thread drains that queue and calls `insert` or `retire`.** It owns `MidiPortMap`
   (TH10), so it is the one thread that turns a platform handle into a `MidiPortInfo`. It then
   pushes one `HotplugEvent` into a second bounded queue at B100, core bound. A drain is not the B9
   path, so moving the `Box<str>` a `PlatformPort` carries costs no note its deadline.
3. **`duet-core` drains the B100 queue once per frame**, in the same
   `Window::on_next_frame` callback that drains the note-entry queue (section 8.3). A device that
   arrives between two frames is visible in the next frame.
4. **On overflow either queue keeps the newest value and sets a resync flag.** A port that connects
   and disconnects faster than one frame produces events the user cannot act on, so the newest state
   is the useful one. The flag makes the MIDI thread issue one `MidiPresence::ports` enumeration on
   its next drain, which rebuilds the whole port list from the platform. The note-entry queue drops
   the oldest and counts; these two keep the newest and re-enumerate, because a presence event is a
   state and a note is an event.
5. **The re-enumeration is bounded by the same rule.** It runs on the MIDI thread under B22 and
   publishes one `HotplugEvent` per present port.

**The collision rule, when two ports share a name.** A platform unique identifier makes the identity
unique on its own, and PipeWire and CoreMIDI both supply one. `midir` supplies none. When the map
must mint an identity from a name alone, and that name is already present, it appends an ordinal in
first-seen order, and the ordinal is stable while the port stays present. Two identical unnamed
devices may therefore swap ordinals across a re-plug. The application re-binds by the same rule, so
the user sees one bound input either way, and the status bar names the port it bound.

#### Why the PipeWire registry and not the ALSA sequencer

The operator set PipeWire as the Linux audio server (platform, orchestrator decision 2). Three
reasons decide the hot-plug source, and the order matters because the first one is conditional.

1. **It needs no `unsafe`.** `ListenerLocalBuilder::global`, `global_remove`, and `register` are safe
   Rust, so node and port hot-plug needs no unsafe in the caller (platform, pipewire facts).
   `unsafe` is denied workspace-wide, so this reason is sufficient on its own.
2. **One session bus serves audio and MIDI.** cpal's PipeWire host already connects to the server,
   so the MIDI listener adds no second connection and no second failure mode.
3. **It is expected to add no duplicate crate version**, and chunk M3 verifies it. cpal 0.18.2 pins
   `alsa` 0.11 on Linux, and that pin is not optional. The PipeWire feature of cpal already brings
   `pipewire` 0.10.1, so the MIDI listener shares that exact version. **The research file records no
   `alsa` version for `midir`, and `midir` is the byte path on Linux** (critic S16). Chunk M3 runs `cargo tree -i alsa` and records the result. If `midir` brings a second
   `alsa` major, this reason is void, reasons 1 and 2 still decide, and `deny.toml` reports the
   duplicate as a warning rather than a failure.

`alsa` is not a direct Duet dependency on either reading.

### 8.2 Plug and play

On `PortAdded` the crate classifies the port. When the port is a music source and no input is bound,
the application binds it and emits `MidiEvent::InputBound`. No dialog appears. When more than one
candidate arrives, the application binds the first and offers a change in the top bar.

**The bind is bounded.** `MidiStream::open_input` runs under B22, on the MIDI thread. On expiry, or
on an unresolved identity, the port stays unbound and the crate raises
`MidiEvent::BindFailed { port, reason }`. The status bar shows one line
with a retry action, and the automatic bind does not try that port again until it leaves and
returns.

Ardour queues connection work on a helper thread rather than the caller's thread, and Duet does the
same (Ardour 7).

#### A bound port that leaves, in a record pass and outside one

Revision 7 covered arrival and a failed bind and said nothing about a departure, so a truncated MIDI
take carried no evidence of its cause. The audio path has `EngineFault::DeviceLost`; the MIDI path
now has the same shape (critic Q7).

**The take continues. It is never cancelled and never truncated.** A record pass is the user's work,
and the loss of an input is not a reason to discard what is already on disk.

Four steps run in order, and each one has an owner.

1. **The engine silences the held notes within one cycle.** `EngineProcess::sounding` holds one
   `SoundingNotes` bitset per bound port, at B139, and the MIDI thread mints one
   `MidiMessage::PortGone` on the B32 ring when a port leaves. The audio thread drains that ring
   every cycle and already orders it by `SampleClock`, so the departure lands in the cycle it
   belongs to; the cycle that reads it synthesizes a note-off for every set bit of that slot and
   clears the bitset, so the monitor voice never sustains a note the user cannot release. It
   allocates nothing: the set is a fixed-size bitset over the 128 note numbers, which is two stores
   to clear. **Revision 22 stated this step and declared neither the set nor the message** (critic
   C22I-7): no declaration held a note set, `MidiMessage` carried no departure arm, and a departure
   reached the CORE over B100 while no declared path ran core to audio, so the step could not
   run at all.
2. **The crate emits `MidiEvent::InputLost { port }`.** The status bar shows one line that names the
   port, with no modal surface, because the user can still sing and still play another controller.
3. **The core sets `TakeFlag::MidiPortLost` on the open take**, through the ordinary
   `SessionCommand` path of section 6.4. The take list marks it, so a user who finds a short MIDI
   take reads the cause.
4. **The bind policy rebinds on return.** `MidiPortMap` keeps the identity and its slot, so the same
   device returns with the same `PortSlot`, and section 8.2's automatic bind runs again with no
   dialog. A record pass that loses and regains a controller therefore continues in one take.

Outside a record pass the same four steps run, and step 3 does nothing because no take is open.

### 8.3 Note entry from a keyboard into the score

The MIDI thread parses bytes into fixed-size records. It then writes each record to **two
independent destinations**, because `rtrb` is strictly single producer and single consumer.

Both record types live in `duet-command` (PL2). `duet-midi`, `duet-engine`, and `duet-core` all
carry that edge.

```rust
/// A MIDI note number, 0 to 127.
///
/// The VR1 row for this type states the use of every derive it carries, and
/// this comment states none (critic C22I-W17). Revision 22 wrote that the
/// derives paid for a sounding-note set, and the VR1 row read that the set
/// is a fixed-size bitset which asks for neither, so one fact had two
/// answers, which DR1 and DR4 forbid.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MidiNote(u8);

/// A MIDI velocity, 0 to 127.
///
/// It derives `PartialEq` and no total comparison. VR1 names no map, no set,
/// and no sort that orders a velocity, and revision 9 gave it `Eq` and `Ord`
/// with no stated use (critic W16).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Velocity(u8);

/// One parsed MIDI message: a tag over at most two data values.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum MidiMessage {
    NoteOn { note: MidiNote, velocity: Velocity },
    NoteOff { note: MidiNote, velocity: Velocity },
    ControlChange { controller: u8, value: u8 },
    PitchBend { value: i16 },
    Sustain { down: bool },
    /// The port this record names has left (section 8.2 step 1).
    ///
    /// **It is the carrier of the departure fact to the AUDIO thread**
    /// (critic C22I-7). A departure reaches the core over B100 and no
    /// declared path runs core to audio, so revision 22 told the audio
    /// thread to silence the held notes of a departed port within one cycle
    /// and gave it no message that named the port. The B32 ring already
    /// orders every MIDI fact by `SampleClock`, so the silence lands in the
    /// cycle the departure belongs to and never earlier. The MIDI thread
    /// mints it, because `MidiPortMap` is the one owner of port identity
    /// (TH10).
    PortGone,
}

/// One parsed MIDI record. Every field is `Copy` and fixed size, so a
/// duplicate write is cheaper than a second thread.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MidiRecord { port: BoundPort, at: SampleClock, message: MidiMessage }

/// Which of the bound input ports one record came from, at B139.
///
/// **It is not a `PortSlot`** (critic C23I-4). A `PortSlot` is dense over
/// every distinct identity the process has SEEN and B88 bounds it at 1024; a
/// `BoundPort` is dense over the ports the engine has BOUND and B139 bounds
/// it at 16, which is the length of `EngineProcess::sounding`. Revision 23
/// indexed a 16-long array with a value whose range is 1024, so a user who
/// connected a seventeenth controller gave a bound port an index past the end
/// of the array and the silence pass of section 8.2 step 1 could not run.
/// `MidiPortMap::bind` mints one and `MidiPortMap::bound` maps it back.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BoundPort(u16);

/// One note the user played, ready for the score. The core turns it into a
/// `ScoreCommand`.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NoteEntry { port: PortSlot, at: SampleClock, note: MidiNote, velocity: Velocity }
```

**Both records are small, fixed, and `Copy`, and the PG24 table prints the size of each one.**
`SampleClock` is an `i64`, so the alignment is 8. `PortSlot` is a `u16`. `MidiMessage` is a one-byte
tag over a two-byte payload at alignment 2. `MidiNote` and `Velocity` are one byte each. Section
1.9's recorded-size block carries a row for `MidiRecord` and for `NoteEntry`, so the PG25 roster
compile measures both on every run and neither number can go stale. A test in `duet-command` asserts
both with `size_of`. Revision 7 stated two sizes over three types that no block declared, so no
reader could check the arithmetic (critic Q1, Q2); revision 12 stated them as literals that no guard
read (critic WR-15).

**Neither record names `MidiPortId`.** A `Box<str>` inside either one would break three rules at
once: the `Copy` derive would not compile, the size claim above would be wrong, and the ring at B32
would allocate on the MIDI thread and free on the audio thread. TH10 forbids the first and TH1
forbids the second, and revision 8 cited TH1 for both (critic R8). **A consumer that needs the name reads the `MidiPortInfo` the hot-plug event carried**,
which the core already holds from its own drain (section 8.1). No thread outside the MIDI thread
touches `MidiPortMap`.

| Destination | Mechanism | Consumer | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| The sound path | `rtrb` ring of `MidiRecord`, B32 | The audio thread, every cycle, in every mode | The monitor voice and, when armed, a MIDI take |
| The note path | `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue<NoteEntry>`, B31 | `duet-core`, once per frame | A `ScoreCommand::InsertNote` and then a `CoreEvent` |

**The sound path never crosses the GPUI thread, in Compose as well as in Record.** The MIDI thread
writes the record, the audio thread reads it in the same cycle, and the monitor voice sounds it. B9
covers exactly this path.

**The note path is a second, slower path, and `crates/duet` is not on it.** `duet-core` drains the
queue once per frame. It turns a note-on into `ScoreCommand::InsertNote` at the caret, with the
duration the `DurationSelector` reports. It applies the command and emits `CoreEvent::ScoreChanged`.
`ComposeView` reacts to the event like any other change, so the view sees a message and not a shared
queue.

The caret and the pending duration live in `ComposeView`. The core reads them from the last
`CoreInput::SetEntryContext { caret, duration }` the view sent, which the view sends whenever either
one changes. That is one value the view pushes, not a value the core pulls.

**The drain and the paint happen in one frame, and that is what makes B10 hold.** `crates/duet`
registers the drain with `Window::on_next_frame` and `duet-core` supplies the plain method it calls
(section 13.2, critic C16-W9). The audit records the callback at
`gpui-pre-0.3.5/src/window.rs:2586`. That callback runs at the start of a frame, before the render
pass of the same frame. **Cite the implementation and not the doc comment**: `window.rs:1765` and
`:1769` run the callbacks and `:1782` to `:1791` draw and present, so the order is in the code. The
doc comment at `:2585` states the opposite of its own implementation, so a reader who checks the
`:2586` citation alone finds a contradiction and not a proof (concern N16-4). A note that arrives between two frames is drained and painted in the next
frame, not the one after it. A `cx.spawn` task would give a worse figure, because GPUI orders no
spawned task against the render pass.

A full note-entry queue drops the oldest record and increments a counter. That is correct: a note
the user cannot see yet is not worth a stall on the MIDI thread. The counter reaches the user
interface as `CoreEvent::EntryDropped { count }` on the next drain.

Velocity does not set a dynamic by default. A keyboard velocity is a poor notation dynamic, so the
score takes the top bar's current dynamic. A context-menu action maps velocity to dynamics when the
user asks.

The monitor voice is one small synthesized vowel-like tone that follows the dynamic (PR 11 Q4). It
lives in `duet-dsp::voice`, so the engine and the Compose monitor share one implementation.

### 8.4 MIDI file import

One function serves the command-line interface, the MCP verb, and the menu item.

```rust
/// Read a Standard MIDI File into a score and a tempo map.
///
/// # Errors
/// Returns `InterchangeError::Parse` for a malformed file, and
/// `InterchangeError::Unsupported` for a format this build does not read.
pub fn import_smf(bytes: &[u8], options: &SmfImportOptions)
    -> Result<SmfImport, InterchangeError>;

/// How to map a Standard MIDI File onto the score.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SmfImportOptions {
    /// Snap every onset and duration to this value. `None` keeps the raw ticks.
    quantize: Option<NoteValue>,
    /// Which track goes to which part.
    part_map: PartMapping,
    /// Take the tempo map from the file, or keep the current one.
    tempo: TempoImport,
}

/// What an import produced.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SmfImport { pub score: Score, pub tempo_map: TempoMap, pub warnings: Vec<ImportWarning> }
```

`midly` carries the Unlicense, which `deny.toml` must allow. Appendix B.4 lists it.

---

## 9. The agent gateway

The vocabulary is `duet-command`. The implementation is `duet-core`. The transport is `duet-agent`.
The front end is the `duet` binary.

### 9.1 One flat verb list

Ardour splits "what the application can do" from "who asks". Every control surface is a translator
over one device-free verb list (Ardour 11, adopt item 9). Duet takes the same shape and makes it the
primary interface.

```rust
/// One verb. Every client speaks this list and no other.
///
/// It derives the VR1 set and nothing else. It asks no payload for `Eq` or
/// `Hash`, so a new payload type can never break this enum. The agent
/// transport compares a request with what `Status` reports, and `PartialEq`
/// is what that comparison needs.
///
/// A large payload is boxed, so that the rustc lint
/// `variant_size_differences` stays satisfied and the enum stays small.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Verb {
    // Project lifecycle
    ProjectCreate(Box<CreateRequest>),
    ProjectOpen { path: Box<PathBuf> },
    ProjectClose,
    ProjectConvertRate { rate: SampleRate },
    Status,
    Gc { purge: Box<[SourceHash]> },

    // The start surface. PR C-01.
    RecentList,
    RecentAdd { path: Box<PathBuf> },

    // Jobs
    JobStatus { job: JobId },
    JobCancel { job: JobId },

    // Transport
    TransportPlay,
    TransportStop,
    TransportLocate { position: Position },
    TransportSetLoop { span: Option<Span> },
    TransportSetPunch { span: Option<Span> },
    TransportSetCountIn { bars: BarCount },
    TransportArmRecord,
    TransportDisarmRecord,
    TransportSetTempo { at: Position, tempo: Tempo },
    TransportCalibrate { device: DeviceKey },

    // Score edit. Every context-menu item maps to one `ScoreCommand`.
    ScoreApply(Box<ScoreCommand>),
    ScoreCopy(Box<Selection>),
    ScoreQuery(Box<ScoreSelector>),
    ScoreImportMidi(Box<ImportRequest>),
    ScoreImportMusicXml(Box<ImportRequest>),
    ScoreExportMusicXml(Box<ExportRequest>),

    // Take management
    TakeList { track: TrackId },
    TakeSelect { track: TrackId, take: TakeId },
    TakeRename(Box<RenameRequest>),
    TakeSplit { take: TakeId, at: Position },
    TakeTrim { region: RegionId, start: Delta, length: Delta },
    TakeComp(Box<CompRequest>),
    TakeSetRecordMode { track: TrackId, mode: RecordMode },
    TakeSetAlign { track: TrackId, align: AlignChoice },
    TakeDelete { take: TakeId },

    // Track lifecycle, input, monitor, and arm. PR R-02, R-04, R-05.
    TrackAdd(Box<TrackAddRequest>),
    TrackRename(Box<RenameRequest>),
    TrackReorder { track: TrackId, before: Option<TrackId> },
    TrackRemove { track: TrackId },
    TrackSetInput(Box<InputRequest>),
    TrackSetMonitor { track: TrackId, monitor: MonitorMode },
    TrackSetArmed { track: TrackId, armed: bool },

    // Mix
    MixSetParam { parameter: ParamId, value: Finite },
    MixSetMute { strip: StripId, mute: bool },
    MixSetSolo { strip: StripId, solo: bool },
    MixClearSolo,
    MixAddSend { from: StripId, to: StripId, tap: SendTap },
    MixAddBus(Box<BusAddRequest>),
    MixInsertSlot { strip: StripId, at: SlotPosition, kind: SlotKind },
    MixRemoveSlot { strip: StripId, slot: SlotId },
    MixWriteCurve(Box<CurveWrite>),
    /// Clear the held over mark. `None` clears every strip. PR M-05.
    MeterReset { strip: Option<StripId> },

    // Master. PR MA-03 needs a measure with progress and cancel.
    MasterMeasure(Box<MeasureRequest>),

    // View state. PR X-08 and C-03.
    ViewSet(Box<ViewState>),
    ViewGet,

    // History
    HistoryCommit(Box<CommitRequest>),
    HistoryLog { limit: u32 },
    HistoryBranch(Box<BranchRequest>),
    HistoryCheckout { commit: CommitId },
    HistoryDiff { from: CommitId, to: CommitId },

    // Session
    Undo,
    Redo,
    Save,
    ExportAudio(Box<AudioExportRequest>),
    Resynchronize,
}

/// Build a composite take from ranges across other takes. Contract 3.4
/// calls this comp mode, and PR R-09 makes it a MUST.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CompRequest {
    track: TrackId,
    /// The new take receives one region per range, in order.
    ranges: Vec<CompRange>,
    name: TakeName,
}

/// One range taken from one source take.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CompRange { from_take: TakeId, start: Position, end: Position }

/// One entry of the recent-project list. `duet-project` reads the file and
/// builds these; the payload type is declared here, because `VerbData`
/// carries it and `duet-project` sits above `duet-command` (VR3).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RecentEntry { path: PathBuf, name: String, opened_at: UnixSeconds }

/// What a verb produced.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum VerbOutcome {
    /// The verb changed state. The events carry the new version.
    Changed { version: Version, events: Vec<DomainEvent> },
    /// The verb answered a question.
    Data(Box<VerbData>),
    /// The verb started long work. Progress arrives as events, and
    /// `JobStatus` and `JobCancel` accept the identifier.
    Started { job: JobId },
}

/// How much a verb costs on the calling thread.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VerbCost { Immediate, Deferred }

impl Verb {
    /// Whether the verb fits B5 on the calling thread.
    pub fn cost(&self) -> VerbCost;

    /// Whether a user started this verb, which reserves a job slot (B36).
    pub fn is_user_started(&self) -> bool;
}

/// The one interface every client calls.
pub trait Gateway {
    /// Apply one verb.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `GatewayError` when the verb is refused or the state is wrong.
    fn call(&mut self, verb: Verb) -> Result<VerbOutcome, GatewayError>;
}
```

`MixAddBus` takes a `BusAddRequest` that carries a `BusRole`, so a reverb bus and a delay bus are one
verb with a role. `TransportArmRecord` carries no track list: it moves `RecordState` only, and
`TrackSetArmed` is the one writer of `Track::armed` (critic R16).

**Every capability is a verb.** ADR 0005 decision 1 states that a capability outside the list
falsifies the claim that the list is the whole interface. Three groups closed that gap in revision 5.

| Verb group | Story | Why a verb and not a view action |
|---|---|---|
| `RecentList`, `RecentAdd` | C-01 | `StartView` opens no file (section 1.3 rule 6). `duet-project` reads the user configuration directory and answers the verb. |
| `ProjectConvertRate` | Section 5.4 | The rate mismatch needs a user answer that an agent can also give. |
| `ViewSet`, `ViewGet` | X-08, C-03 | Layout, mode, zoom, scroll, and selection persist per project. |

There is no string-keyed escape hatch. Ardour offers `access_action(path)`, and Duet rejects it.
`clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm` is denied, so a new verb becomes a compile error at every place
that must handle it. A string key would turn that into a run-time failure.

`Verb::cost` splits the work, and section 9.6 gives the deferred half a thread.

### 9.2 The Model Context Protocol server

`duet-agent` is a transport adapter. It holds no vocabulary.

- **stdio.** `duet mcp` serves MCP over stdin and stdout with `rmcp` 3.4.0 on tokio. The `duet`
  binary never writes to stdout in this mode except through the transport.
- **Unix socket.** `duet serve` accepts on a Unix stream socket. `rmcp`'s `AsyncRwTransport` works
  over any type that implements `AsyncRead` and `AsyncWrite`, so `tokio::net::UnixStream` fits with
  no extra layer (survey).

The socket path is outside the bundle, because a socket must not reach the git index.

| Platform | Path |
|---|---|
| Linux | `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/duet/<project-hash>.sock` |
| macOS | `$TMPDIR/duet/<project-hash>.sock` |

`<project-hash>` is the lowercase hexadecimal BLAKE3 hash of the canonical bundle path. The
application writes the resolved path into `state/agent.sock.path`. The socket mode is B80.

**The client carries two timeouts**, B15 to connect and B16 for a reply, or B17 for `ExportAudio`
and `Gc`. A hung window process cannot hang an agent verb without bound.

Each MCP tool maps to exactly one `Verb`. The tool schema is generated from the `serde` derive, so
the two never drift.

### 9.3 Headless mode

`duet mcp --project <path>` and `duet serve --project <path>` open a bundle with the dummy backend
and never call `gpui_kit::application()`. GPUI is not initialized, no window opens, and
`crates/duet` links GPUI without starting it.

The same binary with no subcommand opens the window. One binary, one verb list, two transports
(PR 11 Q2).

`duet <verb>` with no server takes the writer lock, applies the verb to the files, and saves. It
exits with `ExitCode::SUCCESS`, or with one stderr line and a failure code.

### 9.4 The file watcher

`duet-project` starts `notify` with `notify-debouncer-full` on the thread that `notify` creates. The
debounced batch enters the structural channel as `CoreInput::FilesChanged`. It watches `score/`,
`session/`, `mix/`, `.git/HEAD`, and `.git/refs`. **It does not watch `state/view.json`.** That file
is untracked, this process is its one writer, and `Verb::ViewSet` is the one path that changes it
(section 10.2), so a watch would only see this process's own save.

Section 3.9 gives the reconciliation rule. Section 4.6 gives the `HEAD` rule.

### 9.5 How tokio and the GPUI executor coexist

Two runtimes live in one process under nine rules.

1. **GPUI owns the main thread.** tokio never runs on it. `gpui_kit::application().run` stays the
   outermost call in the window path.
2. **One owner holds the runtime.** `Entity<AgentBridge>` holds a `tokio::runtime::Runtime` and a
   `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken`.
3. **The worker count is B38, and it is explicit.** `Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2)`.
   The default is one worker per core, which oversubscribes the machine and adds jitter to the audio
   callback (critic 6.4, audit 10).
4. **TH7 binds here.** Section 5.7 states the rule and this rule states nothing of its own, which
   is what DR4 requires; revision 11 wrote the rule twice, once at each site (critic 9). The
   boundary for data is a channel.
5. **The seam is executor agnostic.** `async_channel` and `futures::channel::oneshot` work on both
   executors. The tokio task sends a `GatewayRequest`; a `cx.spawn` task on the GPUI side receives
   it, calls the gateway, and returns the result on the oneshot. TH6 holds: no tokio task holds an
   entity handle.
6. **Backpressure is the bound.** The request channel holds B35. A tokio task that finds it full
   suspends on `send().await`, so a runaway agent slows down instead of exhausting memory.
7. **One choke point runs the shutdown, on every exit path.** The choke point is
   `AgentBridge::shut_down`, and four callers reach it.
   - The `Quit` action handler.
   - `cx.on_app_quit`, which GPUI calls for a platform quit and for the last window close.
   - The `Drop` impl of `AgentBridge`, which calls it when it has not run.
   - A signal handler thread that `duet mcp` and `duet serve` install for `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`.

   `shut_down` is idempotent. It checks an `AtomicBool` and returns at once on a second call.

   **The `Drop` path absorbs every failure and never panics.** `shut_down` returns
   `Result<(), ShutdownError>`. The three explicit callers log an error and continue. The `Drop`
   impl calls it, discards the result through a `tracing::warn!`, and returns. A panic during an
   unwind would abort the process, so `Drop` has no `?`, no `unwrap`, and no `expect`.
8. **The nine steps, in this order. They cover the whole process and not the agent bridge alone**
   (critic C19-W23). Revision 19 stopped the tokio runtime and left the transport rolling, a take
   open, the stream open, and the job workers unjoined, so a quit during a record pass abandoned a
   take whose container header `TakeWriter` had never finished.
   1. Cancel the `CancellationToken`, so no new agent verb enters.
   2. Send `CoreInput::Shutdown`, then wait up to B23 for every in-flight verb to reply.
   3. **Stop the transport and finish any open take.** The core sends
      `TransportCommand::Stop`, waits on the B138 channel for `EngineEvent::CaptureDone` for every
      armed track inside **B131**, and commits each take. `duet_media::TakeWriter::finish` writes the container header,
      which is the one step that makes a partial take readable. **B131 is not B23** (critic C21I-2):
      B23 is 250 ms on a tokio reply channel, and this wait is on the structural channel behind a
      disk thread that must drain a full B53 capture ring and then pay one B118 flush, so one slow
      append alone would take 80 percent of B23. On expiry the core stops waiting, marks every
      unfinished take with `TakeFlag::HadOverrun`, and records `EngineFault::CaptureStalled`.
   4. **Close the stream.** The core sends `ConfigureCommand::Close` and waits B116 for
      `EngineEvent::StreamClosed`; on expiry it records `EngineFault::DeviceStalled` and goes on,
      because B116 is a report (step 8 states the cost).
   5. **Stop the job runner.** `JobRunner::shut_down` cancels every queued job and drops the
      queue sender, so each worker sees a closed channel and ends its loop. **Each worker sends
      `CoreInput::WorkerStopped` as its last act**, and the core waits **B132** for the set of B37
      workers to empty. A worker inside an export render answers the cancel at its next progress
      point (section 9.6). **The core measures it and nothing joins** (critic C21-2): revision 21
      bounded a `JoinHandle::join` behind a park on the GPUI foreground thread, which TH3 forbids
      and which the thread table refuses, and the core is waiting for a MESSAGE exactly as it is at
      steps 3 and 4. **B132 is not B23** (critic C21I-2): B23 bounds a reply and this bounds a
      worker loop, and no rule bounds the distance between two progress points, so the bound is on
      the WAIT and never on the work. On expiry the core stops waiting and the process exits with
      the workers abandoned; every deferred verb writes through `exports/.tmp/` or `state/.tmp/`
      and the next start empties both, so an abandoned worker leaves no partial file a user can
      open.
   6. **Save, on the `duet-quit-save` thread, inside B134** (critic C21-3). The core builds the
      byte form of every dirty document, which allocates and performs no file call, and it moves
      those bytes and the writer-lock handle onto one `std::thread` named `duet-quit-save`. That
      thread runs the atomic save of section 4.10, releases the writer lock, and sends
      `CoreInput::QuitSaveDone`. **The save is the one step of this path that writes files**, and
      section 4.10 names three FIXED `fsync` calls, one per temporary file, and one per touched
      directory TWICE, at step 2 and at step 4 (critic C22I-W14); an `fsync` on a network volume is
      the same unbounded wait B117 and B118 already grant the disk thread, and in the application
      the core runs on the GPUI foreground thread, so the save cannot run there. Revision 21 ran it
      on the core with no bound at all and then claimed the path was bounded. **The save cannot
      take a job worker**, because step 5 has already stopped them, which is why this step owns a
      thread of its own. **The save is the section 4.10 save and no other protocol** (critic
      C22I-W15): it writes each temporary file in the SAME directory as its final name, it records
      the set in `state/save.commit`, and the next start reads that marker and completes every
      rename whose temporary file still exists. Revision 22 wrote that the save ran through
      `state/.tmp/` and that the next start emptied that directory, which would delete the files
      the section 4.10 crash matrix needs; `state/.tmp/<job>/` is the section 9.6 job convention
      and not the save convention. On expiry the core stops waiting and the process exits with the
      save abandoned, and the crash matrix then answers exactly as it answers a power loss.
   7. Move the `Runtime` onto a detached `std::thread` and call `shutdown_timeout` with B24 there.
   8. **Send `ConfigureCommand::Reset`, then `ConfigureCommand::Stop`, then wait B119 for
      `EngineEvent::HandoffStopped`.** `Reset` is safe here and nowhere earlier, because step 4
      already had `EngineEvent::StreamClosed`, which means the audio thread has stopped and the
      last `GraphState` is dropped; the two sends are the order `ConfigureCommand::Stop` and
      `EngineEvent::StreamClosed` each state in their own doc comments, and revision 23 left that
      order with no step that performed it (critic C23I-W8). **Neither send carries a wait of its
      own**: both are one `try_send` on the B109 channel, and B119 bounds the one wait this step
      performs. The
      engine handoff thread runs `Collector::collect` and `Collector::try_cleanup`, sends that
      event on the B138 channel, drops its backend, and then ends. **The send is the half revision
      22 omitted** (critic C22I-3): no declared command ended the loop and no declared sender was
      dropped, so the thread never stopped, the wait always reached expiry, and every quit paid
      B119 in full while `try_cleanup` never ran. **The
      core measures it and nothing joins** (critic C21-2): revision 21 bounded a
      `JoinHandle::join` behind a park on the GPUI foreground thread, and the thread that is inside
      `AudioBackend::stop` cannot be interrupted by a park on another thread, so the join bought
      nothing and cost a frozen window. On expiry the core stops waiting and the process exits with
      the thread abandoned; `try_cleanup` does not run and the operating system reclaims every
      byte, so the B55 leak costs nothing at process exit (critic C20-4).
   9. Let GPUI quit. The main thread never blocks, and no drop runs inside an async context.
9. **An in-flight verb reply is best effort, and the agent contract says so.** A verb whose reply
   does not arrive inside B23 receives no reply at all, and the connection closes. The contract is
   explicit: **a verb that returned no reply may or may not have been applied, and the agent must
   call `Status` or `HistoryLog` to find out.** Every mutating verb is idempotent when it names an
   identifier, which is why `Verb` derives `PartialEq`.

**Headless uses the same seam.** With no GPUI, the core runs on a dedicated thread and reads the same
`async_channel`, so one code path serves both hosts. **The nine steps are the same nine**, and the
signal handler of rule 7 is the caller that reaches them.

**Every step of the nine has a bound of its OWN and a stated outcome**, which is what makes the
quit path a Responsive path and not a hope: B23 covers step 2, B131 covers step 3, B116 covers step
4, B132 covers step 5, **B134 covers step 6**, B24 covers step 7, and B119 covers step 8. **Steps 1
and 9 are the only two that perform no cross-boundary wait** (critic C21-3). Revision 21 wrote
"steps 1, 6 and 9" while step 6 ran the atomic save, which is the one step of this path that calls
`fsync`, so the sentence that claimed the path was bounded excluded the longest wait on it by
assertion. **No step waits without a bound, no two steps share a bound that was sized for one of
them, and no bound on this path is a join** (critic C21I-2, C21-2, C21-3). Revision 21 gave steps 2,
3 and 5 one 250 ms budget written for a tokio reply channel, and then gave steps 5 and 8 a blocking
`JoinHandle::join` behind a park on the thread that paints. **Every wait of this path is now a
message the CORE measures**, which is the shape B18, B116 and B131 already carried, and the thread
of each one is named at its own step and in its Appendix B.5 row.

### 9.6 How a deferred verb runs

**`duet-core` owns a `JobRunner`: B37 `std::thread` workers and a bounded queue.** tokio is not the
job runner; tokio serves the Model Context Protocol transport and nothing else.

```rust
/// The worker pool for every deferred verb.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct JobRunner {
    /// One handle per B37 worker.
    workers: Vec<JoinHandle<()>>,
    /// The bounded queue of B36. The reserved half is the tail.
    queue: Sender<JobId>,
    registry: Arc<JobRegistry>,
    /// The write end of the B28 core input channel.
    ///
    /// Each worker holds a clone and sends one `CoreInput::WorkerStopped` as
    /// its last act, which is what bounds B132 at step 5 of section 9.5 rule
    /// 8. Revision 22 stated that duty and declared no sender (critic
    /// C22I-2, TH13).
    core: CoreLink,
}

/// What a job reports while it runs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum JobState {
    Queued,
    Running { done: u32, total: u32 },
    Done,
    Cancelled,
    Failed(GatewayError),
}

/// One `JobRunner` worker's own state. B37 of them exist.
///
/// `queue` is a clone of the read end of the B36 job queue, which is what
/// `async_channel` allows and `triple_buffer` does not: many workers take
/// from one queue and each job goes to exactly one of them. When
/// `JobRunner::shut_down` drops the write end every clone sees a closed
/// channel, each worker sends one `CoreInput::WorkerStopped` on `core`, and
/// the B132 wait of section 9.5 step 5 ends on messages and not on expiry
/// (critic C22I-2, TH13).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct JobWorker {
    /// Which worker this is, as `CoreInput::WorkerStopped` names it.
    worker: u16,
    /// The read end of the B36 job queue.
    queue: CoreReceiver<JobId>,
    registry: Arc<JobRegistry>,
    /// The write end of the B28 core input channel.
    core: CoreLink,
}

/// The registry the core owns. `JobStatus` and `JobCancel` read and write it.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct JobRegistry {
    /// Every job this process run still holds a state for.
    ///
    /// **An entry LEAVES this map** (critic C19-W24). A worker that reaches a
    /// terminal `JobState`, which is `Done`, `Failed`, or `Cancelled`, emits
    /// the last `CoreEvent::JobProgress` and then removes its own entry from
    /// both maps. Revision 19 removed nothing, so both maps grew for the life
    /// of the process and B36 bounded the queue and neither map.
    ///
    /// **A terminal state stays readable for B127**, because `JobStatus` is a
    /// verb an agent calls after the fact. The removal is therefore deferred
    /// by that window: the core sweeps every entry whose terminal moment is
    /// older than B127 on each pass of its own input loop, which is a bounded
    /// walk of a map that B36 bounds. A `JobStatus` for an identifier the map
    /// no longer holds answers `GatewayError::UnknownJob`.
    states: Mutex<BTreeMap<JobId, JobState>>,
    /// One cancel flag per job. A worker reads it between units of work, and
    /// the same removal rule empties it.
    cancels: Mutex<BTreeMap<JobId, Arc<AtomicBool>>>,
    /// The next identifier this process run mints.
    next: AtomicU64,
}
```

- **The queue is B36, and part of it is reserved.** An agent verb sees the unreserved slots only, so
  a script that submits many exports can never refuse the user's next `Save`. A full queue returns
  `GatewayError::JobQueueFull`, and the message names which half is full.
- **Progress through the registry.** A worker writes `JobState::Running { done, total }`, and the
  core emits `CoreEvent::JobProgress`. `JobStatus` reads the same value.
- **Cancellation is a polled flag.** `JobCancel` sets an `AtomicBool` that the worker reads between
  units of work. There is no forced stop, so no job is interrupted mid-write.

**Which verbs are deferred**: `Gc`, `ExportAudio`, `MasterMeasure`, `TransportCalibrate`,
`ProjectConvertRate`, `ScoreImportMidi`, `ScoreImportMusicXml`, `ScoreExportMusicXml`,
`ProjectOpen`, `Save`, `HistoryCheckout`, `HistoryLog`, and the peak pyramid build. TH3 holds for
every one of them.

#### How a job reads core state without a lock

The threading contract has no lock. The rule is a snapshot hand-off in three steps.

1. **The core holds each document behind an `Arc`.** A snapshot is an `Arc::clone`, which is a
   pointer copy and which cannot miss B5. Revision 4 called the snapshot "a memory copy of small
   structures", and a 300-bar SATB score is not small (critic R11).
2. **An edit applied while a snapshot is outstanding calls `Arc::make_mut`.** That clones the
   document once, on the core thread. Every later edit costs nothing until the next snapshot. A
   criterion bench in `duet-core` measures that one clone on the B1 fixture against B5, and section
   5.12 lists it as a measured path.
3. **The worker runs against the snapshot.** It reads files and walks the git object graph freely,
   because it touches no core state. It returns a result value.

#### TH8: every deferred verb that writes re-validates

The core applies a worker's result on the core thread and re-checks it against the state as it
stands now. The rule covers every writing verb, not `Gc` alone.

| Verb | What the core re-checks before it commits |
|---|---|
| `Gc` | Every candidate hash against the live set as it stands now. A take recorded while the walk ran is therefore safe. |
| `Save` | The `Version` the worker serialized against the current `Version`. On a mismatch the core takes one new snapshot and runs the save again. A second mismatch inside B6 makes the core refuse with `GatewayError::SaveRaced`, and the user interface offers `Save again`. |
| `HistoryCheckout` | That `HEAD` has not moved since the snapshot. On a move the verb returns `GatewayError::HistoryUnresolved`. |
| `ScoreImportMidi`, `ScoreImportMusicXml` | That the target part and staff identifiers still exist. A missing one returns `ScoreError::MissingElement`. |
| `ProjectConvertRate` | That every source hash the worker converted is still in the live set. |

The `WriterLedger` records the hash of the bytes the save wrote, so a re-run never leaves a ledger
entry that names bytes the document no longer holds.

#### The cleanup contract for a cancelled job and a failed job

A cancel and a failure leave files behind unless someone deletes them (critic R12).

1. **Every job that writes owns a temporary directory**, which is `exports/.tmp/<job>/` for a render
   and `state/.tmp/<job>/` for any other writer.
2. **The worker deletes its own temporary directory and any partly written output file** before it
   sets `JobState::Cancelled` or `JobState::Failed`. The deletion runs in the worker's `Drop`, so a
   panic-free early return cannot skip it.
3. **A finished render is renamed into place as the last step.** A user therefore never finds a
   truncated `.wav` that looks like a finished render.
4. **The next start empties `exports/.tmp/` and `state/.tmp/`**, because no job survives a restart.
5. **The user sees one line.** After a cancel: `The export stopped. No file was written.` After a
   failure: `The export failed: <reason>. No file was written.`

`basedrop`'s collector runs on the engine handoff thread and nowhere else (TH5), so the audio thread
never calls `free` and an export render that holds a job thread for minutes cannot delay a drain.
Revision 19 wrote "also runs on a job thread" here against TH5's own "no deferred verb runs on that
thread", and the two sentences named two owners for one duty (critic C19-W14).
