```rust
    parts: BTreeMap<PartId, Part>,
    staves: BTreeMap<StaffId, Staff>,
    voices: BTreeMap<VoiceId, Voice>,
    measures: BTreeMap<MeasureId, Measure>,
    notes: BTreeMap<NoteId, Note>,
    rests: BTreeMap<NoteId, Rest>,
    spanners: BTreeMap<SpannerId, Spanner>,
    marks: BTreeMap<MarkId, ScoreMark>,
    tempo_map: TempoMap,
    revision: Revision,
    schema: SchemaVersion,
    /// Fields from a newer schema that this build does not model.
    extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

/// What a read-only score query asks for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ScoreSelector {
    Part(PartId),
    Staff(StaffId),
    Measures { from: MeasureId, count: NonZeroU16 },
    Range { staff: StaffId, from: Ticks, to: Ticks },
}

/// The byte blocks of one canonical score document, in `paths` order.
///
/// It derives serde, because `Snapshot` carries one across the transport and
/// the compile-time assertion of section 3.5 covers `Snapshot` (critic S4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CanonicalDocument { meta: Vec<u8>, notes: Vec<u8>, spanners: Vec<u8> }

/// Every way the score aggregate refuses.
///
/// It derives serde, because `GatewayError::Score` wraps it and every
/// refusal crosses the transport (section 15.5).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ScoreError {
    MissingElement(ElementRef),
    MissingPart(PartId),
    MissingStaff(StaffId),
    MissingMeasure(MeasureId),
    OverlappingNote { staff: StaffId, voice: VoiceId, onset: Ticks },
    TieAcrossPitch { from: NoteId, to: NoteId },
    MeasureNotEmpty(MeasureId),
    Schema { found: SchemaVersion, expected: SchemaVersion },
    Parse(Box<str>),
    Serialize(Box<str>),
    Time(TimeError),
}
```

```rust
pub enum MixError {

    /// The strip set would pass B86. `MixState::validate` returns it at read
    /// time, and `SessionCommand::BusAdd` returns it at edit time (R11).
    StripBudgetExceeded { requested: u32 },
    /// The parameter set would pass B90. `MixState::validate` returns it at
    /// read time, and `SessionCommand::StripInsertSlot` returns it at edit
    /// time (section 5.5, critic W1).
    ParamBudgetExceeded { requested: u32 },
    MissingStrip(StripId),
    MissingParam(ParamId),
    EmptyCurve(ParamId),
    DuplicatePoint { parameter: ParamId, at: Position },
    /// One strip's `pre_fader` or `post_fader` list would pass `MAX_SLOTS`.
    /// `MixState::validate` returns it at read time, and
    /// `SessionCommand::StripInsertSlot` returns it at edit time. **No other
    /// answer exists** (critic C21-6): `ChainTopology::pre_fader` is an
    /// `ArrayVec<SlotSpec, MAX_SLOTS>`, so `configure` cannot build a chain
    /// from a ninth slot, and truncation and silence are both wrong.
    SlotBudgetExceeded { strip: StripId, requested: u32 },
    /// One strip's `sends` list would pass `MAX_SENDS`, for the same reason
    /// (critic C21-6).
    SendBudgetExceeded { strip: StripId, requested: u32 },
    /// One curve's point list would pass B135. `Curve::new` returns it and
    /// `MixState::validate` returns it for a hand-edited `automation.jsonl`.
    /// A write-mode ride at frame rate is bounded by nothing else, and the
    /// list reaches both `automation.jsonl` and the B101 snapshot, so the
    /// growth crosses two boundaries that state a size (critic C21-W14)
    CurveBudgetExceeded { parameter: ParamId, requested: u32 },
}
```

### 15.5 `duet-command`

```rust
/// A git object digest.
///
/// **It is a digest and never a counter.** The bundle is a real git
/// repository (ADR 0003). Revision 8 left this name to a suffix template that
/// gave it a `u64`, which cannot hold one (critic R1).
///
/// **It carries the kind and up to thirty-two bytes.** A SHA-1 digest
/// occupies the first twenty bytes and the remaining twelve are zero; a
/// SHA-256 digest fills all thirty-two, and `kind` says which shape the
/// bytes hold. `History::object_format` supplies the kind: it returns
/// `HashKind::Sha1` when the repository is at format version 0, which is
/// every bundle this build creates, and it reads `extensions.objectFormat`
/// only at format version 1 (section 4.5, critic C-3). `duet.toml` mirrors
/// the value for a reader and decides nothing, and `ProjectOpen` refuses
/// anything but `HashKind::Sha1` with `ProjectError::ObjectFormat`.
///
/// **It is not named `ObjectId`.** `duet-project` depends on `gix`,
/// `gix::ObjectId` is the type its `History` implementation returns, and PL3
/// maps one name to one type in one crate. `duet-project` converts at its own
/// boundary, which is the same shape as the `MeterPoint` and `MeterTap`
/// precedent (critic W9).
///
/// It is declared here and not in `duet-project`, because `Verb` names
/// `CommitId` and VR3 puts every type `Verb` reaches in `duet-command` or
/// lower.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CommitDigest { kind: HashKind, bytes: [u8; 32] }

/// Which digest a repository's object format uses.
///
/// It carries the VR1 comparison set, because `CommitDigest` holds one and a
/// commit identifier is a `BTreeMap` and a `BTreeSet` key (VR1).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum HashKind { Sha1, Sha256 }

/// A commit identifier. It wraps a git object digest.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CommitId(CommitDigest);

/// A git branch name, without its `refs/heads/` prefix. It is never empty.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BranchName(Box<str>);

/// A job identifier. It is unique for one process run.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct JobId(u64);

/// A document version counter. Every core document carries one.
///
/// It derives an order and no `Hash`. The core compares a client's last
/// version with the current one to find a gap (section 5.8), and TH8 compares
/// two in the `Save` re-check (section 9.6). Nothing keys a map by it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Version(u64);

/// One line of the history list the user reads.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CommitSummary { id: CommitId, message: Box<str>, author: Box<str>, at: UnixSeconds, parents: Vec<CommitId> }

/// One unknown key a reader kept, with the path that carried it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ImportWarning { path: Box<str>, key: Box<str>, detail: Box<str> }

/// What a client asks the gateway for, across the transport seam.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct GatewayRequest { verb: Verb, client: u64 }

/// What the user interface reads about the transport, as plain data.
///
/// `duet_core::TransportReader` builds it from the audio thread's
/// `TransportSnapshot`, so `crates/duet` names no `duet-engine` type
/// (critic CR-4). Every field is a `duet-time` value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TransportView {
    position: SuperClock,
    rolling: bool,
    recording: bool,
    count_in_remaining: FrameCount,
    preroll_remaining: FrameCount,
}

impl TransportView {
    /// The transport stopped at the start.
    ///
    /// `TransportReader::latest` answers it before the first `poll`, and
    /// `PlayheadLayer::shown` starts from it, for the reason
    /// `MeterView::silent` exists (critic C-7).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn stopped() -> Self;
}

/// One transport intent.
///
/// It is declared here and not in `duet-engine`, because `DomainEvent`
/// carries it to every client and `duet-engine` depends on this crate, so an
/// intent declared there would be a Cargo cycle (critic S2). `Transport::apply`
/// reads it through the `duet-command` edge (section 5.9).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TransportCommand {
    Play, Stop, Locate(SuperClock), ArmRecord, DisarmRecord,
    SetLoop(Option<Span>), SetPunch(Option<Span>), SetCountIn(BarCount),
}

/// What a loudness measurement produced.
///
/// It is declared here and not in `duet-analysis`, because `VerbData` carries
/// it and VR3 binds. A `duet-command` edge to `duet-analysis` would instead
/// pull `ebur128` into the nine crates that depend on the vocabulary
/// (critic S2, S4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LoudnessReport { integrated_lufs: Finite, short_term_lufs: Finite, momentary_lufs: Finite, true_peak_dbtp: Finite, range_lu: Finite }

/// Which crate above `duet-command` refused.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum FailureSurface { Engine, Project, Interchange, Export }

/// A stable machine-readable code for one upstream failure.
///
/// `clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm` is denied, so a new code is a compile
/// error at the one site that turns a failure into a message (section 12.4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum FailureCode {
    NoServer, DeviceOpen, DeviceRate, Configuration, Transport,
    Io, Parse, Schema, NotFound, Limit, Format, Cancelled, Timeout,
}

/// One failure from a crate above `duet-command`, mirrored as plain data.
///
/// **It exists because a `GatewayError` arm cannot name an upper crate.**
/// `duet-engine`, `duet-project`, `duet-interchange`, and `duet-export` each
/// depend on `duet-command`, so an arm that wrapped one of their error enums
/// was blocker V1 reopened (critic S2). Each of the four implements
/// `From<Self::Error> for UpstreamFailure` at its own boundary, which the
/// orphan rule allows because the source type is local to that crate. The
/// causal chain survives as a surface, a code, and a detail string.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct UpstreamFailure { surface: FailureSurface, code: FailureCode, detail: Box<str> }

/// One fact a client reads about a domain change.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum DomainEvent { Score(ScoreEvent), Session(SessionEvent), Transport(TransportCommand), Job { job: JobId, state: JobState } }

/// A whole-state copy for a client that resynchronized.
///
/// **It carries the session and the mix.** Revision 9 carried the score, the
/// view, and the engine state, so a client that dropped events never
/// recovered its track list, its take list, its region list, or its strips;
/// the Record and Mix work areas then drew the state as it stood before the
/// gap, with no marker and no fault (critic W15). Each document travels in
/// the byte form `BundleDocument::to_bytes` already produces. B101 gives the
/// whole size at B1, and B30 holds one per client.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Snapshot {
    version: Version,
    score: Box<CanonicalDocument>,
    session: Box<SessionDocument>,
    mix: Box<MixDocument>,
    view: Box<ViewState>,
    engine: EngineState,
}

/// What a query verb answered.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum VerbData {
    Status { version: Version, takes: u32, engine: EngineState },
    Takes(Vec<TakeId>),
    Commits(Vec<CommitSummary>),
    Recents(Vec<RecentEntry>),
    View(Box<ViewState>),
    Job { job: JobId, state: JobState },
    Loudness(Box<LoudnessReport>),
    Clipboard(Box<Clipboard>),
}

/// What a client sends the core.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CoreInput {
    Call(Box<GatewayRequest>),
    FilesChanged(Vec<PathBuf>),
    SetEntryContext { caret: Position, duration: NoteValue },
    Resynchronize { client: u64 },
    Shutdown,
    /// One `JobRunner` worker saw its queue close and its loop has ended
    /// (critic C21-2). The core removes the worker from the set it still
    /// owes and stops the B132 wait when the set empties. **It is not a
    /// join**: a `JoinHandle::join` behind a bounded park on the GPUI
    /// foreground thread is the shape TH3 forbids.
    WorkerStopped { worker: u16 },
    /// The `duet-quit-save` thread finished the atomic save of section 4.10
    /// for every dirty document and released the writer lock (critic C21-3).
    /// `outcome` carries the refusal when a save failed, and the core records
    /// it before it lets the process exit. It bounds B134.
    QuitSaveDone { outcome: Result<(), Box<CommandError>> },
}

/// What the core sends a client.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CoreEvent {
    Changed { version: Version, events: Vec<DomainEvent> },
    JobProgress { job: JobId, state: JobState },
    EngineFault(EngineFault),
    EngineStateChanged(EngineState),
    ScoreChanged(Revision),
    PeaksReady(SourceHash),
    MissingSource { hash: SourceHash },
    DocumentReloaded { version: Version },
    ExternalEditRejected { path: PathBuf, error: Box<CommandError> },
    ExternalEditConflict { paths: Vec<PathBuf> },
    CheckoutRejected { commit: CommitId, error: Box<CommandError> },
    ViewStateReset { reason: Box<str> },
    UndoHorizonMoved { dropped: u32, oldest_name: Box<str> },
    EntryDropped { count: u32 },
    ClientDegraded { client: u64 },
    LockLost,
}

/// Create one project from a template.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CreateRequest {
    path: PathBuf,
    name: Box<str>,
    template: Box<str>,
    sample_rate: SampleRate,
    /// The first key of the score. The create form asks for it and revision
    /// 19 dropped all three of these fields (PR C-02, critic C19-W20).
    key: KeySignature,
    /// The first time signature of the score.
    meter: Meter,
    /// The first tempo of the score.
    tempo: Tempo,
}

/// Import one file into the open project.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ImportRequest { path: PathBuf, options: SmfImportOptions }

/// Export the score to one interchange file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ExportRequest { path: PathBuf, overwrite: bool }

/// Render the mix to one audio file.
///
/// **`part` is the per-part choice PR MA-05 asks for** (critic C21-W12).
/// `None` renders the whole mix to `path`. `Some(part)` renders that part
/// alone, and `RenderJob` writes one file per request, so the caller that
/// wants one file per part sends one request per part and the job state names
/// the part it renders now. Revision 21 mapped MA-05 to `ExportSpec`, whose
/// own doc comment states that the record "fully determines a render", and
/// declared no field that could express a part, so the gap was a
/// contradiction and not an omission.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioExportRequest { path: PathBuf, spec: ExportSpec, overwrite: bool, part: Option<PartId> }

/// Rename one named element.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RenameRequest { target: ElementRef, track: Option<TrackId>, take: Option<TakeId>, name: Box<str> }

/// Add one track to the session.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TrackAddRequest { part: PartId, staff: StaffId, name: TrackName, channels: NonZeroU8 }

/// Set one track's input.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct InputRequest { track: TrackId, input: InputSelection }

/// Add one bus to the mix.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BusAddRequest { name: StripName, role: BusRole }

/// Commit the tracked files.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CommitRequest { message: Box<str>, tag: Option<BranchName> }

/// Branch from one commit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BranchRequest { name: BranchName, from: CommitId, checkout: bool }

/// Measure the master output without writing a file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MeasureRequest { span: Option<Span>, normalization: Normalization }

/// Write one automation curve.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CurveWrite { parameter: ParamId, interpolation: Interpolation, points: CurvePoints }

/// Which Standard MIDI File track feeds which part.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PartMapping { entries: Vec<(u16, PartId)>, create_missing: bool }

/// What an import does with the file's tempo map.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TempoImport { Replace, Keep, Append }

/// Every way the vocabulary crate refuses a document.
///
/// It derives serde, because `GatewayError::Command` wraps it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum CommandError {
    Serialize(Box<str>),
    Parse(Box<str>),
    Schema { found: SchemaVersion, expected: SchemaVersion },
}

/// Every way the gateway refuses a verb.
///
/// **It derives serde, and every arm is plain data.** `JobState::Failed`
/// carries one, `DomainEvent::Job` and `VerbData::Job` both carry a
/// `JobState`, and the Model Context Protocol tool schema is generated from
/// the serde derive (section 9.2). Revision 9 gave the enum no serde chain at
/// all and the assertion of section 3.5 could not build (critic S4).
///
/// **No arm names a crate above `duet-command`.** `Upstream` carries the
/// plain-data mirror instead, and each upper crate converts its own error
/// with `From` at its own boundary (critic S2).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum GatewayError {
    NoProject,
    ProjectBusy { pid: u32 },
    RecordInProgress,
    HistoryUnresolved,
    SaveRaced,
    JobQueueFull { user_half: bool },
    PoolExhausted { kind: SlotKind },
    RingBudgetExceeded { requested_bytes: u64 },
    StripBudgetExceeded { requested: u32 },
    ParamBudgetExceeded { requested: u32 },
    BusRoleReserved(BusRole),
    NotYetImplemented,
    Score(ScoreError),
    Session(SessionError),
    Mix(MixError),
    Command(CommandError),
    Upstream(UpstreamFailure),
}
```

```rust
/// A stable identifier for one engraved system.

/// A size in pixels at the scale the engrave step was given.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct SizePx { width: f32, height: f32 }

/// One SMuFL symbol the font supplies.

pub enum Symbol { NoteheadBlack, NoteheadHalf, NoteheadWhole, Flag8Up, Flag8Down, ClefG, ClefF, ClefC, AccidentalSharp, AccidentalFlat, AccidentalNatural, RestQuarter, RestHalf, RestWhole, DynamicPiano, DynamicForte, ArticAccent, ArticStaccato, Fermata }

/// The SMuFL metadata this build read from the shipped font.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct FontMetrics { staff_space: f32, advances: BTreeMap<Symbol, f32>, anchors: BTreeMap<Symbol, (f32, f32)> }

/// What a caller asks the engraver for.

/// converted with `duet_time::convert::finite_to_f32_saturating`. B137 is the
```

```rust
pub struct UnmappedElements { entries: BTreeMap<Box<str>, Vec<Box<str>>> }

/// Every way an interchange read or write refuses.
```

### 15.8 `duet-analysis`

```rust
/// One pitch track over one source, at a fixed frame step.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PitchTrack { source: SourceHash, hop_frames: NonZeroU32, hz: Vec<Finite>, confidence: Vec<Finite> }
```

**B125 is the deviation at which a note is marked** (PR R-15, critic C19-W18, C21-W8). `duet-analysis`
compares each measured `hz` with the engraved note and reports every frame past B125, so the
threshold is one number in section 1.6 and never a literal at a draw site.

**B148 is the per-frame candidate count of the pYIN decode**, and it is the length of each of the
three state arrays that `duet_analysis::pyin::decode::decode_path` holds live across one iteration:
the candidate frequency, the running path cost, and the back pointer. Appendix B.1 names that count
as the one a reader checks in the body. `PitchTrack` holds the decoded result and never those
arrays, so a finished track is two `Vec<Finite>` values and never a matrix.

`PitchTrack` names the `SourceHash` it measured, so section 1.3 carries the edge
`duet-analysis` -> `duet-session`. `LoudnessReport` is a `duet-command` type (section 15.5):
`VerbData` carries it, so VR3 declares it there and this crate reads it through its
`duet-command` edge.

```rust
/// Every way a measurement refuses.
///
/// The expectation is the second of the two `variant_size_differences`
/// refusals in this plan (Appendix B.1). `Rate` carries one `SampleRate` and
/// `SourceRead` carries a fieldless enum, and the PG24 table prints both
/// sizes. The ratio test therefore refuses the difference between them, and
/// no shape that names a sample rate can satisfy it.
#[expect(
    variant_size_differences,
    reason = "the largest arm is the size the PG24 table prints for `SampleRate` and the next \
              is one arm tag, so the ratio test refuses every shape that names a sample rate"
)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub enum AnalysisError { TooShort, SourceRead(DspError), Rate(SampleRate) }
```

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]

}

/// Every way a media read or write refuses.
```

### 15.10 `duet-engine`

```rust
/// Which backend a stream runs on.
///
/// It derives `Eq`, because every arm carries nothing. It derives no `Hash`
/// and no order, because VR1 names no map, no set, and no sort over a backend
/// name (critic W16).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum BackendName { Dummy, Cpal }

/// A device handle the platform host gave us.
///
/// cpal names a device and does not number it, so this is a string newtype
/// and not a counter. `DeviceKey` is the stable digest that `session.json`
/// stores, and `DeviceLabel` is the name a user reads.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct DeviceId(Box<str>);

/// What the host reports about one device.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DeviceInfo { id: DeviceId, label: DeviceLabel, key: DeviceKey, inputs: u16, outputs: u16, default_rate: SampleRate }

/// The block sizes one device accepts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BlockSizeRange { min: FrameCount, max: FrameCount, fixed_only: bool }

/// What a caller asks the backend to open.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StreamRequest { device: DeviceId, rate: SampleRate, block: FrameCount, inputs: u16, outputs: u16 }

/// What the backend opened.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StreamInfo { device: DeviceId, rate: SampleRate, max_block: FrameCount, inputs: u16, outputs: u16, output_buffer: FrameCount }

/// The channel counts one chain agreed at configure time.
///
/// **`input` and `output` are a `ChannelCount` and not a `u16`** (section
/// 5.11, critic C19-8). A chain with no output channel produces nothing and
/// is a misconfiguration, so `configure_chain` refuses it with
/// `ConfigError::ChannelMismatch` off the audio thread, and the audio thread
/// then takes its chunk size from a number that has no zero. `sends` stays a
/// `u16`, because a chain with no send is an ordinary chain and no slice is
/// chunked by it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ChannelConfig { input: ChannelCount, output: ChannelCount, sends: u16 }

/// One send as the runtime reads it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SendSpec { id: SendId, target: NodeIndex, level: ParamId, tap: SendTap }

/// A node index into the published topological order.
///
/// It derives `Eq`, because a `u16` supplies it. The order is a
/// `Box<[NodeIndex]>` that `configure` computes off the audio thread, so
/// nothing sorts or hashes an index (critic W16).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NodeIndex(u16);

/// A request from the audio thread for more playback frames.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RefillRequest { track: TrackId, channel: ChannelIndex, from: SampleClock, frames: FrameCount }

/// The disk reader's per-track playback path.
///
/// **Every ring end sits inside a `basedrop::Owned`, and that is a rule and
/// not a style** (critic CR-16). An `rtrb` end owns a heap allocation, the
/// audio thread owns this value for the life of its chain, and a drop of a
/// bare end on that thread would be a free that TH1 forbids. `Owned` moves
/// the free to the collector thread (TH5), so the free half is a property of
/// the type rather than a line in a block that a reader must trust. PG26
/// refuses a bare end inside any audio-owned declaration. The cost is one
/// extra indirection per ring, paid once per block of B7 frames and not per
/// sample.
///
/// It writes `Debug` by hand for the reason `PoolHandle` states (section
/// 5.5): `basedrop` 0.1.3 implements `Debug` for neither `Owned<T>` nor
/// `Shared<T>`, and `missing_debug_implementations` is denied. **`Owned<T>`
/// does implement `DerefMut`** (`basedrop-0.1.3/src/owned.rs`), which
/// `Consumer::pop` and `Producer::push` each need, and `Shared<T>` implements
/// `Deref` alone. Both answers are measured facts now, so no chunk may delete
/// a wrapper.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
pub struct DiskReader {
    track: TrackId,
    channels: ChannelIndex,
    /// The playback ring, channel major, B53 long per channel.
    samples: Owned<Consumer<f32>>,
    position: SampleClock,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for DiskReader {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("DiskReader").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The disk writer's per-track capture path. It follows the `DiskReader`
/// rule: the ring end sits inside a `basedrop::Owned` and the `Debug` impl is
/// written by hand.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
pub struct DiskWriter {
    track: TrackId,
    take: TakeId,
    channels: ChannelIndex,
    /// The capture ring, channel major, B53 long per channel.
    samples: Owned<Producer<f32>>,
    written_frames: u64,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for DiskWriter {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("DiskWriter").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The write end of the engine-to-core event channel at B138.
///
/// `async_channel::Sender` is `Clone`, so the engine handoff thread and the
/// engine disk thread each hold one and `duet-core` owns the one read end
/// (section 5.8). This newtype is the ONE declaration of that end, so TH13
/// reads one field for every engine report rather than one per thread.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct EngineLink { events: Sender<EngineEvent> }

/// The engine disk thread's own state, and the ROOT of that thread.
///
/// Revision 22 gave this thread four duties and declared no value it holds:
/// section 5.10 made it the reader of the published `PlaybackPlan`, section
/// 5.8 made it the consumer of the B33 refill ring, section 6.4 made it the
/// reporter of one `CaptureInfo` per armed track, and the thread table made
/// it the owner of every take file (critic C22I-2, C22I-4). Each duty needed
/// a field and none existed.
///
/// **It is not audio-owned.** This thread allocates, it opens files, and it
/// blocks on `fsync`, which is why B117 and B118 bound its two file calls and
/// why the ring ends it holds carry no `basedrop` wrapper: a free on this
/// thread is legal and a free on the audio thread is not (TH1, TH4).
pub struct EngineDisk {
    /// The read end of the published playback plan (section 5.8, 5.10).
    plan: Output<PlaybackPlan>,
    /// One record per armed track, at B146.
    ///
    /// **This is where the `CaptureInfo` of a pass is built** (critic
    /// C23I-2). Revision 23 declared the SENDER of that message and none of
    /// the values it is built from, so the declared producer could not
    /// produce one and the thread the table calls the owner of every take
    /// file held no file at all.
    takes: ArrayVec<DiskTake, MAX_DISK_TRACKS>,
    /// One record per playing track, at B146.
    sources: ArrayVec<DiskSource, MAX_DISK_TRACKS>,
    /// The single consumer of the B33 refill ring from the audio thread.
    requests: Consumer<RefillRequest>,
    /// The disk half of every playback ring, at B140.
    fills: ArrayVec<Producer<f32>, MAX_DISK_RINGS>,
    /// The disk half of every capture ring, at B140.
    drains: ArrayVec<Consumer<f32>, MAX_DISK_RINGS>,
    /// The write end of the B138 engine event channel. Every `CaptureInfo`
    /// this thread reports travels on it (section 6.6).
    events: EngineLink,
    /// Every event `try_send` refused, at B147. This thread retries them at
    /// the head of its next pass, exactly as `GraphConfigurator` does.
    ///
    /// **It is a LIST and not one slot** (critic C23I-W5). This thread sends
    /// one `CaptureInfo` per armed track at the end of a pass, so one slot
    /// would drop every report but the first, the core's owed set would never
    /// empty, and B131 would reach expiry and mark a finished take with
    /// `TakeFlag::HadOverrun`, which is a false fact about it.
    pending_events: ArrayVec<EngineEvent, MAX_PENDING_EVENTS>,
}

/// The engine disk thread's record for ONE armed track.
///
/// It exists for the reason `GraphConfigurator::backend` exists: section 5.10
/// gives this thread a take file, a peak file and a per-pass count, and
/// revision 23 declared no value that holds any of the three (critic C23I-2).
pub struct DiskTake {
    track: TrackId,
    /// The take file this pass appends to. B118 bounds one append and its
    /// flush, and `TakeWriter::finish` writes the container header, which is
    /// the step that makes a partial take readable (section 9.5 step 3).
    writer: TakeWriter,
    /// The peak pyramid this pass builds beside the take (section 5.10).
    peaks: PyramidBuilder,
    /// What this pass has recorded so far. It becomes the one `CaptureInfo`
    /// this thread sends when the pass ends (section 6.6).
    info: CaptureInfo,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for DiskTake {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("DiskTake").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The engine disk thread's record for ONE playing track.
pub struct DiskSource {
    track: TrackId,
    /// The source file the refill path reads. B117 bounds one block read.
    reader: SourceReader,
    /// Where the last refill of this track ended.
    position: SampleClock,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for DiskSource {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("DiskSource").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for EngineDisk {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("EngineDisk").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The INPUT callback's end of the cpal input-to-output sample ring
/// (section 5.4, section 5.8).
///
/// cpal gives macOS and Linux two callbacks and never one duplex callback, so
/// the input callback writes each channel into a ring and the output callback
/// reads the same ring in the same cycle. Revision 22 named that boundary in
/// the section 5.8 sample table and declared neither end (critic C22I-2,
/// TH13). **The two ends are two TYPES, one per callback** (critic C23I-W4):
/// `cpal::Device::build_input_stream` and `build_output_stream` each take
/// their own `FnMut` closure and each closure owns what it captures, and an
/// `rtrb` end is `Send` and not `Sync`, so one value cannot sit in both.
/// Revision 23 declared one type with both ends and gave it two owners.
/// **One of each exists per input channel**, which is the count the section
/// 5.8 row states. Both callbacks are real-time callbacks the backend owns
/// and TH1 binds each word for word, so every end sits inside a
/// `basedrop::Owned` and the free happens on the collector thread (TH5).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
pub struct CpalInput {
    /// Which input channel this end carries.
    channel: ChannelIndex,
    /// The input callback's half of the ring.
    write: Owned<Producer<f32>>,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for CpalInput {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("CpalInput").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The output callback's half of the same ring (section 5.4, section 5.8).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
pub struct CpalOutput {
    /// Which input channel this end carries.
    channel: ChannelIndex,
    /// The output callback's half of the ring.
    read: Owned<Consumer<f32>>,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for CpalOutput {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("CpalOutput").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The note numbers sounding on one `PortSlot`.
///
/// It is a fixed-size bitset over the 128 MIDI note numbers, which the VR1
/// row for `MidiNote` states and which section 8.2 step 1 reads. Two `u64`
/// words cover 128 bits, so the silence pass of a departed port is two stores
/// and no search (critic C22I-7).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct SoundingNotes { bits: [u64; 2] }

/// Every parameter value the audio thread reads, addressed by `ParamId`.
///
/// It is fixed size: the core writes it and the core drops it, and the audio
/// thread only reads it, so TH9 does not bind this path. At B90 the array is
/// past the VR5 size bound, which the PG24 table prints for `ParamSnapshot`;
/// VR5 states why a type that must be `Copy` may be larger, and this is one
/// of the two sites it names (critic C5).
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ParamSnapshot { values: [Finite; MAX_PARAMS], generation: Generation }

/// One fact the engine reports on the structural channel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EngineEvent {
    Fault(EngineFault),
    StateChanged(EngineState),
    Latency(LatencyReport),
    Drift(DriftReport),
    CaptureDone(CaptureInfo),
    /// The engine handoff thread pushed a handoff and published its
    /// topology. The core clears `pending_configure` and re-sends whatever
    /// waits there (section 5.5).
    GraphConfigured { generation: Generation },
    /// `configure` refused. The core keeps the cause and section 12.4 gives
    /// the user a message.
    ConfigureRefused(ConfigError),
    /// `AudioBackend::stop` returned and the last `GraphState` is dropped,
    /// so the audio thread has stopped (section 5.5, critic C19-7).
    ///
    /// **The core waits for it before it sends `ConfigureCommand::Reset`**,
    /// which is the order that makes an empty layout agree with an empty
    /// array. `outcome` carries the refusal when `stop` failed or B116
    /// expired, and the core moves the engine to `EngineState::Faulted` on
    /// either, because a device that will not stop is a device the user must
    /// be told about.
    StreamClosed { outcome: Result<(), BackendError> },
    /// The engine handoff thread ran its last `Collector::collect` and its
    /// `Collector::try_cleanup` and its loop has ended (critic C21-2).
    ///
    /// **It is the message that bounds B119**, and it exists because the
    /// alternative is a `JoinHandle::join` behind a bounded park on the GPUI
    /// foreground thread, which TH3 forbids and which the thread table
    /// refuses. The core is waiting for a MESSAGE, so the core can measure,
    /// which is the shape B18, B116 and B131 already use.
    HandoffStopped,
}

/// Every way a device refuses.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub enum BackendError {
    Enumerate(Box<str>),
    NoServer(ServerDetail),
    Open(Box<str>),
    OpenTimeout(DeviceId),
    RateUnavailable { project: SampleRate, device: SampleRate },
    Start(Box<str>),
    Stop(Box<str>),
    NotOpen,
    CalibrationInvalid,
}

/// Every way `configure` refuses, before audio flows.
///
/// It derives `Copy`. The PG24 table prints its size, which is below the VR5
/// size bound, and every arm is `Copy` because `MixError` is. Revision 10
/// refused the derive with a reason that stated a size no guard measured and
/// named the third VR5 refusal; both were false, and Appendix B.1 carried a
/// suppression the rule did not sanction (critic C-4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub enum ConfigError {
    ChannelMismatch { stage: SlotId, produced: u16, accepted: u16 },
    PoolExhausted { kind: SlotKind },
    RingBudgetExceeded { requested_bytes: u64 },
    StripBudgetExceeded { requested: u32 },
    /// The parameter set would pass B90 (section 5.5).
    ParamBudgetExceeded { requested: u32 },
    /// The B105 handoff ring is full at the B95 attempt, so the audio thread
    /// has not adopted the array the last `configure` built.
    ///
    /// **The retry runs on the engine handoff thread**, which paints nothing:
    /// `GraphConfigurator` keeps the built `Configured` in `handoff_retry`
    /// and tries again on the next pass of its own loop, one attempt per
    /// B108, which is the period the loop's bounded receive sets.
    /// No wait of any kind sits on the GPUI foreground thread, and revision
    /// 14 left this comment stating the opposite (section 5.5, critic CR-15,
    /// CR-19, WR-21). Nothing retries while the engine is stopped, because no
    /// cycle drains the ring. Past B95 the engine becomes `Faulted` and
    /// section 12.4 gives the user a message.
    PoolHandoffBusy,
    /// A second `ConfigureCommand::Apply` arrived while `handoff_retry` was
    /// already `Some`. One attempt is in flight at a time, so the core keeps
    /// the request in `pending_configure` and re-sends it when the handoff
    /// thread reports the pending one resolved (section 5.5, critic WR-27).
    HandoffRetryPending,
    /// `hand_off` was called and `handoff_retry` was `None`, so no caller had
    /// built anything to push.
    ///
    /// **The loop never produces it**, because the loop calls `hand_off`
    /// only on the pass that filled `handoff_retry`. It is declared because
    /// the `# Errors` section of `hand_off` states it, and a `# Errors`
    /// contract that names an arm the type does not hold cannot be matched
    /// (critic C16-3). Revision 16 stated the arm in prose at three sites and
    /// declared it at none.
    NothingToHandOff,
    /// The mix document itself refused first. `From<MixError>` bridges it,
    /// so `configure` keeps the cause and `duet-session` names no engine
    /// type (R11, PL1).
    Mix(MixError),
}

/// Carry an engine refusal to a gateway caller with no second vocabulary.
///
/// **One failure set reaches a client** (critic C16-16, C17-4). `ConfigError`
/// and `GatewayError` each declare `PoolExhausted`, `RingBudgetExceeded`,
/// `StripBudgetExceeded`, and `ParamBudgetExceeded` with the same payloads,
/// and revision 17 declared no conversion between them, so a caller that held
/// one had to write a second match over the same four failures. ADR 0004
/// clause 12a asserted that no second variant existed while four did.
///
/// **The four shared arms map one for one.** `PoolHandoffBusy`,
/// `HandoffRetryPending`, and `NothingToHandOff` never reach a client:
/// section 5.5 states that the loop produces none of the three, and section
/// 12.4 gives each one no user message. `ChannelMismatch` and `Mix` map
/// through `GatewayError::Mix`, which already carries a `MixError`.
/// **A gateway caller sees a `GatewayError` and never a `ConfigError`**, and
/// section 12.4's refusal table is the one table it matches on.
///
/// **The impl lives in `duet-engine`, not in `duet-command`.** Rust's orphan
/// rule allows `impl From<Local> for Foreign`, and section 1.3 gives
/// `duet-command` no edge to `duet-engine`, so `duet-command` cannot name
/// `ConfigError` at all. The `impl-sites` row carries `in duet-engine` and the
/// roster compiles it there; that row is the one source of the placement.
impl From<ConfigError> for GatewayError {
    fn from(error: ConfigError) -> Self {
        match error {
            ConfigError::PoolExhausted { kind } => Self::PoolExhausted { kind },
            ConfigError::RingBudgetExceeded { requested_bytes } => {
                Self::RingBudgetExceeded { requested_bytes }
            }
            ConfigError::StripBudgetExceeded { requested } => {
                Self::StripBudgetExceeded { requested }
            }
            ConfigError::ParamBudgetExceeded { requested } => {
                Self::ParamBudgetExceeded { requested }
            }
            ConfigError::Mix(cause) => Self::Mix(cause),
            ConfigError::ChannelMismatch { .. }
            | ConfigError::PoolHandoffBusy
            | ConfigError::HandoffRetryPending
            | ConfigError::NothingToHandOff => Self::Upstream(UpstreamFailure {
                surface: FailureSurface::Engine,
                code: FailureCode::Configuration,
                detail: Box::from("the engine refused a graph configure"),
            }),
        }
    }
}

/// Every way the transport machine refuses.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub enum TransportError { PunchAndLoop, LocateOutOfRange(SuperClock), RecordWhileStopped }

/// The B34 fault queue and its drop counter, as one shared allocation.
///
/// Section 5.8 decides the primitive and section 12.4 states the path. The
/// queue has TWO producers, the audio callback and the cpal error callback
/// (TH11), so it is a `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue` and not an `rtrb` ring:
/// an `rtrb::Producer` is one value and it is not `Sync`.
///
/// `push` refuses the NEWEST record on a full queue and the producer adds one
/// to `dropped` with a relaxed fetch-and-add, which allocates nothing and
/// locks nothing. The engine handoff thread drains the queue, swaps `dropped`
/// to zero, and mints `EngineFault::FaultsDropped` when the swap returns a
/// value above zero.
///
/// It is allocated once, when the stream opens, off the audio thread, and it
/// is never resized, which is why it is a reachable LEAF and not an
/// audio-owned root: the rule that matters below it is the one the
/// `basedrop::Shared` above it already carries (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct FaultQueue { queue: ArrayQueue<EngineFault>, dropped: AtomicU32 }

/// The one `GraphRunner` of version one: one topological pass on the audio
/// thread (section 5.6).
///
/// It holds no state. The state is `GraphState`, which `run` takes as an
/// exclusive reference, so the runner is a unit struct and `EngineProcess`
/// names a type rather than a `Box<dyn GraphRunner>`, which would be a heap
/// handle on the audio thread.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct ChainRunner;

impl GraphRunner for ChainRunner {
    fn run(&mut self, topology: &GraphChain, state: &mut GraphState, cycle: &mut Cycle<'_>)
        -> CycleOutcome;
}

/// One span of one source on the timeline, as the DISK thread reads it.
///
/// **This is the value that answers "which file" and "where inside it"**
/// (critic C21I-1). Revision 21 declared a `RefillRequest` that named a track
/// and a device position and no source at all, so the disk thread was asked
/// to open a file no declaration named, and sections 6.1 and 6.2 described a
/// take model with no consumer.
///
/// It is FLAT: the core has already applied the layer order, the `opaque`
/// rule, and the record mode of section 6.2, so a span never overlaps another
/// span of the same track and the reader needs no decision. It is `Copy` and
/// fixed size, so a plan allocates once, off the disk thread.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PlaybackSpan {
    source: SourceHash,
    /// The first timeline frame this span covers.
    at: SampleClock,
    /// The first frame inside the source.
    offset: u64,
    frames: FrameCount,
    /// The region gain, already combined with the take gain.
    gain: Finite,
    /// The fade lengths in frames. The disk reader applies both before the
    /// ring, which is why no chain stage carries a region envelope.
    fade_in: FrameCount,
    fade_out: FrameCount,
}

/// Every span one track plays, in timeline order.
///
/// B128 bounds the length. A track past it is refused when the plan is built,
/// off every real-time thread, with `SessionError::PlaybackTooDense`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TrackPlayback { track: TrackId, spans: Box<[PlaybackSpan]> }

/// The whole playable set, as the disk thread reads it.
///
/// **The core builds it on a job thread and publishes it** (section 5.8).
/// `triple_buffer` carries it, so the core is the dropper and the disk thread
/// borrows, which is the same rule section 5.8 states for every publication.
/// B129 bounds the total span count and B130 bounds the build.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PlaybackPlan { generation: Generation, tracks: Box<[TrackPlayback]> }

/// The real-time body the backend owns, and the ROOT of the audio thread.
///
/// `AudioBackend::open` takes a `Box<dyn AudioProcess>` and moves it into the
/// backend's own callback state, so this value is the one the audio thread
/// holds for the life of the stream and `GraphState` is one of its fields.
/// Revision 20 declared no implementor of `AudioProcess` at all and rooted
/// every audio rule at `GraphState`, so six heap-owning handles sat above the
/// root with no declaration to read (critic C20-3).
///
/// **Every heap handle here sits inside a `basedrop` wrapper**, which is the
/// rule `DiskReader` states and not a style: a `triple_buffer::Output`, an
/// `rtrb` end, and a `crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue` each own a heap
/// allocation, and a drop of a bare one on this thread is a free TH1 forbids.
/// The audio thread builds none of them and drops none of them: the engine
/// handoff thread builds this value before `open`, and the backend drops it
/// when `stop` returns (section 5.5).
///
/// It writes `Debug` by hand for the reason `DiskReader` states: `basedrop`
/// 0.1.3 implements `Debug` for neither `Owned<T>` nor `Shared<T>`, and
/// `missing_debug_implementations` is denied.
/// **Audio-owned** (section 5.7).
pub struct EngineProcess {
    /// The runner's own mutable state, which section 5.6 declares.
    graph: GraphState,
    /// The published topology. `process` resolves it once per cycle and hands
    /// `GraphRunner::run` a shared reference (section 5.6).
    topology: Owned<Output<GraphChain>>,
    /// The published tempo map (section 2.11). It is read and never written
    /// here, which is what lets a `Vec` sit below it (section 5.6).
    tempo: Owned<Output<TempoMap>>,
    /// The published parameter set, read once per cycle (section 5.8).
    params: Owned<Output<ParamSnapshot>>,
    /// The single consumer of the B32 MIDI ring (section 5.8, section 8.3).
    midi: Owned<Consumer<MidiRecord>>,
    /// The single producer of the B33 refill ring to the disk thread.
    refills: Owned<Producer<RefillRequest>>,
    /// The B34 fault queue, shared with the cpal error callback that also
    /// pushes and with the engine handoff thread that drains (section 12.4).
    faults: Shared<FaultQueue>,
    /// The transport this cycle advances (section 5.9).
    transport: Transport,
    /// The write end of the transport publication (section 5.8).
    ///
    /// **The three write ends below are the audio thread's half of the
    /// publication seam** (critic C22I-2). Revision 22 declared the three
    /// read ends on `MeterReader` and `TransportReader`, named the audio
    /// thread as the writer in the `snapshot-table` block, and declared no
    /// write end at all, so TH9 bound a field that did not exist. Each one
    /// sits inside a `basedrop::Owned` for the reason this declaration's own
    /// doc states: a `triple_buffer::Input` owns a heap allocation and a drop
    /// of a bare one on this thread is a free TH1 forbids.
    transport_out: Owned<Input<TransportSnapshot>>,
    /// The write end of the meter publication (section 7.3).
    meters: Owned<Input<MeterSnapshot>>,
    /// The write end of the per-slot meter publication (section 7.3).
    slot_meters: Owned<Input<SlotMeterSnapshot>>,
    /// The notes sounding on each bound port, at B139.
    ///
    /// Section 8.2 step 1 silences them within one cycle when a port leaves,
    /// and the departure arrives as `MidiMessage::PortGone` on the B32 ring,
    /// which already orders every MIDI fact by `SampleClock` (critic
    /// C22I-7).
    sounding: [SoundingNotes; MAX_BOUND_PORTS],
    /// The one `GraphRunner` implementation of version one.
    runner: ChainRunner,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for EngineProcess {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("EngineProcess").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl AudioProcess for EngineProcess {
    fn process(&mut self, cycle: &mut Cycle<'_>) -> CycleOutcome;
}

/// Every way the engine refuses at run time. It wraps the other three.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub enum EngineError { Backend(BackendError), Config(ConfigError), Transport(TransportError), Media(MediaError), Dsp(DspError) }
```

### 15.11 `duet-midi`

```rust
/// Where a parsed MIDI message goes. The byte path owns one.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MidiSink {
    port: PortSlot,
    /// The note-entry queue to the core, bounded by B31. It must drop the
    /// OLDEST record on a full queue, which `ArrayQueue::force_push` does and
    /// an `rtrb` producer cannot (section 5.8, critic WR-11). `duet-core`
    /// holds the other handle.
    notes: Arc<ArrayQueue<NoteEntry>>,
    /// The record ring to the audio thread, bounded by B32. `rtrb` evicts
    /// nothing, so a full ring drops the newest record.
    records: Producer<MidiRecord>,
    /// Every record either path dropped. `duet-core` holds the other handle
    /// and reads it once per frame (section 8.3).
    dropped: Arc<AtomicU32>,
}

/// Where a raw platform port goes. The presence source owns one, and it
/// pushes into the B87 queue that the MIDI thread drains (section 8.1).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct HotplugSink {
    /// It must keep the NEWEST port on a full queue, which `force_push`
    /// gives and an `rtrb` producer does not (section 5.8, critic WR-11).
    ports: Arc<ArrayQueue<PlatformPort>>,
    /// Set when a push evicted, so the MIDI thread rescans the whole set.
    /// The MIDI thread reads it, so both threads hold a handle.
    resync: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

/// A live hot-plug subscription. Dropping it stops the notification.
///
/// The platform listener keys its registration by `token`, so `Drop` needs
/// the token and nothing else. Section 8.1 names the listener per platform.
///
/// **It carries no `missing_copy_implementations` expectation, and the
/// section 1.9 Drop block says why.** A type with a hand-written `Drop` impl
/// cannot implement `Copy`, so the lint never fires on it, and
/// `-D warnings` turns an expectation that cannot be fulfilled into a build
/// error. Revision 12 carried that expectation and a compiler run refuses it
/// (critic WR-12).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct HotplugSubscription {
    token: u64,
}

/// A live MIDI input. Dropping it closes the port.
///
/// The platform connection lives in the MIDI thread's own map, keyed by
/// `port`, so the handle carries the two identities and nothing else. It
/// writes a `Drop` impl, so the section 1.9 Drop block names it and no
/// expectation applies.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MidiInputHandle {
    port: PortSlot,
    id: MidiPortId,
}

/// A live MIDI output. Dropping it closes the port, through the `Drop` impl
/// the section 1.9 Drop block names.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MidiOutputHandle {
    port: PortSlot,
    id: MidiPortId,
}

/// One fact the MIDI crate reports to the core.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum MidiEvent {
    InputBound(MidiPortInfo),
    BindFailed { port: MidiPortInfo, reason: Box<str> },
    /// A bound input left. Section 8.2 states the four steps.
    InputLost(MidiPortInfo),
    PortsChanged { present: u16 },
}

/// Every way the MIDI crate refuses.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub enum MidiError {
    Enumerate(Box<str>),
    Hotplug(Box<str>),
    Open(Box<str>),
    OpenTimeout(MidiPortId),
    Unresolved { port: MidiPortId },
    PortSlotsExhausted,
}
```

```rust
/// One file the history tracks, as its bundle-relative path and its bytes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TrackedFile { path: Box<str>, bytes: Vec<u8> }

/// The tracked files of one commit, read into memory.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TreeSnapshot { commit: CommitId, files: Vec<TrackedFile> }

/// Where `HEAD` points now.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HeadState { Branch { name: BranchName, commit: CommitId }, Detached(CommitId), Unborn }

/// The content hash of every file the project writer last wrote.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct WriterLedger { entries: BTreeMap<Box<str>, [u8; 32]> }

/// The recent-project list, read from the user configuration directory.
///
/// **B142 bounds it and `Verb::RecentAdd` drops the OLDEST entry past that
/// count** (critic C22I-W18). Revision 22 declared an unbounded `Vec` that
/// one agent verb appends to, against this design's own rule that every
/// collection carries a bound, a budget row and a refusal, so a script that
/// called `RecentAdd` in a loop grew the vector and `state/recent.json`
/// without a limit. The list stays a `Vec` and not an `ArrayVec`, for the
/// reason `Strip` states: the file a user or an agent may have edited must
/// PARSE before the reader can trim it, and a fixed capacity would make the
/// parse fail where the design wants a repair.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
```

### 15.14 `duet-core`

```rust
/// The one writer of project state. Section 5.7 gives it the core thread.
///
/// Each document sits behind an `Arc`, so a client reads a snapshot with no
/// lock and the core replaces the whole value with `Arc::make_mut`
/// (Appendix A).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DuetCore {
    score: Arc<Score>,
    session: Arc<Session>,
    mix: Arc<MixState>,
    view: Arc<ViewState>,
    version: Version,
    undo: UndoStack,
    jobs: JobRunner,
    engine: EngineState,
    /// The shared meter-reset generations. `GraphState` holds the other
    /// handle and `MeterReader` holds a third (section 7.3).
    resets: Arc<ResetGenerations>,
    /// The note-entry queue the MIDI thread fills, drained once per frame
    /// (section 8.3). `MidiSink` holds the other handle.
    notes: Arc<ArrayQueue<NoteEntry>>,
    /// The hot-plug queue at B100, drained in the same callback (section 8.2).
    hotplug: Arc<ArrayQueue<HotplugEvent>>,
    /// Every note record the MIDI thread dropped, read in the same drain and
    /// reported as `CoreEvent::EntryDropped { count }`.
    entry_dropped: Arc<AtomicU32>,
    /// The topology change the engine handoff thread has not taken yet, or
    /// `None`. It covers one case: a full B109 channel.
    ///
    /// **Latest wins, and the one re-send trigger is
    /// `EngineEvent::GraphConfigured`.** The core makes one `try_send` on
    /// that event and clears the field when the send succeeds. **On
    /// `EngineEvent::ConfigureRefused` the core clears this field and sends
    /// nothing**: a budget refusal is a fact about the request, so a second
    /// send would be refused again and the pair would loop without a cap
    /// (section 5.5, critic C16-4). No user change is lost, because step 1
    /// already changed the document in memory and the user already sees it.
    pending_configure: Option<Box<ConfigureRequest>>,
    /// Where the project lives, or `None` before the first open.
    bundle: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The read end of the B28 client input channel (section 5.8).
    ///
    /// **The four ends below are the core's half of the structural seam**
    /// (critic C22I-1, C22I-2). Revision 22 gave `DuetCore` the duty of
    /// receiving every `CoreInput`, of answering every client, of sending
    /// every `ConfigureCommand`, and of receiving every `EngineEvent`, and it
    /// declared no channel end of any kind, so four stated duties had no
    /// value that could perform them.
    inputs: CoreReceiver<CoreInput>,
    /// The read end of the B138 engine event channel (section 5.8).
    ///
    /// The core's input loop selects over this receiver and `inputs` with
    /// one `futures` select, so a message on either channel wakes the same
    /// loop and every bound of section 9.5 rule 8 is measured on its passes.
    engine_events: CoreReceiver<EngineEvent>,
    /// The write end of the B109 configure channel (section 5.8).
    ///
    /// It is a `SyncSender`, so `try_send` returns the command on a full
    /// channel and the core keeps it in `pending_configure`. A blocking send
    /// here would park the thread that paints, which TH3 forbids.
    configure: SyncSender<ConfigureCommand>,
    /// Every client this core serves, at B141.
    clients: ArrayVec<ClientLink, MAX_CLIENTS>,
    /// The write end of the published tempo map (section 2.11, section 5.8).
    tempo: Input<TempoMap>,
    /// The write end of the published parameter set (section 5.8).
    params: Input<ParamSnapshot>,
    /// The write end of the published playback plan (section 5.10).
    ///
    /// A job thread builds the plan inside B130 and hands it here; the core
    /// performs the one `write` that publishes it, because `Input` is the
    /// write end and one owner holds it (section 5.8, critic C21I-1).
    plan: Input<PlaybackPlan>,
    /// The flags each armed track has accumulated in the current pass, at B146.
    ///
    /// **Each element names its own track** (critic C23I-5). Revision 23
    /// declared an `ArrayVec<TakeFlags, MAX_DISK_RINGS>`, which gives a
    /// position and not a track and which counts rings where the list holds
    /// one entry per armed TRACK, so nothing mapped an entry to the
    /// `CaptureInfo::track` whose take the flags belong to. C21-4 closed the
    /// identical hole on the message side one revision earlier.
    ///
    /// **The CORE assembles `TakeFlags`, and this is the field that holds
    /// them** (critic C22I-4). Section 6.4 names five observers and four of
    /// them are the backend, the audio thread and `duet-midi`; no boundary
    /// carries any of the four to the disk thread, so a `CaptureInfo` built
    /// on the disk thread could carry at most the one flag that thread
    /// raises itself. The core already receives every `EngineFault`, every
    /// `HotplugEvent` and every `Calibration`, so the core is the one party
    /// that sees all five.
    take_flags: ArrayVec<TrackFlags, MAX_DISK_TRACKS>,
}

/// The write end of the B28 core input channel, as every producer holds it.
///
/// `async_channel::Sender` is `Clone`, so one channel has many producers and
/// one receiver, which is the shape section 5.8 states for B28. **This
/// newtype is the ONE declaration of that end** (TH13, critic C22I-2). The
/// core clones one into every thread it starts, which is each B37 job worker
/// and the `duet-quit-save` thread of TH12, and one into the debounce
/// callback it hands `duet-project` at section 9.4. Every client holds one
/// as well, inside its own `CoreClient`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CoreLink { inputs: Sender<CoreInput> }

/// The three ends one CLIENT holds, as that client holds them.
///
/// `async_channel::Receiver` is `Clone`, so the drain task of section 10.2
/// takes a clone and the owner keeps one; `triple_buffer::Output` is not,
/// which is why a publication has exactly one read end and a channel does
/// not (section 5.8).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CoreClient {
    /// The write end this client sends every `CoreInput` on, at B28.
    link: CoreLink,
    /// The read end of this client's own `CoreEvent` channel, at B29.
    events: CoreReceiver<CoreEvent>,
    /// The read end of this client's own `Snapshot` channel, at B30.
    snapshots: CoreReceiver<Snapshot>,
}

/// The `duet-quit-save` thread's own state (TH12).
///
/// The core builds it at step 6 of section 9.5 rule 8 and moves it onto one
/// `std::thread`. The thread runs the atomic save of section 4.10, releases
/// the writer lock, sends `CoreInput::QuitSaveDone` on `core`, and ends.
/// Revision 22 named the thread, named the bytes it carries and named the
/// message it answers with, and declared no value that holds any of the
/// three (critic C22I-2, TH13).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct QuitSave {
    /// Where the project lives.
    bundle: PathBuf,
    /// The byte form of every dirty document, in `BundleDocument::paths`
    /// order. The CORE builds it, because a serialization is an allocation
    /// and not a file call, and step 6 states that split.
    documents: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    /// The write end of the B28 core input channel.
    core: CoreLink,
}

impl DuetCore {
    /// Register one client and return the ends that client holds.
    ///
    /// **A bounded registry needs a declared path to its own refusal**
    /// (critic C23I-W7). Revision 23 declared `clients`, B141 and
    /// `CoreError::ClientBudgetExceeded`, and no `CoreInput` arm, no method
    /// and no carrier row could fill the list or reach the refusal. This is
    /// the one party that creates both halves: it builds the B29 and B30
    /// channels, keeps the `ClientLink` and returns the `CoreClient`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns `CoreError::ClientBudgetExceeded` when B141 clients are
    /// already registered.
    pub fn register_client(&mut self, client: u64) -> Result<CoreClient, CoreError>;

    /// Forget one client and drop its two write ends, which closes both
    /// channels and ends that client's drain task.
    pub fn release_client(&mut self, client: u64);
}

/// The two write ends of one client, as `DuetCore` holds them.
///
/// Section 5.8 gives each client its own `CoreEvent` channel at B29 and its
/// own `Snapshot` channel at B30, and revision 22 declared neither end
/// (critic C22I-2). `client` is the identifier `CoreInput::Resynchronize` and
/// `CoreEvent::ClientDegraded` both name, so the registry needs no second
/// index.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ClientLink {
    client: u64,
    events: Sender<CoreEvent>,
    snapshots: Sender<Snapshot>,
}

/// The one read end of the meter publication.
///
/// **It is the one place outside `duet-engine` that names a `triple_buffer`
/// type**, and it is the one owner of that publication's `Output`.
/// `Entity<CoreHost>` holds exactly one of these, and no view holds any
/// (section 10.2, critic CR-4, CR-11). It also holds a third handle on the
/// shared reset generations, so it answers the per-strip over-mark compare of
/// section 7.3 without an event and without a copy of any audio-owned memory.
///
/// `latest` is the foreground-only slot the last `poll` filled. It is a
/// `Copy` value, so any number of views read it and none of them can make the
/// reader answer twice in one frame.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MeterReader {
    output: Output<MeterSnapshot>,
    /// The one read end of the per-slot publication (section 7.3, section
    /// 5.8, critic C21-7). It sits on this reader and not on a reader of its
    /// own, because `CoreHost` polls once per frame before any child view
    /// renders and a second reader would be a second poll of the same frame.
    slots: Output<SlotMeterSnapshot>,
    resets: Arc<ResetGenerations>,
    latest: MeterView,
    /// The per-slot measurements of this frame, indexed by the section 7.3
    /// cell formula. `poll` fills it from `slots`.
    latest_slots: [SlotMeasure; MAX_SLOT_METERS],
    /// How many cells of `latest_slots` the configured topology fills.
    live_slots: u16,
    /// Per strip, the peak cap this reader holds between frames (B111, B112).
    /// It is the foreground half of the meter seam: the audio thread
    /// publishes no cap (section 7.3, critic C16-8).
    caps: [Finite; MAX_STRIPS],
    /// Per strip, the milliseconds of B111 hold that remain for the cap in
    /// `caps`. Zero means the cap falls at B112 on the next poll.
    holds: [Finite; MAX_STRIPS],
}

impl MeterReader {
    /// Read the publication, resolve every held mark, and age every peak cap
    /// into the slot.
    ///
    /// `CoreHost::poll_frame` calls it once per frame, before any child view
    /// renders (section 10.2), and it passes the milliseconds since the last
    /// call. The frame delta is the only clock this rule reads, so a test
    /// drives B111 and B112 with plain numbers (section 7.3).
    pub fn poll(&mut self, elapsed_ms: Finite);

    /// The meter values of this frame, as the last `poll` resolved them.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn latest(&self) -> MeterView;

    /// The measurement at one cell of the section 7.3 formula, or `None`
    /// when the cell is at or above the number the topology fills.
    ///
    /// It is the one producer of `StageCurve::measure`, so the limiter
    /// gain-reduction bar of contract 5.2 and the compressor live dot of PR
    /// M-03 both read a value this reader resolved (critic C21-7).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn slot_measure(&self, cell: u16) -> Option<SlotMeasure>;
}

/// The one read end of the transport publication.
///
/// It exists for the same reason `MeterReader` does, it holds the same
/// foreground-only slot, and it answers in the plain-data `TransportView` of
/// section 15.5.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct TransportReader {
    output: Output<TransportSnapshot>,
    latest: TransportView,
}

impl TransportReader {
    /// Read the publication into the slot, once per frame.
    pub fn poll(&mut self);

    /// The transport of this frame.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn latest(&self) -> TransportView;
}

/// The name of one undo transaction, as the History surface shows it.
///
/// It derives `Eq`, because a `Box<str>` supplies it. A name is not an
/// identity: nothing looks a transaction up by its display string, so it
/// derives no `Hash` and no order and VR1 names no use (critic W16).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TransactionName(Box<str>);

/// Every way the core refuses. It wraps the gateway refusal.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub enum CoreError { Gateway(GatewayError), NothingToUndo, NothingToRedo, ChannelClosed, ClientBudgetExceeded }
```
