### 15.16 `crates/duet`

Every type here is `pub(crate)`. `crates/duet` is a binary, so `unreachable_pub` makes that the
only correct visibility, and no type below crosses the transport.

**No type here carries a `missing_copy_implementations` expectation, and VR5's site says why.** The
lint fires on a type that is publicly reachable from a library root, so it cannot fire inside this
crate, and `-D warnings` then turns an unfulfilled expectation into a build error. Revision 9
carried three of them, and a compiler run proves that each one stops its chunk (critic S3).
`PunchRange`, `LevelMeter`, and `LufsMeter` derive `Copy`; a `RenderOnce` element is consumed by
value in `render`, so the derive costs nothing at a call site.

```rust
/// The root view. It owns the mode and every child entity (section 10.2).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct DuetApp {
    mode: Mode,
    core: Entity<CoreHost>,
    agent: Entity<AgentBridge>,
    title_bar: Entity<TitleBar>,
    mode_switcher: Entity<ModeSwitcher>,
    top_bar: Entity<TopBar>,
    transport_bar: Entity<TransportBar>,
    sidebar: Entity<Sidebar>,
    inspector: Entity<Inspector>,
    status_bar: Entity<StatusBar>,
    history: Entity<HistorySheet>,
    start: Entity<StartView>,
    menu: Entity<MenuHost>,
    view_state: Entity<ViewStateStore>,
    compose: Entity<ComposeView>,
    record: Entity<RecordView>,
    mix: Entity<MixView>,
    master: Entity<MasterView>,
    focus: FocusHandle,
    subscriptions: Vec<Subscription>,
}

/// Why a frame driver runs this frame.
///
/// **Each field is one START condition of section 10.2**, and a driver stops
/// when every condition it reads is false and its own slot equals what it
/// last painted. Revision 14 gave each driver a stop condition and no start
/// condition, so an armed input meter froze while the transport was stopped
/// (critic CR-21).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct FrameDemand {
    /// The transport rolls or locates, so the playhead moves.
    transport_moves: bool,
    /// An input level can change with the transport stopped, because at
    /// least one strip is armed OR at least one track carries
    /// `MonitorMode::Always`.
    ///
    /// **The two causes are one demand, and one field carries both** (critic
    /// C15-10). Revision 15 read the arm state alone, so a user who monitored
    /// without arming saw a meter that froze, which is CR-21 at a second
    /// site. They are one field and not two because four `bool` fields trip
    /// `clippy::struct_excessive_bools`, which the roster compile proved, and
    /// because a driver that reacts to one reacts to the other in the same
    /// way. Setting a record level before the transport rolls is a product
    /// function (design contract 4.4), and it is the same function through
    /// either path.
    input_live: bool,
    /// A meter bar or a held over mark still differs from silence, so the
    /// fall of design contract 4.4 has frames left to paint.
    meter_decays: bool,
}

/// The entity that owns `DuetCore`, drains its event channel, and holds the
/// one read end of each audio publication.
///
/// **`poll_frame` is the frame order of section 10.2.** `DuetApp::render`
/// calls it first, before it builds any child element, and it reads both
/// `triple_buffer` outputs into their foreground-only slots. A frame driver
/// then reads a slot through `MeterReader::latest` or
/// `TransportReader::latest`. Revision 12 gave the one `MeterReader` to two
/// views and the one `TransportReader` to two more, which needs four read
/// ends where two exist (critic CR-11).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct CoreHost {
    core: DuetCore,
    /// The drain task. Dropping it stops the drain (Appendix A).
    drain: Task<()>,
    version: Version,
    engine: EngineState,
    fault: Option<EngineFault>,
    meters: MeterReader,
    transport: TransportReader,
    /// This host's own client ends, at B28, B29 and B30 (section 5.8).
    ///
    /// `drain` reads a clone of `CoreClient::events`, which is what lets the
    /// owner keep the value while the task runs. Revision 22 gave `CoreHost`
    /// the drain task and declared no channel end for it to drain (critic
    /// C22I-2).
    client: CoreClient,
    /// Whether the frame pump re-armed itself on the last poll. It is the
    /// one place the start condition of section 10.2 is decided, so the four
    /// drivers read one answer.
    pumping: bool,
    /// The theme observer.
    ///
    /// `Context::observe_global::<gpui_kit::component::Theme>`
    /// (`gpui-pre-0.3.5/src/app/context.rs:177`) returns a `Subscription`,
    /// and `gpui_kit::component::Theme` is a `Global`
    /// (`gpui-component-0.6.4/src/theme/mod.rs:193`). The closure calls
    /// `DuetTokens::resolve` and `cx.set_global`, which is contract 7.1
    /// rule 2. The field lives here because `CoreHost` outlives every mode
    /// view and Appendix A rule 3 makes a dropped subscription a defect;
    /// revision 14 stated the duty and declared no holder (critic WR-28).
    theme: Subscription,
}

impl CoreHost {
    /// Read both publications into their slots and re-arm the frame pump.
    ///
    /// It calls `MeterReader::poll` with the milliseconds since its own last
    /// call, which is the clock B111 and B112 read, then it calls
    /// `TransportReader::poll`, it
    /// stores `frame_demand`, and **when any driver is active it re-arms
    /// itself** with `Context::on_next_frame`
    /// (`gpui-pre-0.3.5/src/app/context.rs:293`), which schedules a closure
    /// against `Window::on_next_frame` at `src/window.rs:2586`. The poll is
    /// therefore driven by the window's frame callback and not by
    /// `DuetApp::render` alone (section 10.2, critic CR-21).
    ///
    /// `DuetApp::render` still calls it as its first statement, which is what
    /// makes the slot of the current frame ready before any child element is
    /// built.
    pub(crate) fn poll_frame(&mut self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>);

    /// Why a frame driver runs this frame, from the slots the last poll
    /// filled and the armed set `DuetCore` holds.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn frame_demand(&self) -> FrameDemand;

    /// The meter values of this frame, as `MeterReader::latest` answers them.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn meters(&self) -> MeterView;

    /// The transport of this frame, as `TransportReader::latest` answers it.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn transport(&self) -> TransportView;

    /// The measurement at one cell of the section 7.3 formula, or `None`
    /// when the cell is at or above the number the topology fills.
    ///
    /// **It is the one path from `MeterReader::slot_measure` to a view**
    /// (critic C22I-8). Section 5.8 keeps every publication read end
    /// out of `crates/duet` and gives `duet-core` the one owner of each one
    /// (critic C23I-N5), and `meters` answers a `MeterView` that carries
    /// no slot cell, so `MixView`, `MasterView` and `Inspector` could fill
    /// no `StageCurve::measure` at all. It follows the `meters` pattern
    /// exactly: the host polled once this frame and every caller reads the
    /// `Copy` result.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn slot_measure(&self, cell: u16) -> Option<SlotMeasure>;
}

/// One verb in flight from a tokio task to the gateway, with its reply end.
///
/// **This is the seam between the two runtimes of this process, and revision
/// 23 declared no end of it at all** (critic C23I-1). Section 9.5 rule 5
/// states that a tokio task sends a `GatewayRequest` and that a `cx.spawn`
/// task returns the result on a oneshot, and TH13 binds every cross-thread
/// duty, so the one seam the two thread rows share needed two carrier rows
/// and four declared ends. `GatewayRequest` itself stays plain data in
/// `duet-command`, because VR3 puts every value that crosses the transport
/// there and a reply end is not plain data.
pub(crate) struct GatewayCall {
    request: GatewayRequest,
    /// The write end of the reply. `send` consumes it, so one reply exists.
    reply: OneshotSender<Result<VerbOutcome, GatewayError>>,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for GatewayCall {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("GatewayCall").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The tokio side of one in-flight verb (section 9.5 rule 5).
///
/// The task awaits `reply` under a `tokio::time::timeout` of B23, which is
/// the Appendix B.5 row for that bound, and rule 9 states what an elapsed
/// wait means for the agent contract.
pub(crate) struct AgentCall {
    request: GatewayRequest,
    /// The read end of the reply.
    reply: OneshotReceiver<Result<VerbOutcome, GatewayError>>,
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for AgentCall {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("AgentCall").finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// The entity that owns the tokio runtime and the shutdown choke point.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct AgentBridge {
    runtime: Option<Runtime>,
    cancel: CancellationToken,
    /// Set by `shut_down`, so a second call answers `AlreadyRun`.
    finished: bool,
    /// The write end of the B35 request channel, cloned into every tokio
    /// task (section 9.5 rule 6).
    ///
    /// `async_channel::Sender` is `Clone` and its `send` suspends when the
    /// channel is full, which is the backpressure rule 6 states: a runaway
    /// agent slows down instead of exhausting memory.
    requests: Sender<GatewayCall>,
    /// The read end of the same channel, which the `cx.spawn` task drains on
    /// the GPUI foreground thread.
    inbox: CoreReceiver<GatewayCall>,
}

/// One fact `DuetApp` emits to its children.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum AppEvent { ModeChanged(Mode), PendingDuration(NoteValue), ProjectOpened, ProjectClosed, SelectionChanged }

/// Every way the shell refuses.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub(crate) enum AppError { Core(CoreError), Shutdown(ShutdownError), NoProject }

/// Every way the shutdown choke point refuses. `Drop` absorbs it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error)]
pub(crate) enum ShutdownError { RuntimeStuck, ReplyTimeout, AlreadyRun }

/// One path through the menu model, from the root to the item.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub(crate) struct MenuPath(Box<str>);

/// Where one strip's meter sits in the mixer row, for `MeterLayer`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct MeterSlot { strip: StripId, x: f32, width: f32 }

/// Every colour role design contract section 7 defines, resolved once.
///
/// **Contract 7.1 mandates this layer and revision 13 declared no type for
/// it** (critic WR-20). `gpui_kit::component::Theme` has no field for a staff, a
/// waveform, a meter, or a playhead, so Duet publishes its own roles as a
/// GPUI `Global`: chunk K1 writes `impl gpui_kit::Global for DuetTokens {}`,
/// resolves the value once at start, and resolves it again on every change
/// of `cx.theme().mode`. **A view reads `cx.global::<DuetTokens>()` and holds
/// no `Hsla` literal**, which is contract 7.1 rule 3 and the reason every
/// painting element of chunks K2 to K5 has a token to read.
///
/// The four `part_*` roles carry the meaning of a part everywhere, and the
/// two waveform roles derive from them, so contract 7.2 states them as one
/// row each and this type answers them with a method rather than four more
/// fields. **The two are `duet.wave.fill` and `duet.wave.rms`**, which
/// `wave_fill` and `wave_rms` answer below, and naming them here is what
/// makes the count readable: contract 7.2 states 29 tokens, this type
/// declares 27 fields, and the remaining two are the derived pair
/// (critic N21-15). Revision 21 stated the derivation and named neither
/// token, so a reader could not join the two numbers. `resolve` applies contract 7.3 rule 6: a role the contract marks
/// `own` is checked against the live background and moved by up to twelve
/// lightness points to meet the contrast floor of contract section 9.
/// It derives `Debug` and `Clone` and nothing else. `Hsla` is a framework
/// type, so section 1.9 decides none of its traits and a `Copy` derive over
/// it would rest on a shape no section states (PG10b). A `Global` is read by
/// reference through `cx.global`, so no caller needs the copy.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub(crate) struct DuetTokens {
    staff_paper: Hsla,
    staff_ink: Hsla,
    staff_ink_muted: Hsla,
    staff_line: Hsla,
    staff_grid: Hsla,
    staff_preview: Hsla,
    note_selected: Hsla,
    note_selected_halo: Hsla,
    note_cursor: Hsla,
    part_soprano: Hsla,
    part_alto: Hsla,
    part_tenor: Hsla,
    part_bass: Hsla,
    wave_zero: Hsla,
    wave_absent: Hsla,
    record_red: Hsla,
    record_tint: Hsla,
    meter_low: Hsla,
    meter_mid: Hsla,
    meter_high: Hsla,
    meter_clip: Hsla,
    meter_peak_cap: Hsla,
    meter_scale: Hsla,
    playhead: Hsla,
    automation_line: Hsla,
    lufs_target: Hsla,
    lufs_tolerance: Hsla,
}

impl DuetTokens {
    /// Resolve every role against the theme in scope.
    ///
    /// K1 calls it at start and again on every theme change, and it writes
    /// the value with `cx.set_global`.
    pub(crate) fn resolve(cx: &App) -> Self;

    /// The colour of one part, which contract 7.3 rule 2 makes the one
    /// identity of that part across the sidebar, the lane, the waveform, the
    /// strip, and the filter.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn part(&self, voice: VoiceType) -> Hsla;

    /// The waveform fill of one part, which contract 7.2 derives from the
    /// part colour.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn wave_fill(&self, voice: VoiceType) -> Hsla;

    /// The waveform mean-square colour of one part, which is the part colour
    /// itself.
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn wave_rms(&self, voice: VoiceType) -> Hsla;
}

impl Global for DuetTokens {}
```

/// click on one meter share one verb (critic C9).
pub(crate) struct EnterCompose;

pub(crate) struct EnterRecord;

The view entities and the custom elements follow. Each one is a `RenderOnce` element or an
`Entity<T>` view, and Appendix A names the owner, the mutation path, and the identity source of
each piece of state.

#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct LaneView {

    slots: Vec<MeterSlot>,
    cache: PathCache,
    /// The one owner of the linear path build task (section 10.5). A `Task`
    /// that no field holds is dropped at the end of the statement and the
    /// work is cancelled before it starts, so every Mix path would miss and
    /// the miss rule paints nothing (critic C16-W5).
    build: Option<Task<()>>,
    split: Finite,

#[derive(Debug)]

#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct MasterView {
    meters: Entity<MasterMeterLayer>,
    /// **Master owns its own linear path cache** (critic C16-15, C17-3).
    /// Design contract section 5 gives Master a linear timeline above the
    /// master chain, and a GPUI child reaches a sibling only through its
    /// parent. Revision 17 gave the linear key to `MixView` alone, so the
    /// engineer who builds K5 had to invent an owner or ship Master with no
    /// timeline. The two caches hold the same key type and never one value:
    /// B61 bounds each one on its own, and 10.5 states the arithmetic.
    cache: PathCache,
    /// The one owner of this view's path build task, for the reason
    /// `MixView::build` states.
    build: Option<Task<()>>,
    /// The samples-per-pixel scalar of the linear timeline, which is the
    /// third term of the linear key.
    zoom: ZoomScalar,
    stages: Vec<SlotConfig>,
    report: Option<LoudnessReport>,
    target: Normalization,
    export: Option<ExportSpec>,
    job: Option<JobId>,
    state: WorkAreaState,
    focus: FocusHandle,
    subscriptions: Vec<Subscription>,
}

```rust
/// The one frame driver of Compose and Record. It paints the playhead only.
///
/// It reads the transport through `CoreHost::transport`, which returns a copy
/// of the slot the frame order already filled, so no `duet-engine` name, no
/// `triple_buffer` name, and no publication read end reaches this crate
/// (section 5.8, section 10.2, critic CR-4, CR-11). Compose and Record each
/// own one of these, and the `Entity<CoreHost>` handle each one holds is a
/// handle and not a reader.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct PlayheadLayer {
    core: Entity<CoreHost>,
    /// The value the last frame painted.
    ///
    /// **It saves the next frame, not this paint.** `render` returns an
    /// element on every call, so the field cannot stop a paint.
    ///
    /// **The START condition is `FrameDemand::transport_moves`, and the STOP
    /// condition is its negation with the slot at rest** (critic CR-21). The
    /// driver calls `Window::request_animation_frame` when the demand is set
    /// or when the slot differs from this field, so a rolling or locating
    /// transport keeps the loop alive and a still transport with a settled
    /// playhead ends it. The loop restarts because a transport verb produces
    /// a `CoreEvent`, the drain task notifies, and this view renders again.
    shown: TransportView,
}
/// The one frame driver of Mix. It paints every strip meter in one canvas.
///
/// It reads the meters through `CoreHost::meters`, and `duet_core::MeterReader`
/// owns the `triple_buffer` output and resolves the held over marks against
/// the shared reset generations (section 7.3, critic CR-1, CR-4, CR-11).
/// **The layer therefore holds no generation state of its own, no
/// `duet-engine` name, and no publication read end.** It paints the bar, the
/// peak cap, the `CLIP` text, and the numeric readout of design contract 4.4
/// through `duet_dsp::meter_law::db_to_fraction` (critic WR-5, WR-13).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct MeterLayer {
    core: Entity<CoreHost>,
    /// Where each strip's meter sits, published by `MixView`.
    slots: Vec<MeterSlot>,
    /// The value the last frame painted. It saves the next frame request,
    /// exactly as `PlayheadLayer::shown` does.
    ///
    /// **The START condition is `FrameDemand::input_live` or
    /// `FrameDemand::transport_moves`, and the STOP condition is both of them
    /// false with `FrameDemand::meter_decays` false** (critic CR-21). **An
    /// armed strip therefore keeps the loop alive whatever the transport
    /// does**, which is what setting a record level needs.
    ///
    /// **The driver holds no copy of the armed set.** It calls
    /// `CoreHost::frame_demand` in `render`, so `DuetCore` stays the one
    /// owner of the armed set and no second copy can go stale (Appendix A).
    /// The loop restarts because `MixView` calls `cx.notify` on this entity
    /// when the armed set changes, which is a notification and not a value,
    /// and because `CoreHost::poll_frame` re-arms itself from
    /// `Window::on_next_frame` while any demand is set, so a fresh slot
    /// exists before this view renders.
    shown: MeterView,
}
/// The one frame driver of Master. It reads the same slot `MeterLayer` reads,
/// because the publication has one read end and `CoreHost` owns it.
///
/// It carries the same start and stop conditions `MeterLayer` states, it reads
/// the same `CoreHost::frame_demand`, and `MasterView` restarts it with the
/// same `cx.notify`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct MasterMeterLayer {
    core: Entity<CoreHost>,
    shown: MeterView,
    report: Option<LoudnessReport>,
    target: Normalization,
}
/// Paints one system: lines, glyphs, stems, beams, and ties.
#[derive(Debug, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct StaffSystem { placement: Arc<SystemPlacement>, system: SystemId }
/// Paints one audio lane from the cached peak paths.
#[derive(Debug, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct WaveformLane { segments: Arc<[TakeSegment]>, track: TrackId }
/// The punch band and its two drag handles.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct PunchRange { span: Option<Span>, track: TrackId }
/// One meter bar, painted from a reading its parent hands it.
///
/// **It is stateless.** It owns no reading, no clip latch, and no frame; the
/// caller passes the value it paints, so the element cannot go stale at a
/// rate of its own (critic W-7, WR-5). `held` is the resolved over mark that
/// `MeterReader` already decided (section 7.3), so the element runs no
/// generation compare.
///
/// **It is not the mixer strip row.** `MeterLayer` paints every strip meter
/// and every numeric readout in one canvas (section 10.2). This element
/// serves the single meters outside that canvas, such as the input meter of
/// the inspector and the take-strip meter of Record.
///
/// **It carries no scale field.** Design contract 4.4 fixes the scale, B106
/// carries its numbers, and `duet_dsp::meter_law::db_to_fraction` applies it,
/// so the element holds a reading and a resolved mark and nothing else.
/// Revision 12 gave it a `ParamRange`, which was an identifier range and
/// could produce no decibel (critic WR-13).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct LevelMeter {
    strip: StripId,
    reading: MeterReading,
    held: bool,
}
/// One channel fader with a decibel taper and detents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct Fader { parameter: ParamId, value: Finite, strip: StripId }
/// One radial control with an arc and a pointer line.
///
/// `range` is the parameter's own value range, which
/// `duet_session::param_range` answers. Design contract 4.5 moves the value
/// by one percent of that range per pixel, so the element needs the bounds
/// and not a count of parameters (critic WR-13).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct Knob { parameter: ParamId, value: Finite, range: ParamRange }
/// A polyline and its handles over a linear time axis.
#[derive(Debug, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct AutomationLane { parameter: ParamId, points: Arc<CurvePoints>, zoom: ZoomStep }
/// One processor's response curve, with a live dot where the contract asks.
///
/// `cell` is the section 7.3 cell index of this slot and `measure` is what
/// `MeterReader::slot_measure` answered for it this frame. **The two
/// quantities are separate fields of `SlotMeasure`**, because contract 5.2
/// draws the compressor dot at the INPUT level and the limiter bar at the
/// gain REDUCTION, and one scalar cannot carry both (critic C21-7).
#[derive(Debug, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct StageCurve { slot: SlotId, kind: SlotKind, params: Arc<[Finite]>, cell: u16, measure: Option<SlotMeasure> }
/// Momentary, short term, integrated, target, and tolerance.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct LufsMeter { report: LoudnessReport, target: Normalization }
/// One control inside a toolbar group.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum ToolbarControl {
    Button { id: MenuPath, label: SharedString },
    Toggle { id: MenuPath, label: SharedString, on: bool },
    Select { id: MenuPath, label: SharedString, options: Vec<SharedString>, chosen: usize },
    Separator,
}

/// One group of the top bar: its label and the controls contract 1.5 gives it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ToolbarGroup {
    id: MenuPath,
    label: SharedString,
    controls: Vec<ToolbarControl>,
}

/// One mode's toolbar, as the groups the design contract names for that mode.
///
/// **`ModeToolbar::render` returns one of these.** Revision 11 returned a
/// one-byte `Toolbar` that held the mode alone, so every group the
/// implementation built and the `visible` count it was given were lost at the
/// return (critic WR-4). `groups` is in the fixed removal order of contract
/// 1.5: the trailing end moves into the overflow menu first.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ToolbarGroups {
    mode: Mode,
    groups: Vec<ToolbarGroup>,
    /// How many groups the bar paints. `TopBar` computes it from the width it
    /// measured, so the cut point follows the window (critic K-12).
    visible: usize,
}

/// The top bar container with the overflow rule.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, IntoElement)]
pub(crate) struct Toolbar { groups: ToolbarGroups }
/// One mode's group set inside the top bar.
///
/// **It is a trait, and `TopBar` holds a registry of four boxed
/// implementations.** `TopBar` keys the registry by `Mode` and calls `render`
/// on the one the current mode names. Chunk K1 writes `top_bar.rs`, the
/// registry, and the four implementations below, and each of the four returns
/// an empty toolbar. K2, K3, K4, and K5 each replace one `render` body in its
/// own module file and none of them edits `top_bar.rs`. Revision 10 gave each
/// chunk a stub file that held module documentation and nothing else, so
/// `TopBar` could name no item inside it and every later chunk wrote dead code
/// (critic W-2). **It is not a GPUI element**: it builds a `Toolbar`, which is
/// the element, so section 10.3's list is unchanged (critic K-11).
pub(crate) trait ModeToolbar: core::fmt::Debug {
    /// How many groups this mode has, in the fixed removal order of
    /// contract 1.5. The order is fixed per mode; the count that fits is not.
    fn group_count(&self) -> usize;

    /// Build this mode's groups, with `visible` of them on the bar and every
    /// later group in the overflow menu. `TopBar` wraps the answer in a
    /// `Toolbar` element.
    ///
    /// **`visible` is width dependent, and `TopBar` computes it.** Contract
    /// 1.5 removes groups from the trailing end until the widths fit, so the
    /// cut point follows the window and one fixed index cannot express it
    /// (critic K-12).
    fn render(&self, visible: usize, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> ToolbarGroups;
}

/// The Compose group set. Chunk K1 creates it and K2 fills `render`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct ComposeToolbar;
/// The Record group set. Chunk K1 creates it and K3 fills `render`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct RecordToolbar;
/// The Mix group set. Chunk K1 creates it and K4 fills `render`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct MixToolbar;
/// The Master group set. Chunk K1 creates it and K5 fills `render`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct MasterToolbar;
```

---

## Appendix A: ownership boundaries

Every row names one state, its one owner, the one path that mutates it, who observes it, and the
source of its identity.

| State | Owner | Mutation path | Observers | Identity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Score`, `Session`, `MixState`, `ViewState`, `UndoStack`, the job registry | `DuetCore` inside `Entity<CoreHost>`, each document behind an `Arc` | `Gateway::call` on the core thread only | `DuetApp` through `CoreEvent` | Persisted `u64` counters |
| The mode | `Entity<DuetApp>` | `on_action` for the four mode actions | Every child view through `AppEvent::ModeChanged` | Not repeated |
| The engraved systems | `Entity<ComposeView>` | `cx.update` from the background engrave task, guarded by revision | `SystemView` children | `SystemId` |
| One system placement | `Entity<SystemView>` | Set by `ComposeView` on a new engrave result | `StaffSystem` | `SystemId` |
| Caret and selection | `Entity<ComposeView>` | `on_mouse_down`, `on_action` | `StaffSystem` through its input | `NoteId` |
| The duration selector | `Entity<ComposeView>` | `on_key_down`, `on_key_up`, `on_focus_out`, window deactivate, number keys, top bar | `TopBar` through `AppEvent::PendingDuration` | Not repeated |
| The tessellated `PathCache` | `Entity<RecordView>` in Record, `Entity<MixView>` in Mix, and `Entity<MasterView>` in Master, which is one cache per mode and three owners (section 10.5, B61, critic C21-W6, C22I-W7). **Compose holds none**, because Compose paints no waveform (critic K-13) | `cx.update` from the path build task | Every `LaneView` reads it | `(SourceHash, RegionId, SystemId, ZoomStep)` in Record and `(SourceHash, RegionId, ZoomScalar)` in Mix and Master, bounded by B61 |
| One peak pyramid | `DuetCore` | The peak read task, then `CoreEvent::PeaksReady` | `LaneView`, which opens no file | `SourceHash` |
| The start surface and the recent list | `Entity<StartView>` | `on_click`, then `Verb::RecentList` and `Verb::RecentAdd` through the gateway | `DuetApp` | Bundle path |
| The menu model | `Entity<MenuHost>` | Built once at start; rebuilt on a mode change | The platform menu bar or `AppMenuBar` | `MenuPath` |
| The whole `ViewState`: mode, one `ModeView` per mode, window geometry | `Entity<ViewStateStore>`, which holds one `ProjectView` | `on_drag_move`, `on_scroll_wheel`, a mode action; written through `Verb::ViewSet` | `DuetApp`; `duet-project` saves a `ViewDocument` as `state/view.json`, which git does not track | `Mode` keys the per-mode map |
| Track selection, lane heights, comp mode | `Entity<RecordView>` | `on_mouse_down`, `on_drag_move` | `LaneView` children | `TrackId` |
| The one `BufferPool` and every `ChainState`, each behind a `basedrop::Owned` | The audio thread while a cycle runs, inside `GraphState`. `configure` builds the pool once per open stream and the state of every ADDED chain, on the engine handoff thread, and the collector releases every retired value on that same thread (TH5) | The generation check of section 5.6: a drain of the B105 ring, then the per-position move that turns each `ChainSlot::Keep` into the state it takes out of the old array, then the in-place slot migration of section 5.5 inside each kept chain. The audio thread never resizes the array, never copies a `ChainState`, and never frees a ring (critic CR-16, CR-17) | Nothing; **no other thread ever holds a reference to one `ChainState`**, which is why a migration is a plan and never a copy | `StripId` and `PoolSlot`; a bus chain carries no `TrackId` and no ring |
| The chain layout, the pending configuration, and the `basedrop` collector | `GraphConfigurator`, on the engine handoff thread | One `ConfigureCommand` at B109 per pass of that thread's loop. **`configure` refuses to build while `rtrb::Producer::slots` reports no free slot**, so the layout is always the array the audio thread holds. `ConfigureCommand::Reset` clears the pending configuration and the layout, and the core sends it only after the stream is closed (critic WR-27) | Nothing; the thread reports through `EngineEvent` | `ChainIndex`, which is a position of the array the layout names |
| Fader and knob drag state | `Entity<StripView>` | `on_drag_move`, `on_mouse_up` | `Fader`, `Knob` | `(StripId, ParamId)` |
| Meter slot positions | `Entity<MixView>` | Recomputed when the strip list or the layout changes, not per frame | `MeterLayer` | `StripId` |
| Transport position, meter values, and per-slot measurements, which are the audio-written rows of the section 5.8 snapshot table | The audio thread, published by `triple_buffer` | The audio cycle writes; nothing else. Every published type is `Copy` with no heap field (TH9) | `duet_core::MeterReader` and `duet_core::TransportReader`, each one the single read end (section 5.8) | `StripId`, through the `MeterSnapshot` array index that `MixView` publishes as a `MeterSlot`, and the section 7.3 cell formula for a `SlotMeasure` |

Four rules hold across the table.

1. **One frame driver per work area.** Section 10.2 names the four. No other view requests an
   animation frame, and none of the four owns a publication: `CoreHost` reads both `Output` values
   at the top of the frame and each driver reads the slot (critic CR-11).
2. **No `ElementId` comes from a list index or a translated label.** A note uses `NoteId`, a region
   uses `RegionId`, a strip uses `StripId`, a system uses `SystemId`.
3. **Every `Subscription` is stored on the subscriber entity.** A dropped subscription is a defect,
   and test 6 of section 10.7 catches it.
4. **The path cache has one owner and one key per timeline shape.** Section 10.5 holds the two
   keys and ADR 0006 gives the bound. `ZoomScalar` is a `duet-command` type that `ZoomStep::scalar`
   produces; revision 9 named it here and declared it nowhere (critic W14).

## Appendix B: policy exceptions

Each row needs a decision from the Orchestrator before the chunk that contains it is dispatched.

### B.1 Lint suppressions

**This list is a budget, not an approval.** An implementer must try to avoid every row. A row that is
avoided is a gain, and the implementer records how. A suppression outside this list is a plan defect
and returns to the Architect.

Seven suppressions in `duet-time::convert`. Each reason names an invariant that a reader CHECKS in
the function body, not a promise a caller made and not a prediction about a refactor nobody
performed (critic C20-N4).

**Each row names its LINTS, and a cast site names more than one.** `Cargo.toml:6` reads "A crate may
relax ONE lint at ONE site", and a bare `as` cast trips `clippy::as_conversions` beside at least one
pedantic cast lint, so the real attribute names two or three. **One `#[expect]` attribute carries
every lint of one site**, which is what "one site" means; the rule counts sites and not lint names.
Revision 20 stated a lint for none of the twenty rows and never addressed the multi-lint shape
(critic C20-N4).

#### Conversion suppressions

<!-- GUARD BLOCK id=b1-convert rows>=7 -->
| Site | Lints the attribute names | Reason text that the code must carry |
|---|---|---|
| `i24_to_f32` | `as_conversions`, `cast_precision_loss` | "a 24-bit integer fits the f32 mantissa exactly and the divisor is 2^23, which is a power of two, so the conversion is lossless and the result is in the unit range" |
| `i32_to_f32` | `as_conversions`, `cast_precision_loss` | "a 32-bit integer rounds to the nearest f32, so the loss is below the 24th bit, and the divisor 2^31 is a power of two, which puts the result in the unit range and adds no further loss" |
| `unit_to_i24` | `as_conversions`, `cast_possible_truncation` | "the `Unit` type carries the range -1.0 to 1.0 and the scale factor is 2^23, so the rounded product lies in -8_388_608.0 to 8_388_608.0, and `I24::new` refuses the one product above `I24::MAX`, which the match clamps" |
| `unit_to_i32` | `as_conversions`, `cast_possible_truncation` | "the `Unit` type carries the range -1.0 to 1.0 and the scale factor is 2^31, so the rounded product lies in -2_147_483_648.0 to 2_147_483_648.0 and the `as i64` cast is exact, and `i32::try_from` refuses the one product above `i32::MAX`, which the match clamps" |
| `f64_to_f32` | `as_conversions`, `cast_possible_truncation` | "the function returns an error for a non-finite value and for a magnitude outside the f32 range before it reaches this line" |
| `ticks_to_f64` | `as_conversions`, `cast_precision_loss` | "the function returns an error at or above 2^53 ticks before it reaches this line, so every integer below that bound converts to an f64 exactly" |
| `finite_to_f32_saturating` | `as_conversions`, `cast_possible_truncation` | "every constructor of `Finite` refuses a NaN and an infinity, so the input is finite; the narrowing drops mantissa bits, and it saturates to an f32 infinity only above the f32 range, which the documentation of this function states" |

**Five rows above are the repair of the two defects chunk T1 found, and chunk M91 lands the code.**
The engineer copied every revision-23 text correctly; only an edit here may change one. ADR 0007
records the decision and states which round trip is exact and which is bounded.

**No guard compared a cell of this block with the `reason =` string in the code, and chunk M90 adds
one** (critic C1-4). That gap is the mechanism that let the T1-1 defect survive a whole revision:
this appendix stated one scale factor, `crates/duet-time/src/convert.rs` carried another, and every
gate was green. Rule CG9 of section 2.3 states the contract, and section 1.9 states how the row and
the register land together.

1. **`unit_to_i24` takes the scale factor 2^23, and the 24-bit round trip is now EXACT.** Revision
   23 fixed the encode factor at 2^23 - 1 while the decode divisor is 2^23, so the composition was
   `x * (1 - 2^-23)`, which is the identity for no sample of magnitude 2^22 or above: measured,
   8_388_607 answered 8_388_606 and -8_388_608 answered -8_388_607. At unity gain a decode and a
   re-encode moved every sample above half scale by one least significant bit, in the trunk crate
   of a product whose value is lossless editing. **The two scale factors are now one number**, both
   2^23, and `i24_to_f32` then `unit_to_i24` is the identity for all 16,777,216 values. The encode
   body already matched `I24::new` and answered `None => I24::MAX`, so the one product a unit value
   of exactly +1.0 produces, 8_388_608.0, clamps to `I24::MAX` through the arm that is already
   there. Plan store `fluid:next_steps_from_T1`, item FU-1 (chunk T1, 2026-09-22).
2. **`unit_to_i32` takes the scale factor 2^31 and an explicit clamp, so the pair is symmetric.**
   Revision 23 fixed the encode factor at 2^31 - 1 against a decode divisor of 2^31, which is the
   same defect at 32 bits, and it relied on the saturating behaviour of an `as` cast for the one
   product above `i32::MAX`. **A reader cannot CHECK a language rule in a body that does not state
   it**, which is the rule this appendix opens with, so the body now rounds into an `i64`, which is
   exact, and narrows with `i32::try_from` in a match that mirrors the `I24::new` match exactly.
   **The 32-bit round trip is EXACT at a magnitude of 2^24 or below and BOUNDED above it**, because
   an `i32` sample of a larger magnitude does not fit the 24-bit f32 mantissa. **The bound is one
   half of the f32 spacing at the top of the 32-bit range.** The widest binade an `i32` magnitude
   reaches is 2^30 up to 2^31, where one unit in the last place is 2^7, which is 128; round to
   nearest moves a value by at most half of that, which is 64. Both divisors are powers of two, so
   neither scaling adds a further loss. An exhaustive scan of all 4,294,967,296 values confirms the
   bound. **Many samples attain it and no sample is the singular worst case**: 1_073_741_888,
   1_195_673_408 and 1_946_040_768 each drift by exactly 64, and the first the ascending scan finds
   is -2_147_483_584. Section 2.3 gives the derivation in full.

   **Both negative arms of the two matches are unreachable at these factors and stay for totality.**
   A scale factor of 2^23 sends a unit value of -1.0 to exactly -8_388_608.0, which `I24::new`
   accepts, and 2^31 sends it to exactly -2_147_483_648.0, which `i32::try_from` accepts. Each
   binding is named for that state rather than for the clamp, so a reader of a lossless kernel does
   not read the negative arm as the arm the clamp uses (critic C1-18).
3. **The `finite_to_f32_saturating` row names an invariant the body carries, and it names no
   `LogicalPx`.** `LogicalPx` is a `duet-command` type (sections 1.5 and 10.2), and section 1.3
   puts `duet-command` above `duet-time`, so a narrowed parameter would invert the crate graph. The
   function also takes every `Finite` from every crate, so a bound that names one caller's type is
   a promise the body cannot keep. **The invariant a reader checks is the parameter type**: every
   constructor of `Finite` refuses a NaN and an infinity, so the one loss left is the mantissa and
   the one unreachable case is a magnitude above the f32 range. **This function is not on the
   sample path**, so the lossless standard of ADR 0007 does not reach it; an f64 to f32 narrowing
   drops mantissa bits by construction, and section 2.3 rule 2 keeps `f64_to_f32` as the fallible
   form for every caller that can report. Plan store `fluid:next_steps_from_T1`, item FU-2.

Six complexity suppressions. **Each reason names a COUNT a reader checks in the body**, and not an
opinion about a split (critic C20-N4). Revision 20 wrote "a split would hide the order between the
rules" and five sentences like it: a reader can agree or disagree with a prediction and cannot check
it, while a reader can count the arms of a match.

### B.2 Unsafe

**No crate in this plan contains `unsafe`.** Every new crate carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in its
root, as `crates/duet` already does. **Section 8.1 is the one caller of the `pipewire` crate.** It uses the registry listener, which is
safe Rust. Section 5.4 calls no `pipewire` stream method at all: it reaches the same server through
cpal's PipeWire host, and revision 15 named section 5.4 here as a second caller (critic C15-13).
The stream API of the crate is also safe in the caller, which is why ADR 0004 rejects the crate on
the reason the research supports and not on an unsafe claim. Only the raw `pw_buffer` path and
`pw::deinit()` are `unsafe`, and neither is needed (platform, pipewire facts).

TH1 therefore has no mechanical guard, because `GlobalAlloc` is an unsafe trait. Section 5.7 states
the three verification means that do exist and claims no more.

| Licence | Already in `deny.toml` | Action |
|---|---|---|
| MIT, Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0, CC0-1.0, OFL-1.1, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception | Yes | None |
| `Unlicense` | No | **Add it.** `midly` carries it, and chunk X3 needs `midly`. Chunk M0 applies the edit, because `deny.toml` is a policy file (SM4). |

`cargo deny check` reports `multiple-versions` as a warning, not a failure. Section 8.1 reason 3 depends on `midir`'s transitive `alsa` version, and the research file does not
record it (critic S16). Chunk M4 records the output of `cargo tree -i alsa`, because M4 pins `midir`.

`Unlicense` is the only `deny.toml` licence edit this plan requires.

The Bravura font ships with the application under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. A font file is data,
not a crate, so it does not enter `deny.toml`. The Bravura licence text goes in the `NOTICE` file and
in an asset licence list, and chunk M0 writes both.

### B.5 The feature set of every pin that needs one

Revision 6 named a feature set for `cpal` alone, and four other pins needed one that no row stated
(critic N15). A default feature set is a decision as much as a named one, so the rule is stated
first: **every pin that this table omits takes its default feature set, and the manifest chunk
records that choice in its own verification step.**

| Pin | Feature requirement | Line in `[workspace.dependencies]` | Owner | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cpal` | The PipeWire host, and no JACK and no PulseAudio client code | `default-features = false, features = ["pipewire"]` | M4 | Verified by the platform research |
| `serde` | The derive macro | `features = ["derive"]` | M0 | Already in the root manifest |
| `clap` | The derive macro | `features = ["derive"]` | M8 | **Already in the root manifest.** M8 CONFIRMS the pin and the feature rather than adding the entry, which SM1 decision 4 of section 13.1 states for every pin the repository already holds; `tracing` is the same case (concern N16-9, N17-1) |
| `symphonia` | MP3 and AAC decoding, which the default set omits, beside FLAC and OGG | The decoder features for MP3, AAC, and the ISO base media container, plus the default set | M4 | **M4 resolves the exact names against the pinned version and records them** |
| `gix` | Object write, tree build, commit, reference edit, and reflog read, with no network transport and no clean or smudge filter | `default-features = false` plus the object and reference features that list needs | M4 | **M4 resolves the exact names and records them** |
| `tokio` | A multi-thread runtime (section 9.5 rule 3), a Unix stream socket (section 9.2), a signal handler (section 9.5 rule 7), and a deadline for B15, B16, B17, and B23 | `default-features = false, features = ["rt-multi-thread", "net", "time", "signal", "io-util", "sync", "macros"]` | M8 | **M8 confirms each name against the pinned version** |
| `rmcp` | The server role and a transport over any `AsyncRead` and `AsyncWrite` pair | `default-features = false` plus the server feature and the stream transport feature | M8 | **M8 resolves the exact names and records them** |
| `criterion` | The bench harness with no plotting back end, so the tree stays small and `cargo deny` stays quiet | `default-features = false` plus the cargo bench support feature | M4 | **M4 resolves the exact names and records them** |
| `smallvec` | serde support. `Note`, `ScoreCommand::SetArticulations`, and `Lyric` all sit under a `Serialize` derive and hold a `SmallVec`, and the crate's default feature set carries no serde at all | `features = ["serde"]` | M0 | **M0 confirms the name against the pinned version and records it** |
| `crossbeam-queue` | No feature beyond the default. `ArrayQueue` is in the default set, and no declaration serializes one | The default set | M4 | Verified against section 5.8 |
| `blake3` | The `pure` feature, so the build needs no C compiler on x86. The survey records that requirement, and the C16-W18 closure row cited a B.5 row that did not exist until this revision (critic C20-W9). **It is NOT the `git2` case**: `git2` was rejected because it binds a C library at run time; `blake3` compiles one optional C file at build time and the `pure` feature replaces it with Rust, so the decision costs throughput on x86 and buys a build with no toolchain assumption | `default-features = false, features = ["pure", "std"]` | M4 | **M4 confirms each name against 1.8.7 and records the `cargo tree -e features -i blake3` output** |
| `arrayvec` | No feature beyond the default. No `ArrayVec` field of this design is serialized: `ChainTopology` derives `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq` and `Eq` and no serde, and `EngineDisk`, `DuetCore` and `ChainState` each hold one inside a value that crosses no file, so the serde feature would be an unused dependency | The default set | M3 | Verified against section 5.5 and section 15.14 |
| `async-channel` | No feature beyond the default. The crate is `no_std` capable behind its own default `std` feature, and both ends of the B138 channel run on a thread of the section 5.7 table, so the default set is the set this design needs | The default set | M4 | Verified against section 5.8 and section 15.14 |

#### Every timeout, and the feature that provides it

A feature list that omits the mechanism for a declared timeout is a contradiction inside one
document, and revision 7 carried one (critic Q9). Each row of section 5.12 resolves to a mechanism
here.

| Timeouts | Thread | Mechanism | Feature it needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| B15, B16, B17 | The command-line client, on tokio | `tokio::time::timeout` | `tokio` `time` |
| B23 | The shutdown wait, on tokio | `tokio::time::timeout` over the reply channel | `tokio` `time` |
| B24 | A detached `std::thread` | `Runtime::shutdown_timeout` | `tokio` `rt`, which `rt-multi-thread` implies |
| B20, B21 | The calibration run, on a job thread | `std::time::Instant` plus a bounded `recv_timeout` on the pass reply | None |
| B18, B116 | **The CORE thread** | `std::time::Instant`, started when the core sends `ConfigureCommand::Open` or `ConfigureCommand::Close` and read on each pass of the core input loop. **Both are a REPORT and not a cancel** (critic C20-4): `AudioBackend::open` and `AudioBackend::stop` are blocking calls on the engine handoff thread, and an `Instant` read on the thread that is inside a call cannot end that call. The core is waiting for a MESSAGE, so the core can measure. Revision 20 gave B18 a `recv_timeout` on "the engine thread", which the section 5.7 thread table does not hold, and gave B116 an `Instant` around the very call it claimed to abandon | None |
| B119 | **The CORE thread** | `std::time::Instant`, started when the core sends `ConfigureCommand::Stop` on the B109 channel, which is the one message that ends that thread's loop, and read on each pass of the core input loop while it waits for `EngineEvent::HandoffStopped` on the B138 channel (critic C22I-3). **A report and not a cancel**, and NOT a join: revision 21 named `JoinHandle::join` behind a bounded park on the GPUI foreground thread, which TH3 forbids and which the section 5.7 thread table refuses (critic C21-2) | None |
| B131 | The CORE thread | `std::time::Instant`, started when the core sends `TransportCommand::Stop` on the quit path and read on each pass of the core input loop while it counts the `EngineEvent::CaptureDone` events it still owes. **A report and not a cancel** (critic C21I-2) | None |
| B132 | **The CORE thread** | `std::time::Instant`, started when `JobRunner::shut_down` drops the queue sender and read on each pass of the core input loop while the core waits for one `CoreInput::WorkerStopped` per B37 worker. **A report and not a cancel**, and NOT a join, for the B119 reason (critic C21-2) | None |
| B134 | **The CORE thread** | `std::time::Instant`, started when the core hands the dirty documents to the `duet-quit-save` thread and read on each pass of the core input loop while it waits for `CoreInput::QuitSaveDone`. **A report and not a cancel**, because an `fsync` on macOS and on Linux cannot be interrupted, which is the B117 and B118 reason (critic C21-3) | None |
| B22 | The MIDI thread | The same shape | None |
| B19 | A job thread | The same shape | None |
| B25 | The command-line front | `std::thread::sleep` between attempts | None |
| B26 | The watcher thread | `notify-debouncer-full`'s own window | Its default set |
| B27 | Measured, not enforced | `Instant::elapsed` at the allocation site | None |
| B95 | The engine handoff thread | **The bounded receive itself, at B108, counted in `GraphConfigurator::attempts`.** One pass of the loop is one B108 deadline, so three attempts are about 150 ms and the count IS the clock. No `Instant` is read on this path, no host, no GPUI task, and no thread that paints is involved (critic CR-19, C16-5) | None |
| B108 | The engine handoff thread | The bounded `recv_timeout` that parks the loop; each wake drains the `basedrop` collector before it serves anything else (TH5) | None |
| B117, B118 | The disk thread | `std::time::Instant` around the `duet_media` call, checked after it returns. **The bound is a REPORT and not a cancel**, because a blocking file call on macOS and on Linux cannot be interrupted without a second thread, and a second thread on this path would need a lock the audio path forbids. The value of the bound is the fault it raises and the flag it sets, which is what the user and the take need (section 5.10, critic C19-10) | None |
| B85 | The workflow shell | A shell wait loop in `audio-smoke.yml` | None |

**This table and the section 5.12 table are ONE SET, with ONE stated exception** (critic N16-10,
N17-2, C20-N1, N21I-4). Every row here has a row there, and every row there has a row here except
**B110**, which bounds an ALLOCATION and not a wait and therefore has no timeout mechanism to name.
Revision 21 stated the exception at section 5.12 and stated the rule without it here. Revision 17 broke the rule in one direction
with B24, B25, B26 and B85, and revision 20 broke it in the other with B108, which had a mechanism
here and no row there. The rule is stated at both sites now.
**A row marked "resolves" is an instruction, not a gap.** The owning chunk reads the pinned
version's own manifest, writes the resolved list into the root `[workspace.dependencies]` line, runs
`cargo tree -e features -i <crate>`, and pastes the output into its verification step. A chunk that
cannot obtain the capability with the pinned version reports the discrepancy instead of proceeding
(SM0).

## Appendix C: where every Critic finding is closed

**This appendix carries one section per review, and it registers one GUARD BLOCK for every review
that `run_all_gates.py` gives a closure gate.** Revision 21 carried a sentence that counted the
reviews, and revision 23 carried a sentence that counted the sections and the registered blocks;
every one of those numbers was stale, in the same document whose preamble calls the review count "a
fact of this document and not a sentence that ages" (critic N21I-3). The count is the section list
and the register, and no sentence states it. `run_all_gates.py` derives the closure gate list from
`reviews/` and refuses a review with no block and a block with no review, so the register and the
review set are held to one set by a machine. Revision 4
carried four closure appendices, and each one was written against the finding text rather than
against the resulting types (critic R4, R8). This appendix replaces all four.

**One row per finding. One section per row. The mechanism is visible in that section's text or in
its types.** A row that cites a section which does not hold the mechanism is a defect that returns
to the Architect.

Id families. **C**n.n is the premise review, which cited itself as "critic N.N". **V**n is the first
specification review. That review numbered only its twelve blockers, so revision 5 assigns an id to
every row in the review's own order. **N**n, **P**n, **R**n, and **S**n are the revision-2 to
revision-5 reviews, each of which numbered its own findings. The revision-9 review numbered its own
findings S1 to S4, W1 to W16, and C1 to C8, which collide with three earlier families; section C.10
is the one place that joins them, and every citation in the body writes the review's own number.

**The revision-6 review numbered its findings N1 to N18, which collide with the revision-2 family.**
This appendix gives that review the family **W**n and each row states the number the review itself
used. Every citation of a revision-6 finding in the body of this document writes "critic N<n>",
which is the review's own number, and the row below is the one place that joins the two.

### C.12 The revision-11 review

That review ran all three guards, added 35 probes of its own, and ran two compiler experiments. Its
four Criticals share one cause: **the roster substituted an empty body for 44 declarations**, so the
two design faults with the largest blast radius sat where no guard looked. Revision 12 writes every
field of every declaration, and PG3 refuses a comment where a field belongs.

| Id | Finding | Section |
|---|---|---|
| CR-1 | The generation compare makes the `CLIP` indicator unreachable, and one scalar cannot publish B86 counters | 7.3, the per-strip compare and its four cases; 5.9 `MeterSnapshot::latched`; 15.14 `MeterReader`; 10.7 rung three test 9, which asserts both directions |
| CR-2 | The boxed `SlotState::Equalizer` arm allocates and frees on the audio thread | 15.2 `SlotState`, every arm inline with two expectations; 5.5 migration rules 2 and 3; 5.7, the audio-owned block; 1.5 PG26; B.1; 1.6 B51 |
| CR-3 | Two recorded probe results are false, so PG21 and PG22 are unverified rules | 1.9, whose every recorded result comes from a fresh run over this revision |

### C.20 The revision-16 review, over the frozen document

The sixteenth review read the whole frozen document at md5 `dcb7b1c3238a08d37860403731a1e15c`.
It returned 17 Criticals, 18 Warnings, and 11 Concerns, and this block holds one row for each of the 46.

**Revision 17 recorded this review as thirteen Criticals and thirteen Warnings, and it carried a row
for 26 of the 46.** Twelve ids had no row, no citation, and no fix, and the seventeenth review
verified that nine of the twelve numbered findings were open verbatim (critic C17-1). The count
sentence made the drop invisible: a reader who audits the appendix reads thirteen, counts thirteen
rows, and concludes the review is closed. **The denominator was wrong, not one row**, and a
truncated read of a review is the one failure this appendix exists to prevent.

**The id list of this block is GENERATED and never typed.** `tools/review_ids.py` reads the review's
own `## CRITICAL n`, `## WARNING n`, and `## CONCERN n` headings and prints the list.
`tools/closure_check.py` compares that list with this block in both directions and compares the
count sentence above with the counts it generated. Rule PG32 states the contract and section 1.9
records probe PP32. A review this document has not read is now a red run and not a silent gap.

below names the source it took.

The review file this block records is stored at plan-store key `36304ki7dzd2p-review-r20` (closure-r20).

**Two of its five Criticals are evidence defects and three are design defects**, and that split is
the finding behind the finding. `probe_run.py` did not run at all, so not one of the 58 probe rows
was verified for revision 20, and the section 1.9 roster transcript was three revisions stale with
two guards red on it. The Architect of revision 20 reported both as green. **The cause was an
ORDER**: the harness ran, the document then changed, and the earlier run was recorded. Revision 21
answers it with a machine rather than a habit: `roadmap/duet-v1/tools/run_all_gates.py` runs every
guard and every harness in one pass and exits 2 when any file under `roadmap/duet-v1/` changed
while it was in progress, so a transcript it prints is a transcript of one tree.

**Two rows of C.23 were not honestly CLOSED when revision 20 wrote them.** C19-7 and C19-10 each
had a fix that was complete at three sites and open at one: B116 promised a cancel an `Instant`
cannot perform, and section 5.8 still routed the fault queue to the thread revision 20 had removed
from that path. Both are closed at every site in this revision, and the C.23 rows say where.

### C.25 The revision-21 inner review, over the frozen document

The twenty-first review read the whole frozen directory at architecture md5
`e42bc8b6640a5831d0342f5868e11fc7`.
It returned 3 Criticals, 6 Warnings, and 4 Concerns, and this block holds one row for each of the 13.

The review file this block records has md5 `98a746967cb9fd02c4a3b5cb5029ea0b` (closure-r21-inner).
The review file this block records is stored at plan-store key `36304kihouge4-review-r21-inner` (closure-r21-inner).

**It is the INNER review of this revision**, which means the Architect dispatched it against the
frozen revision-21 text, closed every Critical and every Warning it returned, and re-froze. The
document a later reviewer reads is therefore the document AFTER these thirteen rows, and the rows
state what changed.

**All three Criticals came from its engineering pass, and that is the finding behind the findings.**
The nineteenth review recorded that three reviews in a row had been almost wholly about the guard
tooling while four Criticals sat unread in sections 5, 9 and 12 (N19-8). This review read the
engineering first and found that the specification described a mixer in detail and did not describe
how a recorded take reaches it: no type, no boundary and no thread turned a track and a position
into a source file and a region envelope, so sections 6.1 and 6.2 had no runtime at all. The guard
pass by contrast found one weak rule and no fail-open; eleven of the twelve gates answered every
hostile input, including a four-step attack on the new floor scheme that the derived root set
refused on its own.

**One further defect is recorded here and no reviewer raised it.** While the Architect read
`dependency_audit` to answer C21I-W1, it found that PG12 compared `crates/duet` with `duet` and
skipped every declaration of the application crate, so the rule had never read one of them.
`HeldDuration(ArrayVec<NoteValue, 6>)` is the live instance it hid. Section 1.2 states it at the
site and the rule normalises the name now.

its seven Criticals were invisible to every rule that runs. PG32 passed a closure row that named a
field its own declaration did not hold, PG35 and PG36 passed a chunk row that a renderer truncates,

for: PG38 holds every table row of this document to its own header, PG39 holds the rule index to the
live rule set, PG40 holds a chunk to the crate its line owns, and CL1c takes the closure record's
second source out of the Architect's write scope.

this document recorded 77 CLOSED and 4 OPEN.** Every one of those rows is corrected in C.23, C.24
and C.25: each row now states what the mechanism does, and each one is closed by a mechanism that

### C.27 The revision-22 inner review, over the frozen document

The twenty-second inner review read the whole frozen directory at architecture md5
`b28e979bafda0a9b3f954a1eaec371a0`.
It returned 8 Criticals, 18 Warnings, and 9 Concerns, and this block holds one row for each of the 35.

The review file this block records has md5 `67eb9b00246eb537823b6e0599b6eae8` (closure-r22-inner).
The review file this block records is stored at plan-store key `3630i3sif1czf-review-r22-inner` (closure-r22-inner).

**Thirty-four rows are CLOSED and one is PARTIAL, and the PARTIAL row states why.** N22I-5 asks for
a dated correction note inside `design-contract.md`, which sits outside the write scope of this
revision; the rule that binds the note is written and the note itself is owed, and this appendix
says so rather than claim a file it did not touch.

**All eight Criticals were ONE class: a stated duty whose carrier no declaration holds.** The class
spanned the engine, the core, the MIDI path, the view seam and the plan graph. It was invisible to
all sixty-three rules of revision 22, because this plan held a rule for a type with no place, a
place with no type, a derive with no use, a citation with no site and a chunk with no crate, and no
rule for a MESSAGE with no channel.

**Revision 23 wrote that rule first, and every other row follows from it.** TH13 makes every
cross-thread duty name one row of the `carrier-table` block of section 5.8, and PG41 runs TH13 in
both directions: a row whose end names a field no declaration holds is red, and a declared field
that holds a channel end, a ring end or a publication end and that no row names is red. Writing the
23 rows of that block is what found the six missing write ends, the four missing structural ends,
the disk thread with no type, the sounding-note set, the handoff thread with no stop command and
the fault queue with one declared handle instead of two. The run prints `CARRIERS` and
`CARRIER FIELDS`, so both denominators are readable, and probe PP41 plants a thread the section 5.7
table does not declare and a declared write end that no row names.

### C.28 The revision-23 inner review, over the frozen document

The twenty-third inner review read the whole frozen directory at architecture md5
`eb3890c943a565eaa681b990cfc9d705`.
It returned 6 Criticals, 16 Warnings, and 9 Concerns, and this block holds one row for each of the 31.

The review file this block records has md5 `eb24bbb015b702cf9ca48e32cd0bf8a7` (closure-r23-inner).
The review file this block records is stored at plan-store key `36315vzy3foa5-review-r23-inner` (closure-r23-inner).

**Every row is CLOSED, and the class of this review is narrower than the class of the last one.**
The twenty-second review found eight duties whose carrier no declaration held. TH13 and PG41 closed
that class, and this review found what the new rule and the new declarations did NOT reach: one seam
the rule's own sentence covers and the table omitted, a root that gained its channel end and none of
its file handles, two chunk orders the new fields broke, an index whose range the array refutes, an
accumulator with no key, and a rule that read two cells and never held either one against the
declared end set.

**PG41 is a stronger rule than the one revision 23 first wrote** (critic C23I-W1). It decides the
DIRECTION of every end now: `Sender`, `SyncSender`, `Producer`, `Input` and `OneshotSender` are
write ends, `Receiver`, `CoreReceiver`, `Consumer`, `Output` and `OneshotReceiver` are read ends, and
an `ArrayQueue` behind an `Arc` is one value both ends share. The two shapes the Critic planted, a
Sender cell that names a field holding no carrier and a row whose two ends are swapped, are each red
now and each carries a probe.

**One parser defect is closed with them.** The declaration scanner let a run of `#[must_use]`
attributes backtrack across the code between it and the next declaration, so two structs this
revision added were invisible to every rule that reads a declaration. The attribute run may not
cross a `;`, a `{` or a `}` now.
